title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
皇上嗣大曆服之四年歲在丙子
天下復當賓興之期屬禮卿
以言者謂天下士日靡於文
而鮮實也上其議
請嚴爲之式以端士趨而崇理道
詔下所司所司皇皇焉奉行惟謹
===
獎抑所加雷動風馳而學官
弟子員鮮不灑然易慮爭自
劃削就矩矱以待徵解惟是
山西則巡按監察御史孫〔代〕
實監臨之祇肅周愼夙夜匪
懈迺與督學之臣約務崇雅
黜浮以仰稱
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序
皇上嗣大曆服之四年，歲在丙子，天下復當賓興之期。屬禮卿以言者謂天下士日靡於文而鮮實也，上其議，請嚴爲之式，以端士趨而崇理道。詔下所司，所司皇皇焉奉行惟謹，獎抑所加，雷動風馳，而學官弟子員鮮不灑然易慮，爭自劃削就矩矱，以待徵解。惟是山西則巡按監察御史孫〔代〕實監臨之，祇肅周愼，夙夜匪懈，迺與督學之臣約，務崇雅黜浮，以仰稱
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the fourth year after His Majesty succeeded to the Great Imperial Mandate, the cyclical year being bingzi (1576), the realm once again reached the appointed time for presenting worthy men as guests of the court. Just then, because commentators maintained that the scholars of the realm were growing daily more extravagant in their literary style while lacking in substance, the Minister of Rites submitted a deliberation requesting that strict standards of form be established, so as to rectify the orientation of scholars and exalt the Way of principle. When the imperial edict was handed down to the competent authorities, those authorities anxiously and reverently carried it out with the utmost care. Wherever encouragement or restraint was applied, the response was as swift as thunder and wind, and among the government students in the schools there were few who did not refresh their thoughts and change their minds, vying to pare away their excesses and conform to the proper rules and measures as they awaited recruitment and forwarding for the examination.

Here in Shanxi, it was the Regional Investigating Censor Sun Dai 孫代 who served as Supervising Official. Reverent, solemn, thorough, and circumspect, never slackening from morning to night, he made a pact with the Education Intendant to devote themselves to exalting elegance and rejecting superficiality, so as to respectfully live up to…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
德意先事禮聘〔之在藩〕暨學正梅
〔廷〕爲考試官教諭唐〔棟〕葉〔正〕
〔蒙〕王〔正宇〕梁〔紹震〕周〔于用〕爲
同考試官凡簾以內悉以屬
之罔有弗毖以提調則左布
政使徐〔行〕右布政使劉〔孝〕以
監試則按察使孫〔應元〕副使
===
張〔楚城〕暨百執事咸掄選以
充凡簾以外悉以屬之罔有
弗戒及期合巡按宣大監察
御史沈〔涵〕暨提學副使蔡〔叔〕
〔逵〕所造士二千一百有奇三
試之校其俊六十有五人相
與縱觀其文率典則雅醇根
punctuated: 德意。先事禮聘〔之在藩〕暨學正梅〔廷〕爲考試官，教諭唐〔棟〕、葉〔正〕〔蒙〕、王〔正宇〕、梁〔紹震〕、周〔于用〕爲同考試官，凡簾以內悉以屬之，罔有弗毖；以提調則左布政使徐〔行〕、右布政使劉〔孝〕，以監試則按察使孫〔應元〕、副使張〔楚城〕暨百執事，咸掄選以充，凡簾以外悉以屬之，罔有弗戒。及期，合巡按宣大監察御史沈〔涵〕暨提學副使蔡〔叔〕〔逵〕所造士二千一百有奇，三試之，校其俊六十有五人。相與縱觀其文，率典則雅醇，根
translation_en: … his benevolent intent. Before the proceedings, he courteously engaged me, [Zhi]fan [之在藩, sic, for 之藩], along with the Subprefectural Director of Studies Mei Ting 梅廷, to serve as Examiners; and the County Directors of Studies Tang Dong 唐棟, Ye Zhengmeng 葉正蒙, Wang Zhengyu 王正宇, Liang Shaozhen 梁紹震, and Zhou Yuyong 周于用 to serve as Associate Examiners. All matters inside the curtain were entrusted entirely to them, and there was none who was not scrupulously careful. As for the Proctors, the Left Administration Commissioner Xu Xing 徐行 and the Right Administration Commissioner Liu Xiao 劉孝, and as for the Monitoring Officials, the Surveillance Commissioner Sun Yingyuan 孫應元 and the Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Chucheng 張楚城, together with the hundred functionaries, were all carefully selected to fill their posts. All matters outside the curtain were entrusted entirely to them, and there was none who was not vigilant. When the appointed time arrived, they gathered the more than two thousand one hundred scholars cultivated by the Regional Inspector of Xuanfu and Datong and Investigating Censor Shen Han 沈涵 and the Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Cai Shukui 蔡叔逵, tested them in three sessions, and selected sixty-five outstanding men from among them. Together we perused their essays at length: they were generally canonical, refined, and pure, rooted in…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
極理趣折中聖言而汜濫淮
淫詭詖誖謬之習滌濯澌盡
可以弗畔於禮鄉之議郁郁
乎美以盛矣遂遵
制列其名氏錄其文以
獻〔之藩〕不佞以職事當序諸首
簡謹執筴而諗之諸大夫曰
===
持此可以報
天子矣乎〔之藩〕怏怏然有深懼焉
遂進諸士而申之曰
聖天子方以實求天下士而諸士
以文舉有司者復以文錄
上毋乃非
明詔意也乎夫文實之彰也實匪
punctuated: 極理趣，折中聖言，而汜濫淮淫、詭詖誖謬之習滌濯澌盡，可以弗畔於禮鄉之議，郁郁乎美以盛矣。遂遵制列其名氏，錄其文以獻。〔之藩〕不佞，以職事當序諸首簡，謹執筴而諗之諸大夫曰：「持此可以報天子矣乎？」〔之藩〕怏怏然有深懼焉，遂進諸士而申之曰：「聖天子方以實求天下士，而諸士以文舉，有司者復以文錄上，毋乃非明詔意也乎？夫文，實之彰也；實匪
translation_en: … reaching the ultimate depths of principle and meaning, and taking the words of the sages as their standard. Habits of unbridled extravagance [?] and deceitful, biased, and perverse writing have been washed away completely, so that they do not rebel against the deliberations of the Bureau of Rites—how richly and splendidly flourishing! Thereupon, in compliance with the imperial system, we listed their names and recorded their essays to present to the throne. I, Zhi Fan 〔之藩〕, unworthy as I am, by virtue of my official duties ought to write the preface on the opening pages. Humbly holding the writing tablets, I spoke to the various grandees, saying: "With this, can we repay the Son of Heaven?" Feeling uneasy and deeply fearful, I, Zhi Fan 〔之藩〕, then brought forward the scholars and admonished them, saying: "The Sacred Son of Heaven is just now seeking scholars throughout the realm on the basis of substance, yet you scholars are recommended on the basis of literary writing, and the authorities in turn record your writings to present to the throne—is this not contrary to the intent of the illustrious imperial edict? Now, literary writing is the manifestation of substance; without…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
文弗達書曰敷奏以言文也
易曰含章從王實也諸士之
文例不可廢已其務實之勝
乎夫山西古冀州域堯舜之
故都也太行恒霍之所環峙
河汾滹沁之所注匯岱岑嵯
峨浩瀚汪濊固函夏之奧區
===
林傑之淵藪也在昔唐虞百
揆四岳九官十二牧布列內
外同德相濟庶尹御事咸備
九德人才之盛卓越千古春
秋時則有若衰偃軫轂隨冀
胥欒林父叔向之徒尊王定
霸奇勳偉略照曜史冊漢唐
punctuated: 文弗達。《書》曰：「敷奏以言。」文也。《易》曰：「含章從王。」實也。諸士之文，例不可廢已，其務實之勝乎！夫山西，古冀州域，堯、舜之故都也。太行、恒、霍之所環峙，河、汾、滹、沁之所注匯，岱岑嵯峨，浩瀚汪濊，固函夏之奧區，林傑之淵藪也。在昔唐、虞，百揆、四岳、九官、十二牧，布列內外，同德相濟，庶尹、御事咸備九德，人才之盛，卓越千古。春秋時，則有若衰、偃、軫、轂、隨、冀、胥、欒、林父、叔向之徒，尊王定霸，奇勳偉略，照曜史冊。漢、唐、
translation_en: … literary expression, it cannot be conveyed. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "They set forth reports in words." That is literary expression. The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Containing brilliance, one follows the king's service." That is substance. In the case of you scholars' compositions, by precedent literary form cannot be dispensed with; yet should you not strive for substance to prevail over it? Now Shanxi is the territory of ancient Jizhou, the former capital of Yao and Shun. Encircled by the towering peaks of Mount Taihang, Mount Heng, and Mount Huo, and converged upon by the flowing waters of the Yellow, Fen, Hutuo, and Qin rivers—its lofty crags rugged and towering, its waters vast and deep—it is truly a heartland of the Chinese realm and a gathering place of dense talents [? 林傑]. In antiquity, during the Tang and Yu eras [of Yao and Shun], the General Regulator (Baikui), the Four岳 (Siyue, Four Peaks), the Nine Officials (Jiuguan), and the Twelve Pastors (Shier mu) were arrayed at court and in the provinces, aiding one another in shared virtue; the various directors and managers of affairs were all endowed with the nine virtues, and the flourishing of talent surpassed all ages. In the Spring and Autumn period, there were men such as Zhao Shuai 趙衰, Hu Yan 狐偃, Xian Zhen 先軫, Xian Gu 先轂, Sui Hui 隨會,郤芮 [? Ji 冀, Que Rui of Ji], Xu Chen 胥臣, Luan Zhi 欒枝, Xun Linfu 荀林父, and Shuxiang 叔向, who honored the king and established hegemony, their extraordinary merits and grand strategies shining brightly in the historical annals. From the Han, Tang, …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
宋而下郭秦王通文潞司馬
諸人彬彬繼作抗跡前脩之
數子者精微之蘊吾不知其
於岳牧之佐何如也然各能
以其材致主立身以顯其名
於不朽無亦惟其實之勝焉
耳而司馬公存誠不妄於道
===
尤爲近之迨我
皇明驅逐胡元肇復土宇
列聖相承乆道成化名世之彥間
不乏稱河津夫子力行篤學
爲時良輔爲世大儒若其居
敬務實之訓讀書錄可考也
今
punctuated: 宋而下，郭泰、王通、文潞、司馬諸人彬彬繼作，抗跡前脩。之數子者，精微之蘊，吾不知其於岳牧之佐何如也，然各能以其材致主立身，以顯其名於不朽，無亦惟其實之勝焉耳。而司馬公存誠不妄，於道尤爲近之。迨我皇明驅逐胡元，肇復土宇，列聖相承，乆道成化，名世之彥，間不乏稱。河津夫子力行篤學，爲時良輔，爲世大儒，若其居敬務實之訓，《讀書錄》可考也。今
translation_en:
…and the Song onward, figures such as Guo Tai 郭泰 [printed 郭秦], Wang Tong 王通, Wen Lu 文潞 (Wen Yanbo 文彥博, Duke of Lu), and Sima 司馬 (Sima Guang 司馬光) arose in illustrious succession, rivaling the footsteps of the worthies of earlier ages. As for the subtle and profound inner attainments of these several gentlemen, I do not know how they compare to those of the assistants such as the Four Peaks and Twelve Pastors; yet each was able to use his talents to serve his ruler and establish himself, making his name shine immortally—was this not simply because their substance prevailed? Moreover, Master Sima preserved sincerity and abstained from falsehood, coming especially close to the Way.

When our August Ming expelled the barbarian Yuan and restored the realm, a succession of sacred emperors followed one another, transforming the world through long-enduring governance, and famous worthies of the age have not been lacking in renown from time to time. The Master of Hejin 河津 (Xue Xuan 薛瑄) practiced earnestly and studied with devotion, serving as a fine chief minister of his time and a great Confucian scholar for the ages; as for his teachings on abiding in reverence and attending to substance, they may be examined in the Reading Notes (Dushulu 讀書錄). Now…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
天子聰明仁聖允恭允塞孚於堯
舜乃奮庸熙載興事考成則
自股肱以至於百僚咸兢兢
師師以撫五辰而凝庶績即
今宇內寧謐窮荒黠虜古所
稱匈奴單于者莫不稽顙受
職委命下吏率服丕敘之
休實與唐虞爭埒夫居堯舜之
地遇
堯舜之君不能率循堯舜之道以
賛佐
隆盛而詡詡然惟文是侈不亦
末乎今夫丹轅繡轂車之文
也歷太行九折之阪積中而
punctuated: 天子聰明仁聖，允恭允塞，孚於堯舜；乃奮庸熙載，興事考成。則自股肱以至於百僚，咸兢兢師師，以撫五辰而凝庶績。即今宇內寧謐，窮荒黠虜，古所稱匈奴單于者，莫不稽顙受職，委命下吏；率服丕敘之休，實與唐虞爭埒。夫居堯舜之地，遇堯舜之君，不能率循堯舜之道以賛佐隆盛，而詡詡然惟文是侈，不亦末乎？今夫丹轅繡轂，車之文也；歷太行九折之阪，積中而
translation_en: …the Son of Heaven is intelligent, benevolent, and sage, sincerely reverent and genuinely substantive, matching Yao 堯 and Shun 舜 in virtue; and so he rouses to achievement and brightens the undertakings, initiating affairs and examining their completion. Thus, from the chief ministers right down to the hundred officials, all are cautious and emulate one another in order to harmonize with the five seasonal celestials and consolidate the myriad achievements. Even now, the realm within the seas is tranquil and at peace, and the cunning caitiffs of the remotest wastelands—those who in antiquity were called the Xiongnu Chanyu 匈奴單于—none fail to knock their foreheads on the ground and accept official appointments, entrusting their lives to minor functionaries. The glory of universal submission and grand order truly rivals that of Tang 唐 and Yu 虞. Now, to dwell in the land of Yao and Shun, and to encounter a sovereign like Yao and Shun, yet to be unable to follow the Way of Yao and Shun in order to assist this flourishing prosperity, instead boastfully indulging only in literary ornament—is this not attending to the trivial? Now then, vermilion shafts and embroidered hubs are the ornamental beauty of a carriage; yet only when it traverses the nine-bend slopes of the Taihang 太行 Mountains, heavily laden within and…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
不敗者斯不爲虛車晉之乘
㞳產尚矣假令詭御失其故
步卽蒼膺朱鬣奚稱焉是故
玄德之升必由歷試惠言之
行期於底績責實之道蓋自
唐虞而重之諸士行將應
詔而往對公車服馳驅之役卽九
===
官十二牧之職且胥遷焉以
稽爾實其何以哉噫盍亦反
求諸其心而已矣精一執中
堯舜傳心之學也斯實之基
乎諸士涵泳典謨亦旣有年
尚其守文清之敬敦文正之
誠會之於中由是精白純粹
punctuated: 不敗者，斯不爲虛車。晉之乘，㞳產尚矣；假令詭御失其故步，卽蒼膺朱鬣奚稱焉？是故玄德之升，必由歷試；惠言之行，期於底績。責實之道，蓋自唐虞而重之。諸士行將應詔而往對公車，服馳驅之役，卽九官、十二牧之職，且胥遷焉。以稽爾實，其何以哉？噫！盍亦反求諸其心而已矣。精一執中，堯、舜傳心之學也，斯實之基乎！諸士涵泳典謨，亦旣有年，尚其守文清之敬，敦文正之誠，會之於中，由是精白純粹，
translation_en: … does not break down—only then is it not an empty chariot. Among the steeds of Jin, the breed of Qu (Quchan 㞳產) has long been prized; yet suppose that through deceitful driving it loses its proper pace, what praise would it deserve even with a dark breast and red mane? Therefore, the elevation of dark virtue must come through repeated testing, and the putting into practice of compliant words aims at the achievement of results. The way of demanding substantive reality was indeed already valued in the time of Tang and Yu. You scholars are soon to respond to the imperial edict, go to answer at the Official Chariots Office (Gongche 公車), and take up the service of galloping forth on duty; even to the offices of the Nine Officials and Twelve Pastors you will all in turn be promoted. When your substantive reality is examined, wherewith will you answer? Alas! Why not simply turn back and seek it in your own minds? "Being refined and single-minded, holding fast to the Mean"—this was the learning of the transmission of the mind of Yao and Shun. Is this not the foundation of substantive reality? You scholars have immersed yourselves in the Canons and Counsels for many years now; may you hold fast to the reverence of Wenqing 文清 (Xue Xuan 薛瑄) and cultivate the sincerity of Wenzheng 文正 (Sima Guang 司馬光), uniting them within yourselves, so that from this, pure, bright, and unadulterated, …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
充積光輝以措諸身以施諸
政以達諸天下臯夔稷契由
此其選也彼春秋之士豈能
望末塵而窺左足耶其或甘
言希進終渝平生惟祟高縈
利之是圖違
明詔失
===
聖意是靜言庸違唐虞之所弃也
諸士其尚慎之以幸釋余之
深懼哉諸大夫曰誠哉訓也
三晉之士其庶幾矣是舉也
總督軍務兵部尚書兼右副
都御史方〔逢時〕巡撫右僉都
御史崔〔鏞〕巡撫大同右僉都
punctuated:
充積光輝，以措諸身，以施諸政，以達諸天下，臯、夔、稷、契由此其選也。彼春秋之士，豈能望末塵而窺左足耶？其或甘言希進，終渝平生，惟祟高縈利之是圖，違明詔，失聖意，是靜言庸違，唐、虞之所弃也。諸士其尚慎之，以幸釋余之深懼哉！諸大夫曰：「誠哉，訓也！三晉之士，其庶幾矣。」
是舉也，總督軍務兵部尚書兼右副都御史方〔逢時〕、巡撫右僉都御史崔〔鏞〕、巡撫大同右僉都
translation_en:
…accumulated in abundance and shining with brilliance, to apply it to their own persons, to put it into practice in governance, and to extend it throughout the realm—the likes of Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Xie will be chosen from this path. How could those scholars of the Spring and Autumn period even hope to catch a glimpse of their trailing dust or peek at a single step of theirs? Yet if anyone uses sweet words in the hope of advancement and ultimately betrays the principles of his life, scheming only after lofty eminence [?] and entangling profit, thereby violating the luminous edicts and failing the sacred intent—this is "speaking smoothly when quiet, yet acting perversely when employed," which was cast aside in the eras of Tang and Yu. May the scholars take heed of this, so as happily to relieve me of my deep anxiety! The grandees said: "True indeed is this admonition! The scholars of the Three Jin will surely come close to attaining it."
In this undertaking, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, Minister of War and concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Fang Fengshi (方逢時), Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Cui Yong (崔鏞), and Grand Coordinator of Datong and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
御史鄭〔洛〕振紀宣猷士習丕
變廵鹽御史先〔金階〕令陳〔用賓〕
章軌貞憲文教聿新若郎
中賈〔實〕主事胡〔來縉〕督儲於
此郎中王〔三錫〕恤刑於此而
光祿寺少卿岳〔相〕尚寶司卿
徐〔理〕中書舍人牛〔惟炳〕行人
===
司行人田〔疇〕皆以使事至若
左叅政張〔士佩〕右叅政張〔夢鯉〕
劉〔漢儒〕賈〔應元〕右叅議馮
〔子履〕副使蔡〔應揚〕許〔守謙〕劉
〔泮〕胡〔來貢〕楊〔愈茂〕許〔希孟〕王
〔汝梅〕栗〔祁〕僉事韓〔應元〕行太
僕寺卿吳〔哲〕少卿黃〔裳〕綜理
punctuated: 御史鄭〔洛〕，振紀宣猷，士習丕變；廵鹽御史先〔金階〕、令陳〔用賓〕，章軌貞憲，文教聿新。若郎中賈〔實〕、主事胡〔來縉〕督儲於此，郎中王〔三錫〕恤刑於此，而光祿寺少卿岳〔相〕、尚寶司卿徐〔理〕、中書舍人牛〔惟炳〕、行人司行人田〔疇〕皆以使事至；若左叅政張〔士佩〕，右叅政張〔夢鯉〕、劉〔漢儒〕、賈〔應元〕，右叅議馮〔子履〕，副使蔡〔應揚〕、許〔守謙〕、劉〔泮〕、胡〔來貢〕、楊〔愈茂〕、許〔希孟〕、王〔汝梅〕、栗〔祁〕，僉事韓〔應元〕，行太僕寺卿吳〔哲〕，少卿黃〔裳〕，綜理
translation_en: … Censor-in-Chief Zheng Luo 鄭洛 have invigorated discipline and proclaimed grand plans, greatly transforming the habits of the scholars; Salt-Control Censors—formerly Jin Jie 金階 and currently [令, error for 今] Chen Yongbin 陳用賓—have manifested the norms and upheld the laws, renewing cultural education. As for Bureau Director Jia Shi 賈實 and Secretary Hu Laijin 胡來縉, who are supervising military supplies here; Bureau Director Wang Sanxi 王三錫, who is showing compassion in penal administration here; and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Yue Xiang 岳相, Chief Minister of the Seal Office Xu Li 徐理, Drafting Official Niu Weibing 牛惟炳, and Messenger of the Messenger Office Tian Chou 田疇, who have all arrived on emissarial missions; as well as Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Shipei 張士佩, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Zhang Mengli 張夢鯉, Liu Hanru 劉漢儒, and Jia Yingyuan 賈應元, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Feng Zilü 馮子履, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Cai Yingyang 蔡應揚, Xu Shouqian 許守謙, Liu Pan 劉泮, Hu Laigong 胡來貢, Yang Yumao 楊愈茂, Xu Ximeng 許希孟, Wang Rumei 王汝梅, and Li Qi 栗祁, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Han Yingyuan 韓應元, Chief Minister of the Branch Court of the Imperial Stud Wu Zhe 吳哲, and Vice Minister Huang Shang 黃裳, who are managing overall affairs…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
予此總兵官白〔九中〕參將謝
〔天祐〕署都指揮僉事王〔江〕防
範予此而參議查〔鐸〕僉事王
〔予蕙〕署都指揮僉事王〔應爵〕
俱以表
賀行法皆得書
河南南陽府儒學教授朱〔之〕
〔蕃〕謹序
punctuated:
予此；總兵官白〔九中〕、參將謝〔天祐〕、署都指揮僉事王〔江〕防範予此；而參議查〔鐸〕、僉事王〔予蕙〕、署都指揮僉事王〔應爵〕俱以表賀行，法皆得書。
河南南陽府儒學教授朱〔之〕〔蕃〕謹序。
translation_en:
… participated in this; Regional Commander Bai Jiuzhong 白九中, Assistant Regional Commander Xie Tianyou 謝天祐, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Wang Jiang 王江 guarded and maintained security for this; while Assistant Administration Commissioner Zha Duo 查鐸, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Yuhui 王予蕙, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Wang Yingjue 王應爵 were all departing to present a congratulatory memorial—by convention, all of them merit being recorded.

Respectfully prefaced by Zhu Zhifan 朱之蕃, Instructor of the Confucian School of Nanyang Prefecture in Henan.

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子路有聞未之能行唯恐有聞
天地位焉萬物育焉
使契爲司徒敎以人倫父子有親君臣有
義夫婦有別長幼有序朋友有信放勳
曰勞之來之匡之直之輔之翼之使自
得之又從而振德之
易
===
彖曰大畜剛健篤實輝光日新其德剛上
而尚賢能止健大正也不家食吉養賢
也利涉大川應乎天也
有孚惠心勿問之矣
繫辭焉以盡其言
兌正秋也萬物之所說也
書
帝曰來禹汝亦昌言禹拜曰都帝予何言
予思日孜孜
punctuated:
第壹場

四書：
「子路有聞，未之能行，唯恐有聞。」
「天地位焉，萬物育焉。」
「使契爲司徒，敎以人倫：父子有親，君臣有義，夫婦有別，長幼有序，朋友有信。放勳曰：『勞之來之，匡之直之，輔之翼之，使自得之，又從而振德之。』」

易：
「彖曰：大畜，剛健篤實輝光，日新其德，剛上而尚賢。能止健，大正也。不家食吉，養賢也。利涉大川，應乎天也。」
「有孚惠心，勿問之矣。」
「繫辭焉以盡其言。」
「兌，正秋也，萬物之所說也。」

書：
「帝曰：『來，禹！汝亦昌言。』禹拜曰：『都！帝，予何言？予思日孜孜。』」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books:
"When Zilu heard anything, if he had not yet succeeded in putting it into practice, his only fear was that he might hear something else." [Analects 5.14]
"Heaven and earth are established in their places, and the myriad things are nourished." [Doctrine of the Mean 1]
"He appointed Xie to be Minister of Education (Situ), to teach the people human relationships: between father and son there should be affection; between ruler and minister there should be righteousness; between husband and wife there should be attention to their separate functions; between old and young there should be a proper order; and between friends there should be faithfulness. Fangxun [Emperor Yao] said: 'Encourage them, lead them on; rectify them, straighten them; help them, give them wings—cause them to possess it for themselves, and then further stimulate them and confer kindness upon them.'" [Mencius 3A.4]

Classic of Changes (Yi):
"The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: 'Great Taming (Dachu): firm and strong, sincere and solid,輝光 [shining brilliantly], daily renewing his virtue. The firm ascends and honors the worthy. Being able to restrain strength is great rectitude. Not eating at home brings good fortune, for the worthy are nourished. It is advantageous to cross the great river, for there is correspondence with Heaven.'" [Hexagram 26, Dachu]
"There is sincerity and a kind heart; ask no questions about it." [Hexagram 42, Yi]
"He appended judgments to exhaust his words." [Great Treatise (Xici) I.12]
"Dui [the Joyous] is mid-autumn, that in which the myriad things rejoice." [Discussion of the Trigrams (Shuogua) 5]

Classic of Documents (Shu):
"The Emperor said: 'Come, Yu! Do you also make a splendid speech.' Yu bowed and said: 'Oh! Emperor, what can I say? I think only of being diligent day by day.'" [Yi and Ji]

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
導河積石至于龍門
一曰水二曰火三曰木四曰金五曰土
三后協心同底于道道洽政治澤潤生民
四夷左衽罔不咸頼
詩
小戎俴收五楘梁輈游環脅驅陰靷鋈續
文茵暢轂駕我騏馵
樂只君子殿天子之邦
其香始升上帝居歆
武王靡不勝龍旂十乘大糦是承邦畿千
里維民所止肇域彼四海
===
春秋
春王正月城楚丘〔僖公二年〕
晉趙盾帥師救陳　宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯
會晉師于棐林伐鄭〔俱宣公元年〕
晉人宋人衛人曹人伐鄭〔宣公十年〕
六月雨〔僖公三年〕　春西狩獲麟〔哀公十有四年〕
punctuated:
導河積石，至于龍門。
一曰水，二曰火，三曰木，四曰金，五曰土。
三后協心，同底于道；道洽政治，澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸頼。

《詩》
小戎俴收，五楘梁輈。游環脅驅，陰靷鋈續。文茵暢轂，駕我騏馵。
樂只君子，殿天子之邦。
其香始升，上帝居歆。
武王靡不勝。龍旂十乘，大糦是承。邦畿千里，維民所止，肇域彼四海。

《春秋》
春，王正月，城楚丘。〔僖公二年〕
晉趙盾帥師救陳。宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭。〔俱宣公元年〕
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人伐鄭。〔宣公十年〕
六月，雨。〔僖公三年〕　春，西狩獲麟。〔哀公十有四年〕
translation_en:
"He guided the Yellow River from Jishi as far as Longmen."
"The first is called water, the second fire, the third wood, the fourth metal, and the fifth earth."
"The three sovereigns united their hearts and together attained the Way; the Way permeated governance and order, and their beneficence moistened the living people, so that even the four barbarian tribes with left-fastened lapels all without exception relied upon them."

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"The small war chariot has a shallow box, and a five-wrapped curved pole. With slip-rings and side-straps, and traces attached with gilt-silver rings to the front board; on a tiger-skin mat and with long hubs, I yoke my dappled horse with the white left hind foot."
"Happy be the noble lord, who secures the states of the Son of Heaven!"
"No sooner does its fragrance rise than the Lord on High tranquilly enjoys it."
"King Wu conquered all. With ten dragon-bannered chariots, they present the sacrificial millet. The royal domain of a thousand li is where the people rest, and it opens up the boundaries to those four seas."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In spring, in the king's first month, they walled Chuqiu." [2nd year of Duke Xi]
"Zhao Dun of Jin led a force to rescue Chen. The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met the force of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng." [Both from the 1st year of Duke Xuan]
"Men of Jin, men of Song, men of Wei, and men of Cao attacked Zheng." [10th year of Duke Xuan]
"In the sixth month, it rained." [3rd year of Duke Xi] "In spring, during the western hunt, a unicorn (lin) was captured." [14th year of Duke Ai]

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
禮記
是故禮者君之大柄也
紀綱旣正天下大定天下大定然後正六
律和五聲弦歌詩頌
其在朝廷則道仁聖禮義之序燕處則聽
雅頌之音行步則有環佩之聲升車則
有鸞和之音居處有禮進退有度百官
得其宜萬事得其序
天下莫不貴者道也
===
第貳場
論
天下文章
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令二千石興廉舉孝詔〔元朔元年〕
擬唐命吏部尚書與學士法官更定律令
誥〔貞觀元年〕
擬
駕幸太學
punctuated:
《禮記》
是故禮者，君之大柄也。
紀綱旣正，天下大定；天下大定，然後正六律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌。
其在朝廷，則道仁聖禮義之序；燕處，則聽《雅》《頌》之音；行步，則有環佩之聲；升車，則有鸞和之音。居處有禮，進退有度，百官得其宜，萬事得其序。
天下莫不貴者，道也。

第貳場
論
天下文章。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令二千石興廉舉孝詔〔元朔元年〕。
擬唐命吏部尚書與學士法官更定律令誥〔貞觀元年〕。
擬駕幸太學
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji):
"Therefore, ritual propriety is the ruler's great handle of authority."
"Once the fundamental principles and institutions have been rectified, the realm is brought to great stability; once the realm is brought to great stability, one then rectifies the six pitch-standards, harmonizes the five notes, and sings the Odes and Hymns to string accompaniment."
"When he is at court, he speaks of the proper order of benevolence, sageliness, ritual propriety, and righteousness; when he rests at leisure, he listens to the music of the Major and Minor Court Hymns (Ya) and the Temple Hymns (Song); when he walks, there is the sound of his girdle-jades and pendants; when he mounts his carriage, there is the sound of the luan and he carriage bells. In his dwelling there is ritual propriety, and in his advancing and retiring there is due measure; thus the hundred officials attain what is fitting for them, and the myriad affairs attain their proper order."
"What none in the realm fails to prize is the Way."

Second Session

Discourse:
"The literary compositions of the realm."

Edicts, Mandates, and Memorials [candidates are examined on one topic from among these]:
An imitation of the Han edict ordering the Two-Thousand-Bushel officials (Commandery Grand Administrators) to promote the incorrupt and recommend the filial [first year of the Yuanshuo era (128 BCE)].
An imitation of the Tang mandate ordering the Minister of Personnel, together with the Academician-Scholars and judicial officials, to revise and establish the statutes and ordinances [first year of the Zhenguan era (627 CE)].
An imitation of [a memorial of gratitude on the occasion of] the Imperial Carriage visiting the Directorate of Education (Taixue) …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
賜三氏子孫宴謝表
判語〔五條〕
信牌
私釁
祭享
夜禁
越訴
第叁場
策〔五道〕
===
問帝王之治莫大於約已裕民三代什一
成賦上下咸足卓乎不可尚已後世履
畝加稅民由之困而其用亦不足乃漢
文帝屢詔免租天下富庶固矣而太倉
之粟陳陳相因此其故何歟
國家經賦之制準諸三代
二祖
列聖一德相承皆以愛養黎元培植基本爲先
務每蠲正供以恤民隱今
punctuated:
賜三氏子孫宴謝表。

判語〔五條〕：
信牌。
私釁。
祭享。
夜禁。
越訴。

第叁場
策〔五道〕

問：帝王之治，莫大於約已裕民。三代什一成賦，上下咸足，卓乎不可尚已！後世履畝加稅，民由之困，而其用亦不足。乃漢文帝屢詔免租，天下富庶固矣，而太倉之粟陳陳相因，此其故何歟？國家經賦之制，準諸三代。二祖、列聖一德相承，皆以愛養黎元、培植基本爲先務，每蠲正供以恤民隱。今
translation_en:
…bestows a banquet on the descendants of the Three Lineages (Kong, Yan, and Zeng).

Legal Judgments [five items]:
1. Official warrants (xinpai).
2. Unauthorized frontier hostilities (sixin).
3. Sacrificial offerings (jixiang).
4. Night curfews (yejin).
5. Bypassing the proper judicial hierarchy in filing lawsuits (yuesu).

Third Session
Policy Questions [five items]

Question: In the governance of emperors and kings, nothing is greater than restraining oneself and enriching the people. In the Three Dynasties, the regular tax was established at one-tenth, so that both superiors and inferiors had sufficient resources—how eminent and unsurpassable! In later ages, fields were surveyed by the acre to increase taxes; the people were thereby impoverished, and yet state revenues were still insufficient. However, Emperor Wen of the Han repeatedly issued edicts remitting land taxes; the empire naturally became wealthy and populous, while the grain in the Grand Granary piled up layer upon layer, old upon old. What was the reason for this?

The regular taxation system of our State is modeled on that of the Three Dynasties. The Two Progenitors (Taizu and Taizong) and Successive Sages have inherited the same virtue, all taking the cherished nurturing of the common people and the cultivation of the fundamental root of the state as their primary task, frequently remitting regular tax quotas in order to show compassion for the people's hidden sufferings. title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
詔令具在可悉指而揄揚之歟我
皇上登極以來日惟惠民是念
萬幾之暇
御書十二事扁之
內庭其於約已裕民之道至肫切也頃以吏
治弊於玩愒因加聚飭顧有司未悉
上意嚮兢以靡文追徵爲塞責計於是
汪濊之澤幾於淤壅
皇上洞見隱微
===
詔責有司幷免積逋大哉
皇仁薄海內外罔不舉手加額歌詠懽呼矣夫
歲入歲出經費有常也乃
天恩浩蕩若此其劑盈縮以裕公私固自有所
本矣諸士子其揚言之以昭
上德且俾有司知所宜云
問阜財利用錢幣爲先自成周立九府圜
法其制可謂備已稽古夏商間一行之
乃其法不盛傳何歟豈二代猶權宜之
punctuated:
詔令具在，可悉指而揄揚之歟？我皇上登極以來，日惟惠民是念，萬幾之暇，御書十二事扁之內庭，其於約已裕民之道，至肫切也。頃以吏治弊於玩愒，因加聚飭，顧有司未悉上意嚮，兢以靡文追徵爲塞責計，於是汪濊之澤幾於淤壅。皇上洞見隱微，詔責有司，幷免積逋。大哉皇仁！薄海內外，罔不舉手加額，歌詠懽呼矣。夫歲入歲出，經費有常也，乃天恩浩蕩若此，其劑盈縮以裕公私，固自有所本矣。諸士子其揚言之，以昭上德，且俾有司知所宜云。
問：阜財利用，錢幣爲先。自成周立九府圜法，其制可謂備已。稽古夏、商，間一行之，乃其法不盛傳，何歟？豈二代猶權宜之
translation_en:
…edicts and ordinances are all extant; can you point them out in full and extol them? Since Our August Emperor ascended the throne, day by day His thoughts have been solely on benefitting the people. In moments of leisure from the myriad affairs of state, He personally wrote out twelve matters and hung them on plaques in the Inner Court; regarding the way of restraining Himself and enriching the people, He is most earnest and sincere. Recently, because official administration had deteriorated into negligent idling, He consequently applied strict admonition [reading 聚飭 as 督飭/整飭?]. Yet local officials failed to comprehend the direction of the Sovereign's intentions, vying to use empty formalities and the pressing of tax arrears as a means to shirk their responsibilities; thus the vast and deep imperial bounty was almost choked and blocked. The August Emperor, with penetrating insight into hidden subtleties, issued an edict reprimanding the officials and at the same time remitting accumulated tax arrears. Great indeed is the Imperial benevolence! Within and beyond the seas, there is no one who does not raise their hands to their foreheads in gratitude, singing praises and cheering with joy. Now, annual revenues and annual expenditures have regular norms for financing; yet since Heaven's grace is as vast and boundless as this, the way it balances surplus and deficit so as to enrich both the state and private individuals must surely have its fundamental basis. You scholars, set this forth clearly so as to manifest the Sovereign's virtue, and moreover to let the officials know what is appropriate to do.

Question: In increasing wealth and facilitating utility, coinage comes first. Since the Flourishing Zhou established the "round currency system" (yuanfa) of the Nine Treasuries (jiufu), its institutions may be called complete. Examining antiquity, during the Xia and Shang dynasties it was practiced from time to time, yet their systems were not widely transmitted—why is that? Could it be that in the Two Dynasties it was still an expedient…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
術而周官則經义之制耶說者謂泉布
之法陶唐氏已有之而漢以後置造不
一或自輕而入於重或自重而入於輕
其稱名殊也果孰爲中乎抑其通塞誠
關於是歟我
國家制錢統局實源
累朝更鑄或通之而輒以塞或各以其方不
相布其究安在頃
主上用言官議令各省開局鼓冶以期通行而
專董以官節目甚備矣其於周之制何
如也夫法貴宜民慮當虔始不知鑄之
之法果何經理而後可以無弊行之之
法若何區畫而後可以無阻乎願詳言
之以覘爾用世之略
問欽若昊天敬授人時王者調元賛化第
一義也粤稽古昔堯之曆象舜之璣衡
洪範所載庶徵班班可考說者謂渾天
一儀獨臻其奥果起自何時與三代而
punctuated:
術，而《周官》則經义之制耶？說者謂泉布之法，陶唐氏已有之，而漢以後置造不一，或自輕而入於重，或自重而入於輕，其稱名殊也，果孰爲中乎？抑其通塞誠關於是歟？我國家制錢統局，實源累朝更鑄，或通之而輒以塞，或各以其方不相布，其究安在？頃主上用言官議，令各省開局鼓冶，以期通行，而專董以官，節目甚備矣。其於周之制何如也？夫法貴宜民，慮當虔始。不知鑄之之法，果何經理而後可以無弊？行之之法，若何區畫而後可以無阻乎？願詳言之，以覘爾用世之略。

問：欽若昊天，敬授人時，王者調元賛化第一義也。粤稽古昔，堯之曆象、舜之璣衡，《洪範》所載庶徵，班班可考。說者謂渾天一儀，獨臻其奥，果起自何時與？三代而
translation_en:
…expedients, whereas the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) represents an enduring system of governance [? 經义 for 經久]? Commentators say that the method of coinage and currency already existed under the Taotang clan (Yao), while from the Han dynasty onward its manufacture varied: sometimes shifting from light to heavy, sometimes from heavy to light, with differing denominations and names. Which of these truly achieved the proper balance? Or did their circulation and obstruction genuinely depend upon this? Our dynasty's system of centralizing the minting of standard cash in official bureaus truly originates from the successive reigns' repeated recoinages; yet sometimes when effort is made to circulate them they quickly become obstructed, or each region uses its own local currency without circulating them mutually. Wherein lies the ultimate cause of this? Recently the reigning Sovereign adopted the deliberations of the Speaking Officials (censors and supervising secretaries) and ordered the various provinces to open minting bureaus and cast coins in hopes of achieving universal circulation, assigning dedicated officials to supervise them, with very thorough detailed regulations. How does this compare with the system of the Zhou? Now, laws value suitability to the people, and planning ought to be reverently careful at the beginning. I do not know by what management the method of casting can be rendered free of abuses, and by what planning the method of circulation can be freed of obstruction? I wish you to speak of this in detail, so that I may observe your practical statecraft.

Question: Reverently following the vast Heavens and respectfully bestowing the seasons upon the people is the foremost principle by which a true king harmonizes the primalvitality and assists the cosmic transformations. Examining antiquity, the calendrical phenomena of Yao, the armillary sphere and transverse tube (jiheng) of Shun, and the various verifications recorded in the "Great Plan" (Hongfan) can all be clearly investigated. Commentators say that the celestial globe (huntian yi) alone reaches the deepest profundity; in what era did it truly originate? From the Three Dynasties…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
下譚象緯者無論數十家圖書凡若干
卷其〔日躔月離日法斗分〕與夫氣朔盈
虛可得而指言之與大初以鍾律大衍
以蓍策直驗陰陽之毫忽稱運用之精
矣其亦根柢渾〔天〕而作否也於時四十
諸家曆若梁〔令瓚李淳風輩〕似非無稽
者豈皆不足法與我
朝司天占步獨有取於郭守敬所製簡儀謂
其智巧兼備矣今歷年既遠天度漸差
隨時脩改以求合天則保章氏職也爾
多士必有能窺其際者願明以告我
===
問
國家鹽政甚詳邇來寖弊他省姑勿論已解
行之邇來民間往往稱不便以故私鹽
盛行月無虛日今關中所食者花馬池
之產而河洛汴鄴之間則用淮蘆即太
汾亦煎鹽矣於是有分地改額之議不
punctuated:
下，譚象緯者無論數十家，圖書凡若干卷。其〔日躔、月離、日法、斗分〕，與夫氣朔盈虛，可得而指言之與？《大初》以鍾律，《大衍》以蓍策，直驗陰陽之毫忽，稱運用之精矣，其亦根柢渾〔天〕而作否也？於時四十諸家曆，若梁〔令瓚、李淳風輩〕，似非無稽者，豈皆不足法與？我朝司天占步，獨有取於郭守敬所製簡儀，謂其智巧兼備矣。今歷年既遠，天度漸差，隨時脩改以求合天，則保章氏職也。爾多士必有能窺其際者，願明以告我。

問：國家鹽政甚詳，邇來寖弊。他省姑勿論已，解行之邇來，民間往往稱不便，以故私鹽盛行，月無虛日。今關中所食者，花馬池之產；而河、洛、汴、鄴之間，則用淮、蘆；即太、汾亦煎鹽矣。於是有分地改額之議，不
translation_en:
…downward, those who have discussed celestial phenomena and the stars and planets number no fewer than several dozen schools, and their charts and books amount to so many scrolls. As for the [solar path, lunar mansions, daily denominator, and Dipper fraction], along with the waxing and waning of solar terms and new moons, can these be pointed out and explained? The Grand Inception (Taichu) calendar used pitch-pipes, and the Great Expansion (Dayan) calendar used yarrow-stalk divination, directly verifying the slightest fractions of yin and yang and earning praise for the precision of their operation—were they also created on the foundation of the [Celestial] Sphere theory or not? Among the calendars of the forty-odd schools over time, figures such as Liang [Lingzan 梁令瓚 and Li Chunfeng 李淳風 and their peers] seem not to have been without basis; could they all be unworthy of emulation? In our dynasty, the astronomers who observe and calculate the heavens have exclusively adopted the Simplified Armillary Sphere (jianyi) constructed by Guo Shoujing 郭守敬, declaring it complete in both wisdom and ingenuity. Now that many years have passed and the celestial degrees have gradually diverged, revising and correcting it in accordance with the times so as to seek conformity with the heavens is the duty of the Astronomer-Royal (baozhangshi). Among you many scholars there must be those able to peer into these subtleties; I wish you to inform me clearly.

Question: The State’s salt administration is exceedingly detailed, yet in recent times it has gradually fallen into abuse. Setting aside other provinces for the moment, in the circuit where Xie池 (Xiezhou) salt circulates [?], the common people have recently often complained of its inconvenience, and for this reason illicit salt is rampant, with not a day in the month free of it. Nowadays, what is consumed in Guanzhong is the product of Huamachi; between the Yellow and Luo rivers and in Bian and Ye, they use Huai and Changlu salt; and even in Taiyuan and Fenzhou they boil earth to make salt. Consequently, there are proposals to redivide the distribution territories and alter the quotas; I do not…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
知果當與否夫額課不足勢必取盈於
商轉運他方民不樂售則官爲之鬻而
商與民胥困矣說者謂自趨支之法立
而商困自澆曬之法立而民困然歟又
謂榦取及期則所獲不可勝用人亦且
樂用之而或者又欲令附近居民籍名
所司聽其撈採計其所獲劑量而歸之
官亦庶幾地無遺利焉果可行歟夫興
利者在革弊今鹽之法弊矣願聞所以
===
革之之道
問山西三關其在寧鴈則大同爲之藩籬
惟偏老與虜爲鄰獨稱要害自辛丑虜
入掠遼沁壬子掠忻代於是大同不可
恃而畫地分守三關益重矣夫山西歲
供大同倍於三關顧不能藉之捍蔽至
以堂奥爲門户籌邊者遂有設官分守
未詳之議果然與總兵之駐兵寧武也
若曰居中調度爲便耳而山西幅員且
punctuated:
知果當與否？夫額課不足，勢必取盈於商；轉運他方，民不樂售，則官爲之鬻，而商與民胥困矣。說者謂：「自趨支之法立而商困，自澆曬之法立而民困。」然歟？又謂：「榦取及期，則所獲不可勝用，人亦且樂用之。」而或者又欲令附近居民籍名所司，聽其撈採，計其所獲，劑量而歸之官，亦庶幾地無遺利焉。果可行歟？夫興利者在革弊，今鹽之法弊矣，願聞所以革之之道。

問：山西三關，其在寧、鴈，則大同爲之藩籬，惟偏、老與虜爲鄰，獨稱要害。自辛丑虜入掠遼、沁，壬子掠忻、代，於是大同不可恃，而畫地分守，三關益重矣。夫山西歲供大同倍於三關，顧不能藉之捍蔽，至以堂奥爲門户。籌邊者遂有設官分守未詳之議，果然與？總兵之駐兵寧武也，若曰居中調度爲便耳。而山西幅員且
translation_en:
…not known whether this is truly appropriate or not. Now, when the quota of revenue falls short, one is bound by circumstance to make up the deficit from the merchants; when the salt is transported to other regions and the common people are not eager to buy it, the officials sell it on their behalf, and thus both merchants and the people are driven into distress. Commentators say: "Since the method of hastening collection (quzhi) was established, the merchants have suffered; since the method of pouring and sun-drying (jiaoshai) was established, the people have suffered." Is this so? Others say: "If it is gathered and extracted at the proper season, the yield will be more than can be exhausted, and people will moreover be glad to use it." Still others wish to have nearby residents register their names with the competent authorities, allow them to dredge and gather the salt, calculate what they obtain, and apportion a share to be turned over to the government, in the hope that no profit of the land will be left uncollected. Can this truly be put into practice? Now, promoting profit lies in eliminating abuses. Today the salt regulations are ridden with abuses; I wish to hear the way by which to reform them.

Question: Of the Three Passes of Shanxi, as for Ningwu and Yanmen, Datong serves as their protective screen; only偏關 (Pianguan) and 老營堡 (Laoying Fort) border the northern caitiffs and alone are deemed vital strategic points. Since the xinchou year (1541), when the caitiffs invaded and plundered Liaozhou and Qinzhou, and the renzi year (1552), when they plundered Xinzhou and Daizhou, Datong could no longer be relied upon; thus territory was demarcated for separate defense, and the Three Passes became even more important. Now, Shanxi's annual provisions for Datong are double those for the Three Passes, yet we cannot rely on Datong for shielding and protection, to the point that the inner chambers have been turned into the outer gateway. Frontier strategists have consequently raised proposals—not yet fully detailed [?]—for establishing officials to divide the defense. Is this truly right? As for the Regional Commander (zongbing) stationing his troops at Ningwu, it is as if to say that being positioned in the center makes it convenient to direct and deploy forces. Yet the territory of Shanxi is…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
不甚廣又地力所入人力所出皆以給
邊撫臣所經理者民事卽邊事也議者
謂不宜兼邊務欲倣延寧之制增一撫
臣專駐偏老與宣大共爲猗角而並移
總兵於其地以當虜衝蓋創於丁卯之
患耳夫虜入此則重此虜入彼則重彼
豈制虜之策在虜而不在我耶卽今虜
衆納款疆圉寧謐當事諸臣仰承
廟謨及時大脩邊政諸備虜事宜無容贅者
獨與爾諸生講建官責守之可否
punctuated: 不甚廣，又地力所入、人力所出，皆以給邊，撫臣所經理者，民事卽邊事也。議者謂不宜兼邊務，欲倣延、寧之制，增一撫臣專駐偏、老，與宣、大共爲猗角，而並移總兵於其地，以當虜衝，蓋創於丁卯之患耳。夫虜入此則重此，虜入彼則重彼，豈制虜之策在虜而不在我耶？卽今虜衆納款，疆圉寧謐，當事諸臣仰承廟謨，及時大脩邊政，諸備虜事宜無容贅者，獨與爾諸生講建官責守之可否。
translation_en: …not particularly expansive; moreover, all the revenue yielded by the land and the labor expended by the people go to supply the frontier, so in what the Grand Coordinator (fuchen 撫臣) manages, civil affairs are themselves frontier affairs. Yet some in the deliberations argue that he should not concurrently handle frontier military affairs, and wish to imitate the system of Yansui 延綏 and Ningxia 寧夏 by adding another Grand Coordinator stationed specifically at Piantou 偏頭 and Laoying 老營, forming mutual support like horns and legs with Xuanfu 宣府 and Datong 大同, while also moving the Regional Commander (zongbing 總兵) to that territory to bear the brunt of caitiff (lu 虜) attacks—an idea prompted, in truth, by the disaster of the dingmao 丁卯 year (1567). Now, if when the caitiffs invade here we place weight here, and when the caitiffs invade there we place weight there, does the strategy for controlling the caitiffs rest with the caitiffs and not with us? At present the caitiff hordes have submitted to tribute relations and the borders are peaceful and tranquil; the officials in charge, reverently upholding the plans of the Imperial Court, are seizing the time to carry out a great overhaul of frontier administration. On the various matters of preparing against the caitiffs there is no need for superfluous words; I ask you students only to discuss the advisability of establishing officials and assigning responsibilities for defense.

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子路有聞未之能行唯恐有聞
張泰徵〔深得子路急行之心且行文典〕
同考試官教諭唐　批〔雅可誦取之〕
考試官學正梅　批〔醇正〕
考試官教授朱　批〔辭不費而意足〕
門人於賢者而狀其聞斯行之之心焉夫以後
===
聞爲恐則前所聞者急於行矣子路之善用其
勇也如此且善之在天下也無窮吾人之聞之
也亦無窮然聞以行爲貴行之敏爲尤貴其惟
子路乎質本兼人而無聞弗行欲以悉衆善於
不遺性無宿諾而無行弗速欲以俟後聞於不
已聞善斯行其心也或未能焉惕然於善之復
繼而懼其聞之或壅所以奮迅於脩爲者何弗
至也有聞則喜其心也或未行焉悚然於聞之
復來而懼其躬之不逮所以激昂於邁往者何
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「子路有聞，未之能行，唯恐有聞。」
張泰徵
同考試官教諭唐批：〔深得子路急行之心，且行文典雅可誦，取之。〕
考試官學正梅批：〔醇正。〕
考試官教授朱批：〔辭不費而意足。〕
門人於賢者，而狀其聞斯行之之心焉。夫以後聞爲恐，則前所聞者急於行矣；子路之善用其勇也如此。且善之在天下也無窮，吾人之聞之也亦無窮；然聞以行爲貴，行之敏爲尤貴，其惟子路乎！質本兼人，而無聞弗行，欲以悉衆善於不遺；性無宿諾，而無行弗速，欲以俟後聞於不已。聞善斯行，其心也。或未能焉，惕然於善之復繼，而懼其聞之或壅，所以奮迅於脩爲者，何弗至也！有聞則喜，其心也。或未行焉，悚然於聞之復來，而懼其躬之不逮，所以激昂於邁往者，何
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books
"When Zilu heard anything and had not yet been able to put it into practice, his only fear was that he should hear something else."
Zhang Taizheng 張泰徵
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 唐: [He deeply grasps Zilu's mind-set of urgency to put things into practice; moreover, the style is refined and elegant, worthy of recitation. Selected.]
Comment by Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Mei 梅: [Pure and orthodox.]
Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu 朱: [The words are not wasteful, yet the meaning is complete.]

The disciples, regarding the worthy man, described his mind-set of immediately putting into practice whatever he heard. Now, since he took hearing something subsequent as a cause for fear, he was all the more urgent to practice what he had previously heard; such was how Zilu made good use of his courage. Moreover, the good that exists in the world is inexhaustible, and our hearing of it is likewise inexhaustible; yet in hearing, putting it into practice is what is valued, and promptness in practice is valued even more—was this not uniquely true of Zilu! His natural endowment had twice the energy of others, and there was nothing he heard that he did not practice, wishing thereby to exhaustively embrace all good without omission; by nature he never slept on a promise, and there was no action in which he was not swift, wishing thereby to await subsequent learning unceasingly. To hear the good and immediately practice it—such was his mind-set. Should he happen not yet to be able to do so, he grew apprehensive that another good might follow in succession, fearing that what he had heard might become backed up; thus, in rousing himself to cultivate and act, to what lengths did he not go! To rejoice upon hearing something—such was his mind-set. Should he happen not yet to have practiced it, he grew alarmed that further learning might arrive again, fearing that his own person might fail to keep pace; thus, in stirring himself to press forward, how…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
弗力也視善常有餘視行常不足皇皇焉日不
暇給即其請益之心蓋善雖已行猶若未行者
矣矧未行耶方以有聞爲幸即以有聞爲恐兢
兢焉不遑寧處推其果行之念蓋聞雖未有常
若已有者矣矧已有耶是未能行者正其欲行
之急而恐有聞者實其樂聞之本心也子路之
勇用之於此其升堂也有以哉抑多聞愼行聖
門之教也子路聞脩已爲政之訓則少之聞浮
海之歎則喜是謂不知不闕無所取裁者也有
===
父兄在夫子固嘗以退之矣雖然其視悅道而
自畫者何如也學者以子路之勇而加以顏子
之擇其庶乎
天地位焉萬物育焉
景　明
同考試官教諭葉　批　〔講一體處透徹有味殆究心於〕〔理學者〕
考試官學正梅　批　〔沖雅〕
考試官教授朱　批　〔理趣悠然〕
punctuated:
弗力也。視善常有餘，視行常不足，皇皇焉日不暇給。即其請益之心，蓋善雖已行，猶若未行者矣，矧未行耶？方以有聞爲幸，即以有聞爲恐，兢兢焉不遑寧處。推其果行之念，蓋聞雖未有，常若已有者矣，矧已有耶？是未能行者，正其欲行之急；而恐有聞者，實其樂聞之本心也。子路之勇用之於此，其升堂也有以哉！抑多聞愼行，聖門之教也。子路聞脩已爲政之訓則少之，聞浮海之歎則喜，是謂不知不闕，無所取裁者也。有父兄在，夫子固嘗以退之矣。雖然，其視悅道而自畫者，何如也？學者以子路之勇，而加以顏子之擇，其庶乎！
「天地位焉，萬物育焉。」
景明
同考試官教諭葉批：〔講一體處，透徹有味，殆究心於〕〔理學者。〕
考試官學正梅批：〔沖雅。〕
考試官教授朱批：〔理趣悠然。〕
translation_en:
…not exert his strength? He regarded the good as always in surplus and his own practice of it as always falling short, urgently pressing on as if the day were not long enough. Judging from his mind that always asked for more, even when a good deed had already been practiced, it was to him as though it had not yet been practiced—how much more so when it had not yet been practiced! Just as he counted himself fortunate to hear a teaching, he at once dreaded hearing another, anxiously unable to rest in peace. Inferring from his determination to act resolutely, even when there was nothing new that he had heard, it was to him always as though he had already heard something—how much more so when he already had! Thus, his not yet being able to put it into practice was precisely the urgency of his desire to act; and his dread of hearing something new was in truth the very heart of his delight in hearing it. That Zilu 子路 applied his courage to this—was there not good reason for his having ascended to the hall!

Even so, to hear much and act cautiously was the teaching of the Sage's school. When Zilu heard the instruction on cultivating oneself in order to govern, he belittled it; when he heard the Master's sigh about setting out on the sea on a raft, he was delighted. This is what is meant by not leaving aside what one does not know, and lacking the means to judge and measure. "While your father and elder brothers are alive"—the Master had indeed once used these words to hold him back. Even so, how does he compare with those who profess to delight in the Way yet set limits for themselves? If the student takes the courage of Zilu and adds to it the discerning choice of Yanzi 顏子, he will be near the mark!

"Heaven and earth take their proper places, and the myriad things are nourished."

By Jing Ming 景明.

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Ye 葉: [His exposition of forming one body with all things is thorough and rich in flavor; he is likely someone who has devoted his mind to the study of Principle.]
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies (xuezheng) Mei 梅: [Serene and refined.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor (jiaoshou) Zhu 朱: [The resonance of its principles is deep and far-reaching.]

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
君子贊化於一心體道之功極矣夫道涵於心
與造化通也君子位天地育萬物而盡道於心
者至矣哉子思之意若曰道也者其三極之精
乎故心不離乎道而天地萬物不離乎心矣何
也天地設位而中其體也君子中天地而致之
則吾心與天地相對越矣由是陰陽順而確然
者常清也剛柔理而隤然者常寧也高明博厚
斂之一心而通之兩儀自各安其所矣其範圍
天地而不過乎萬物竝育而和其命也君子先
===
萬物而致之則吾心與萬物相流衍矣由是絪
緼合而氣化者醇如也精神會而形化者熙如
也人性物性涵之一心而達之庶類自各遂其
生矣其曲成萬物而不遺乎要之天地萬物莫
非吾之心也位天地育萬物莫非盡吾之心也
一心盡而性命全矣體道之極功如此哉夫以
天地萬物而觀天地萬物也則至高矣至厚矣
至繁矣以道而觀天地萬物也則天地一中耳
萬物一和耳中先天地而資萬物之始和生萬
punctuated: 君子贊化於一心，體道之功極矣。夫道涵於心，與造化通也。君子位天地、育萬物，而盡道於心者至矣哉！子思之意若曰：道也者，其三極之精乎？故心不離乎道，而天地萬物不離乎心矣。何也？天地設位，而中其體也；君子中天地而致之，則吾心與天地相對越矣。由是陰陽順，而確然者常清也；剛柔理，而隤然者常寧也。高明博厚，斂之一心而通之，兩儀自各安其所矣，其範圍天地而不過乎？萬物竝育，而和其命也；君子先萬物而致之，則吾心與萬物相流衍矣。由是絪緼合，而氣化者醇如也；精神會，而形化者熙如也。人性物性，涵之一心而達之，庶類自各遂其生矣，其曲成萬物而不遺乎？要之，天地萬物莫非吾之心也，位天地、育萬物，莫非盡吾之心也。一心盡而性命全矣，體道之極功如此哉！夫以天地萬物而觀天地萬物也，則至高矣、至厚矣、至繁矣；以道而觀天地萬物也，則天地一中耳，萬物一和耳。中先天地而資萬物之始，和生萬
translation_en:
When the noble man assists the transformative processes through his single mind, the merit of embodying the Way reaches its ultimate point. Now, the Way is contained within the mind and communicates with the creative transformations of nature. When the noble man establishes Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurtures the myriad things, how supreme is his exhaustion of the Way within his mind!

Zisi’s 子思 meaning is as if to say: Is not the Way the essence of the Three Ultimates (Heaven, Earth, and Man)? Therefore, the mind does not depart from the Way, and Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things do not depart from the mind. Why is this? Heaven and Earth have their established positions, and centrality (equilibrium) is their substance. Standing at the center of Heaven and Earth, the noble man extends this centrality to the utmost, so that our mind responds in mutual presence with Heaven and Earth. From this, yin and yang are in harmony, and that which is firm above (Heaven) remains ever clear; the hard and the soft are in order, and that which is docile below (Earth) remains ever tranquil. High brilliance and broad thickness are gathered into the single mind and communicated outward, so the Two Modes (Heaven and Earth) naturally rest each in its proper place. Does this not encompass Heaven and Earth without erring?

The myriad things are nourished together, and harmony is their mandate. Preceding the myriad things, the noble man extends this harmony to the utmost, so that our mind flows forth in concert with the myriad things. From this, the generative forces fuse together, and things transformed by vital energy (qi) are pure; spiritual essences converge, and things transformed by physical form flourish in joy. The nature of human beings and the nature of things are contained within the single mind and extended outward, so the multitude of species naturally fulfill their lives. Does this not intricately complete the myriad things without leaving any behind?

In sum, Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are none other than my own mind; establishing Heaven and Earth and nurturing the myriad things are none other than fully realizing my own mind. When the single mind is fully realized, nature and destiny are complete. Such is the ultimate achievement of embodying the Way!

Now, if one views Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things from the standpoint of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, they are utterly high, utterly thick, and utterly multitudinous. Yet if one views Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things from the standpoint of the Way, then Heaven and Earth are simply a single centrality, and the myriad things are simply a single harmony. Centrality precedes Heaven and Earth and provides the beginning for the myriad things; harmony gives birth to the myriad…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
物而見天地之情君子致之而位育之者亦還
其本體之眞而已豈待於外而强之一哉故曰
仁者以天地萬物爲一體噫達於一體之義而
道自不可離矣
使契爲司徒敎以人倫父子有親君臣有
義夫婦有別長幼有序朋友有信放勳
曰勞之來之匡之直之輔之翼之使自
得之又從而振德之
王忠顯
===
同考試官敎諭王　批〔此題不難於措詞而難於莊整〕
時義若此可以式矣
考試官學正梅　批〔通篇練達無一字苟且〕
考試官敎授朱　批〔簡潔有味取之〕
聖君命官以敷敎而曲盡其敎之之術焉蓋人
倫者民性之固有也以此立敎而曲盡其術焉
聖人之憂民切矣孟子闢許行之意若曰聖人
以一身而任君師之責則民之逸居無敎固其
責之不容諉者也而豈能以無憂哉於是選於
punctuated:
物而見天地之情。君子致之而位育之者，亦還其本體之眞而已，豈待於外而强之一哉？故曰：「仁者以天地萬物爲一體。」噫！達於一體之義，而道自不可離矣。

使契爲司徒，敎以人倫：父子有親，君臣有義，夫婦有別，長幼有序，朋友有信。放勳曰：「勞之來之，匡之直之，輔之翼之，使自得之，又從而振德之。」
王忠顯
同考試官敎諭王　批〔此題不難於措詞，而難於莊整。〕時義若此，可以式矣。
考試官學正梅　批〔通篇練達，無一字苟且。〕
考試官敎授朱　批〔簡潔有味，取之。〕

聖君命官以敷敎，而曲盡其敎之之術焉。蓋人倫者，民性之固有也。以此立敎，而曲盡其術焉，聖人之憂民切矣。孟子闢許行之意，若曰：聖人以一身而任君師之責，則民之逸居無敎，固其責之不容諉者也，而豈能以無憂哉？於是選於
translation_en:
…myriad things and thereby manifests the true tendencies of Heaven and Earth. When the superior man carries them to their utmost so that Heaven and Earth are given their proper places and the myriad things are nourished, he is merely returning to the authenticity of his original substance. How could he depend upon anything external and forcibly unite them into one? Therefore it is said: "The humane person takes Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one body." Ah! Once one comprehends the meaning of forming one body, the Way naturally cannot be departed from for an instant.

"He appointed Xie (契) to be Minister of Instruction (Situ 司徒), to teach the people the human relationships: that between father and son there should be affection; between ruler and minister, righteousness; between husband and wife, distinction; between old and young, a proper order; and between friends, faithfulness. Fangxun (放勳) [Yao] said: 'Encourage them, lead them on; rectify them, straighten them; help them, give them wings—so as to cause them to attain it for themselves, and then further stimulate them and confer kindness upon them.'"
By Wang Zhongxian (王忠顯).
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (Jiaoyu) Wang: [For this topic, the difficulty lies not in the phrasing, but in achieving solemnity and structural neatness.] An examination essay on the classics (shiyi 時義) such as this can serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies (Xuezheng) Mei: [Seasoned and accomplished throughout, without a single careless word.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor (Jiaoshou) Zhu: [Concise and flavorful; selected.]

The sage ruler appointed an official to propagate instruction, and exhaustively detailed the art of teaching them. For the human relationships are inherent in the nature of the people. By establishing instruction on this basis and exhaustively detailing its art, the sage's concern for the people was earnest indeed. When Mencius refuted Xu Hing (許行), his meaning was as if to say: Since the sage in his own person assumes the responsibilities of both ruler and teacher, if the people dwell in idleness without instruction, it is certainly a responsibility he cannot shirk—how then could he be free from anxiety? Thereupon, choosing from among…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
衆而得契焉使作司徒以掌教也教以人倫以
正德也父子也君臣也夫婦長幼朋友也人之
所爲倫也親也義也序別信也倫之所固有也
因其有者而導之使有則所以爲之法者不得
不詳矣是故放勳命契之辭有曰民性不齊教
不可以槩施也有曲成之方焉勞來以勸其善
也匡直以救其失也輔翼於始而親義序別信
之性使自得之斯已矣然人情易怠教不可以
中弛也有加惠之術焉提撕之以牖其明也警
===
覺之以作其勤也振德於終而親義序別信之
倫使日新焉斯已矣是知聖人之憂民也旣得
人以弘其教而又立法以責其成仁天下之心
固甚切也其何暇於耕哉嗚呼書有之愼徽五
典五典克從言身教也故峻德明而萬邦時雍
玄德升而四方風動聖人之立教蓋有本矣彼
崇師重傅建學召儒教非不至而於化民成俗
竟何補哉噫孟子論堯舜憂民而卒歸之蕩蕩
巍巍其旨深矣
punctuated: 衆而得契焉，使作司徒以掌教也。教以人倫，以正德也。父子也、君臣也、夫婦、長幼、朋友也，人之所爲倫也；親也、義也、序、別、信也，倫之所固有也。因其有者而導之使有，則所以爲之法者不得不詳矣。是故放勳命契之辭有曰：民性不齊，教不可以槩施也，有曲成之方焉：勞來以勸其善也，匡直以救其失也，輔翼於始而親、義、序、別、信之性，使自得之斯已矣。然人情易怠，教不可以中弛也，有加惠之術焉：提撕之以牖其明也，警覺之以作其勤也，振德於終而親、義、序、別、信之倫，使日新焉斯已矣。是知聖人之憂民也，旣得人以弘其教，而又立法以責其成，仁天下之心固甚切也，其何暇於耕哉？嗚呼！《書》有之：「愼徽五典，五典克從。」言身教也。故峻德明而萬邦時雍，玄德升而四方風動，聖人之立教蓋有本矣。彼崇師重傅、建學召儒，教非不至，而於化民成俗竟何補哉？噫！孟子論堯舜憂民，而卒歸之蕩蕩巍巍，其旨深矣。
translation_en:
…the multitude and found Xie 契, appointing him Minister of Instruction (Situ 司徒) to take charge of education. He taught them human relationships in order to rectify their virtue. Father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends—these are what constitute human relationships. Affection, righteousness, precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness—these are what are inherent in those relationships. Since one guides people on the basis of what they already possess so that they may realize it, the methods devised for doing so cannot but be detailed.

Therefore, the words with which Fangxun 放勳 [Yao 堯] charged Xie state: Since the natures of the people are not uniform, instruction cannot be applied to all in the same way; there are methods for bringing each to fulfillment in detail. Comfort them and draw them in to encourage their goodness; correct and straighten them to remedy their failings; support and assist them from the start, so that they may attain for themselves their nature of affection, righteousness, precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness—and nothing more. Yet human feelings easily grow lax, and instruction must not slacken midway; thus there are techniques for conferring further benefit. Prompt and remind them to open up their understanding; rouse and awaken them to stir up their diligence; thus, by renewing and enriching their virtue in the end, cause the relationships of affection, righteousness, precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness to be daily renewed—and nothing more.

From this we know that in the sage's concern for the people, having found the right man to broaden his instruction, he also established methods to require its completion. His heart of benevolence toward the world was truly most earnest—what leisure could he have had for plowing?

Alas! The Book of Documents (Shu 書) has it: "He cautiously set forth the beauty of the Five Constant Relationships, and the Five Constant Relationships were able to be followed." This speaks of teaching by personal example. Thus, when lofty virtue was made illustrious, the myriad states were harmonious; when profound virtue ascended, the four quarters were moved as by the wind. In establishing instruction, the sages indeed had a fundamental root! Those later rulers who honored teachers and esteemed tutors, founded schools and summoned Confucian scholars—their efforts at instruction were not unthorough, yet of what help were they in the end for transforming the people and perfecting customs? Ah! When Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) discussed Yao and Shun's 舜 concern for the people and finally歸 [attributed/returned] it to their being vast and lofty, his meaning was profound indeed.

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
易
彖曰大畜剛健篤實輝光日新其德剛上
而尚賢能止健大正也不家食吉養賢
也利涉大川應乎天也
張泰徵
同考試官教諭唐　批〔筆力簡古發揮體用合一之學〕
考試官學正梅　批〔明當〕
考試官教授米　批〔爽朗可誦〕
〔殆盡〕
===
觀大畜之名詞而體用之學備矣夫體立用行
學之備也卦具是義比大畜之所由以名辭與
彖傳之意謂夫學以大正爲體而尤以經濟爲
用是故畜匪大不足以弘其量卦名大畜者以
內乾剛健而不屈於欲外艮篤實而莫掩其輝
內外合而德不孤德之所以日新也非大畜所
由名乎畜匪正不足以端其趨詞爲利貞者以
變體剛上而尚賢卦德以艮而止健取舍當而
守弗渝德之所以爲至正也非利貞所由係乎
punctuated:
《易》
「《彖》曰：大畜，剛健篤實輝光，日新其德。剛上而尚賢，能止健，大正也。不家食吉，養賢也。利涉大川，應乎天也。」
張泰徵
同考試官教諭唐　批〔筆力簡古，發揮體用合一之學，殆盡。〕
考試官學正梅　批〔明當。〕
考試官教授米　批〔爽朗可誦。〕

觀大畜之名詞，而體用之學備矣。夫體立用行，學之備也。卦具是義，比大畜之所由以名辭與？《彖傳》之意，謂夫學以大正爲體，而尤以經濟爲用。是故畜匪大，不足以弘其量。卦名大畜者，以內乾剛健而不屈於欲，外艮篤實而莫掩其輝，內外合而德不孤，德之所以日新也，非大畜所由名乎？畜匪正，不足以端其趨。詞爲利貞者，以變體剛上而尚賢，卦德以艮而止健，取舍當而守弗渝，德之所以爲至正也，非利貞所由係乎？
translation_en:
Book of Changes (Yi)
"The Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says: Great Accumulation (Dachu): firm and strong, sincere and solid, brilliance daily renewing its virtue. The firm ascends and honors the worthy; able to restrain strength, this is great correctness. Not eating at home brings good fortune: this is nourishing the worthy. It is fitting to cross the great river: this is responding to Heaven."

Zhang Taizheng 张泰徵
Associate Examiner and Instructor Tang 唐 comments: [With a concise and archaic vigor of the brush, he expounds the learning of the unity of substance and function almost exhaustively.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Mei 梅 comments: [Clear and apt.]
Examiner and Prefectural Instructor Mi 米 comments: [Crisp, clear, and worthy of recitation.]

Observe the name and judgment of the hexagram Great Accumulation (Dachu), and the learning of substance and function is complete therein. Now, when substance is established and function is put into practice, learning is complete. Since the hexagram possesses this meaning, is this not why Great Accumulation is given its name and its judgment? The meaning of the Commentary on the Decision (Tuanzhuan) is that learning takes great correctness as its substance, and even more so takes ordering the world and aiding the people as its function. Therefore, if what is accumulated is not great, it is insufficient to broaden one's capacity. That the hexagram is named Great Accumulation is because inwardly the trigram Qian is firm and strong without yielding to selfish desires, while outwardly the trigram Gen is sincere and solid so that nothing obscures its brilliance. Inner and outer combine so that virtue does not stand alone—this is why virtue is daily renewed. Is this not why it is named Great Accumulation? If what is accumulated is not correct, it is insufficient to rectify one's orientation. That the judgment speaks of "advantageous to be firm and correct" is because, in its transformed structure, the firm line ascends and honors the worthy, and in the hexagram's attributes, Gen restrains strength; what is chosen and what is set aside are proper, and one's integrity does not waver—this is why its virtue is supremely correct. Is this not why the phrase "advantageous to be firm and correct" is appended to it?

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
夫德妙日新道由大正自可見之行矣於此而
不得乎君非君子經世之心也今六五有尚賢
之義則大亨之典隆而所畜之大而正者不患
於無用矣不家食之所以吉也於此而不得乎
時非君子濟世之心也今六五有應天之義則
經綸之猷顯而所畜之大而正者不終於小試
矣涉大川之所以利也吁大所畜而歸諸正體
也莫非用也推所畜而見諸行用也莫非體也
畜之道大矣哉大抵德非畜爲難正爲難伊尹
以天民自任遂成救民之功非應天之業乎然
堯舜之樂一介不苟所畜者正也彼好古知雄
博學如通畜非不弘矣而所仕非人所售非時
其何以大有爲哉是故君子正之爲貴
允正秋也萬物之所說也
王藻
同考試官教諭梁　批〔行文潔淨形容說字清切可玩〕
〔宜錄以式〕
考試官學正梅　批〔簡當〕
punctuated:
夫德妙日新，道由大正，自可見之行矣。於此而不得乎君，非君子經世之心也。今六五有尚賢之義，則大亨之典隆，而所畜之大而正者，不患於無用矣，「不家食」之所以吉也。於此而不得乎時，非君子濟世之心也。今六五有應天之義，則經綸之猷顯，而所畜之大而正者，不終於小試矣，「涉大川」之所以利也。吁！大所畜而歸諸正，體也，莫非用也；推所畜而見諸行，用也，莫非體也。畜之道大矣哉！大抵德非畜爲難，正爲難。伊尹以天民自任，遂成救民之功，非應天之業乎？然堯、舜之樂，一介不苟，所畜者正也。彼好古知雄，博學如通，畜非不弘矣，而所仕非人，所售非時，其何以大有爲哉？是故君子正之爲貴。
「允正秋也，萬物之所說也。」
王藻
同考試官教諭梁　批：〔行文潔淨，形容「說」字清切可玩，宜錄以式。〕
考試官學正梅　批：〔簡當。〕
translation_en:
Now, when one's virtue is wondrously renewed each day and one's Way proceeds from great rectitude, it can naturally be manifested in action. At such a point, not winning the favor of a ruler is not the intention of a gentleman who seeks to order the world. Now, since the Six in the fifth place carries the meaning of honoring the worthy, the rites of great sacrificial offering are grandly observed, and that which has been accumulated in greatness and rectitude need not worry about going unused; this is why "not eating at home" brings good fortune. At such a point, not meeting with the right time is not the intention of a gentleman who seeks to aid the world. Now, since the Six in the fifth place carries the meaning of responding to Heaven, the plans for ordering the state are made manifest, and that which has been accumulated in greatness and rectitude will not end in mere minor trials; this is why "crossing the great stream" is advantageous. Ah! Enlarging what one accumulates and returning it to rectitude is substance, yet none of it is not function; extending what one accumulates and manifesting it in action is function, yet none of it is not substance. Great indeed is the Way of accumulation! On the whole, with virtue, it is not the accumulation that is difficult, but the rectitude that is difficult. Yi Yin 伊尹 took upon himself the responsibility of being one of Heaven's awakened people, and thereby achieved the merit of saving the people—was this not a work of responding to Heaven? Yet he delighted in the Way of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, and would not carelessly give or take a single straw, because what he had accumulated was upright. As for those who loved antiquity like Yang Xiong 揚雄 [reading 知 as 如] or were broadly learned like Wang Tong 王通, what they accumulated was not unextensive; yet the men they served were not the right men, and the times in which they sought to sell their talents were not the right times—how could they accomplish anything great? Therefore, the gentleman prizes rectitude.

"Dui [reading 允 as 兌] is mid-autumn, that in which the myriad things rejoice."
By Wang Zao 王藻.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Liang 梁, comments: [The writing is clean and pure, and its depiction of the word "rejoice" (yue 說) is lucid, incisive, and worthy of savoring; it should be recorded as a model.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Mei 梅, comments: [Concise and apt.]

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授朱　批〔明切剰語取之〕
論兌爲收物之候而物由以遂焉夫天以秋收
萬物而兌其候也物之所由以說者不在是哉
大傳之意若謂氣機之出不能不入而其職必
有所司所謂說言乎兌者何哉蓋兌前爲坤雖
入乎秋而猶未離乎夏非正秋也兌後爲乾將
離乎秋而已入乎冬非正秋也唯兌爲正秋焉
位居西方正金氣用事之候時當始肅値少陰
利物之權萬物於此有不得其說者哉吾見仁
===
以顯而漸藏萬寶之告成者油然其寧謐誠以
通而漸復品彙之咸章者熙然其厭飫爲大爲
小雖若至賾也一理之所翕聚各欣欣焉而順
適非復昔之發舒而未斂者矣以形以色雖若
不齊也一氣之所凝結各怡怡焉而充足非復
昔之流形而未實者矣前之致養者至此而固
其機後之相薄者至此而歸其命信乎兌爲遂
物之府而爲帝之所乘以說者乎圖學之妙如
此㧞秋不可治以春治以春則華欲其說得耶
punctuated:
考試官教授朱　批：〔明切，剰語，取之。〕

論兌爲收物之候，而物由以遂焉。夫天以秋收萬物，而兌其候也，物之所由以說者，不在是哉？《大傳》之意，若謂：氣機之出不能不入，而其職必有所司。所謂「說言乎兌」者，何哉？蓋兌前爲坤，雖入乎秋而猶未離乎夏，非正秋也；兌後爲乾，將離乎秋而已入乎冬，非正秋也。唯兌爲正秋焉。位居西方，正金氣用事之候；時當始肅，値少陰利物之權，萬物於此，有不得其說者哉？吾見仁以顯而漸藏，萬寶之告成者，油然其寧謐；誠以通而漸復，品彙之咸章者，熙然其厭飫。爲大爲小，雖若至賾也，一理之所翕聚，各欣欣焉而順適，非復昔之發舒而未斂者矣；以形以色，雖若不齊也，一氣之所凝結，各怡怡焉而充足，非復昔之流形而未實者矣。前之致養者，至此而固其機；後之相薄者，至此而歸其命。信乎兌爲遂物之府，而爲帝之所乘以說者乎！圖學之妙如此。㧞秋不可治以春，治以春則華，欲其說，得耶？
translation_en:
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zhu comments: [Clear and incisive, with striking phrasing [?]; select it.]

This discusses how Dui (the Joyous, Lake) is the season for harvesting all things, and how things thereby achieve their fulfillment. Now, Heaven harvests the myriad things in autumn, and Dui is its season; is it not precisely in this that things find their joy (yue 說)? The meaning of the Great Commentary (Dazhuan 大傳) is as if to say: when the vital mechanism goes forth, it cannot but re-enter, and its function must have that which presides over it. What is meant by "they are joyous in Dui"? Before Dui is Kun (the Receptive, Earth), which, though having entered autumn, has not yet departed from summer, and thus is not mid-autumn. After Dui is Qian (the Creative, Heaven), which is about to depart from autumn and has already entered winter, and thus is not mid-autumn. Only Dui is true mid-autumn. Positioned in the west, it is precisely the season when the qi of metal is in command; the time corresponds to the beginning of austerity, coinciding with the authority of lesser yin (shaoyin 少陰) to benefit all things. At this point, could any of the myriad things fail to attain their joy? We see benevolence (ren 仁) having been manifest now gradually withdrawing into storage, and the myriad treasures that announce their completion are calmly at peace and tranquil; sincerity (cheng 誠) having penetrated through now gradually returning, and the manifold categories of beings that have all become resplendent are harmoniously satisfied and replete. Whether great or small, though they seem utmost in their complexity, as the one principle gathers them together, each is delighted and smoothly contented, no longer expanding without restraint as in the past. In form and in color, though they seem uneven, as the one qi condenses and solidifies them, each is cheerful and amply fulfilled, no longer flowing into shape without solidity as in the past. What previously brought about nourishment (Kun) reaches this point and consolidates its vital mechanism; what subsequently contends with one another (Qian) reaches this point and submits to its destiny. Truly, is not Dui the storehouse where things achieve fulfillment, and that upon which the Lord rides to bring joy? Such is the subtlety of the learning of the diagrams. Yet [?] autumn cannot be governed by the principles of spring; if governed as in spring, things will merely blossom—should one wish them to rejoice in fulfillment, how could that be attained?…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
一機感乎物有常說則五氣順布而化功成此
又聖人贊化而與天地參者也故說在兌而贊
之說者則在於聖人
書
帝曰來禹汝亦昌言禹拜曰都帝予何言
予思日孜孜
王忠顯
同考試官教諭周　批〔來禹都帝四字正是虞庭都俞氣象士子往往遺漏此作提掇明白且辭意精練宜錄以式〕
===
考試官學正梅　批〔保治之意發揮詳盡〕
考試官教授朱　批〔莊雅無一剩語〕
聖君求言於臣而大臣惟致意於行焉甚矣聖
世君臣之心無窮也君以忠言望臣臣以力行
自任保治之心其共切矣乎且夫天下之治每
成於上下之交儆而圖治之實必期於言行之
兼盡舜好問者也故曰來致其進也曰禹專其
責也乃命之曰忠益當集大衆思嘉猷不厭於
再聞臯陶之言昌矣予之所深嘉也然治道無
punctuated:
一機感乎物，有常說，則五氣順布而化功成。此又聖人贊化而與天地參者也。故說在兌，而贊之說者則在於聖人。

書
帝曰：「來，禹，汝亦昌言。」禹拜曰：「都！帝，予何言？予思日孜孜。」
王忠顯
同考試官教諭周　批〔「來禹」、「都帝」四字，正是虞庭都俞氣象，士子往往遺漏。此作提掇明白，且辭意精練，宜錄以式。〕
考試官學正梅　批〔保治之意，發揮詳盡。〕
考試官教授朱　批〔莊雅無一剩語。〕

聖君求言於臣，而大臣惟致意於行焉。甚矣，聖世君臣之心無窮也！君以忠言望臣，臣以力行自任，保治之心，其共切矣乎！且夫天下之治，每成於上下之交儆；而圖治之實，必期於言行之兼盡。舜好問者也，故曰「來」，致其進也；曰「禹」，專其責也。乃命之曰：忠益當集大衆思，嘉猷不厭於再聞。臯陶之言昌矣，予之所深嘉也。然治道無
translation_en:
…When this single vital mechanism moves things so that they possess enduring joy, then the five qi spread harmoniously and the work of transformation is completed. This, moreover, is how the sage assists in transformation and forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. Therefore, joy lies in the trigram Dui, while the one who assists them in rejoicing is the sage.

Book of Documents (Shu)
The Emperor said, "Come, Yu, you also make a splendid speech." Yu bowed and said, "Oh! Emperor, what can I say? I think only of being diligent day by day."
Wang Zhongxian
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhou comments: [The four words "Come, Yu" and "Oh! Emperor" capture the very spirit of harmonious deliberation at the court of Yu; candidates often overlook them. This essay highlights them clearly, and its diction and thought are refined and concise; it should be recorded as a model.]
Examiner Confucian School Director Mei comments: [The idea of preserving good governance is elaborated thoroughly.]
Examiner Instructor Zhu comments: [Dignified and elegant, without a single superfluous word.]

A sage ruler seeks words of counsel from his minister, while the great minister devotes his mind solely to action. Profound indeed is the boundless dedication in the minds of ruler and minister in a sage age! The ruler looks to his minister for loyal words, and the minister takes strenuous action as his own responsibility—how equally earnest are their minds in preserving good governance! Moreover, the governance of the world is always accomplished through mutual admonition between superior and inferior, and the reality of striving for order must aim at the full realization of both words and deeds. Shun was one who loved to question; therefore he said, "Come," inviting him to step forward, and said, "Yu," assigning the responsibility specifically to him. He then commanded him, saying: Loyal benefit ought to gather the thoughts of the great multitude, and one never tires of hearing fine counsels again. The words of Gao Yao were splendid indeed, and I deeply approve of them. Yet the way of governance is…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
盡或不止於知人則凡有資於贊襄者不可以
獨缺也亦或不止於安民則凡有可以啓沃者
不容以獨默也況寅恭之衷既協而謨弼之懷
素切汲其亦昌言矣乎是帝之求言若不及有
如此者禹拜昌言者也故曰都美其問也曰帝
誇其聽也乃承之曰進言者善不必出於已踐
言者行唯恐惰於終皐陶之謨至矣予更何所
言哉惟思治功以勤而成予之終日以圖之者
期天工之恒亮也亦以怠而隳予之畢力以効
===
之者欲天人之恒達也況爲治不在多言而臣
職惟先敬事予敢不日孜孜矣乎是禹之輔治
若不及有如此者吁君臣圖治而俱若不及此
有虞之治不可及也嗚呼納言明試知人也脩
和府事安民也禹豈終於無言哉乃惟以孜孜
爲思而皐陶亦曰朕言惠可底行蓋俱以力行
望之君也然其君之樂取猶未已焉斯其所以
稱明良與
三后協心同底于道道洽政治澤潤生民
punctuated:
盡，或不止於知人，則凡有資於贊襄者，不可以獨缺也；亦或不止於安民，則凡有可以啓沃者，不容以獨默也。況寅恭之衷既協，而謨弼之懷素切，汲其亦昌言矣乎！是帝之求言若不及，有如此者。禹拜昌言者也，故曰「都」，美其問也；曰「帝」，誇其聽也。乃承之曰：進言者，善不必出於已；踐言者，行唯恐惰於終。皐陶之謨至矣，予更何所言哉？惟思治功以勤而成，予之終日以圖之者，期天工之恒亮也；亦以怠而隳，予之畢力以効之者，欲天人之恒達也。況爲治不在多言，而臣職惟先敬事，予敢不日孜孜矣乎！是禹之輔治若不及，有如此者。吁！君臣圖治而俱若不及，此有虞之治不可及也。嗚呼！納言明試，知人也；脩和府事，安民也。禹豈終於無言哉？乃惟以孜孜爲思，而皐陶亦曰「朕言惠，可底行」，蓋俱以力行望之君也。然其君之樂取猶未已焉，斯其所以稱明良與！
三后協心，同底于道，道洽政治，澤潤生民，
translation_en:
… inexhaustible. Perhaps it does not stop at knowing men; then whatever contributes to assisting governance must not be left lacking by you alone. Or perhaps it does not stop at bringing peace to the people; then whatever can enlighten and enrich the sovereign's mind must not be kept in silence by you alone. How much more so since our reverent and respectful hearts are already in harmony, and your desire to counsel and assist has always been earnest—should you [Reading 汲 as 汝] not also offer splendid words?" Such was how the Emperor sought counsel as though he could never reach enough. Yu was one who bowed to splendid words. Therefore he said, "Oh!", praising his inquiry; and he said, "Emperor!", commending his readiness to listen [?]. He then replied to him, saying: "In offering words, goodness need not come from oneself; in putting words into practice, in action one only fears growing lax at the end. Gao Yao's counsels are supreme—what more have I to say? I only reflect that the achievements of governance are accomplished through diligence, and what I plan for all day long is to hope that Heaven's work will forever be assisted; and that they are ruined through indolence, so what I devote all my strength to is wishing that Heaven and man [or Heaven's appointees] will forever be in accord [?]. Moreover, governing does not lie in many words, and a minister's duty puts reverent attention to affairs first—how dare I not be diligent day after day?" Such was how Yu assisted in governance as though he could never reach enough. Ah! Sovereign and minister both planned for governance as though they could never do enough—this is why the governance of Yu [Shun] could never be equaled. Alas! Receiving words and clearly testing by merits is knowing men; cultivating and harmonizing the six treasuries and three affairs is bringing peace to the people. Did Yu really end up saying nothing at all? Yet he only took daily diligence as his thought, while Gao Yao also said, "My words are accordant with reason and can be carried into practice," for both of them looked to their sovereign for vigorous action. Yet their sovereign's delight in adopting the good of others still did not cease—is this not why they were celebrated as an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers!

"The three sovereigns united their hearts and together arrived at the Way; the Way permeated and governance was well-ordered, their bounty moistened the living people, …"

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
四夷左衽罔不咸賴
同考試官教諭周　批　張問官〔治化根本於心作者不浮則贅〕
〔此篇獨爲得肯〕
考試官學正梅　批〔構意精確檃詞簡潔〕
考試官教授朱　批〔沉著可佳〕
賢王於大臣期其同心以成治功焉夫澤生民
而綏四夷治功成矣然非三后之同心同道何
以致之康王所以期望於畢公也以爲人臣之
===
經治也以道而其行道也以心心之不一道因
之戾而治化不可成矣惟公之於二公也忠君
之貞得於不二而圖化之意妙於相孚始之中
之終之時不一也而化殷之心則百慮而一致
以故克慎克和克成事不同也而化殷之道則
殊途而同歸以是心也行是道也漸滋浸漬而
化理之流通浹如也以是道也出是政也振飭
脩舉而紀綱之敷布秩如也夫政善則民安舉
東郊之衆而沐浴於膏澤者將沛然其維新矣
punctuated:
四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。」

同考試官教諭周　批　張問官〔治化根本於心，作者不浮則贅，此篇獨爲得肯〕
考試官學正梅　批〔構意精確，檃詞簡潔〕
考試官教授朱　批〔沉著可佳〕

賢王於大臣，期其同心以成治功焉。夫澤生民而綏四夷，治功成矣；然非三后之同心同道，何以致之？康王所以期望於畢公也。以爲：人臣之經治也以道，而其行道也以心。心之不一，道因之戾，而治化不可成矣。惟公之於二公也，忠君之貞得於不二，而圖化之意妙於相孚。始之、中之、終之，時不一也，而化殷之心則百慮而一致；以故克慎、克和、克成，事不同也，而化殷之道則殊途而同歸。以是心也，行是道也，漸滋浸漬，而化理之流通浹如也；以是道也，出是政也，振飭脩舉，而紀綱之敷布秩如也。夫政善則民安，舉東郊之衆而沐浴於膏澤者，將沛然其維新矣，
translation_en:
… the four barbarian tribes with left-fastened lapels all without exception depend on them."

Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhou, comments on Zhang Wenguan 张问官: [Governance and transformation are rooted in the mind; other writers on this theme are either superficial or prolix, whereas this piece alone hits the mark.]
Examiner, Confucian School Director Mei, comments: [The conception of ideas is precise, and the crafted wording is concise.]
Examiner, Instructor Zhu, comments: [Steady and thorough—commendable.]

A worthy king expects his grand ministers to unite their minds so as to bring the achievements of governance to completion. Now, to enrich the living people with blessings and pacify the four barbarian tribes is the completion of the achievements of governance; yet without the three rulers uniting their minds and sharing the same Way, how could this be brought about? This is what King Kang expected of the Duke of Bi. He considered that a minister's ordering of governance is through the Way, and his practicing of the Way is through the mind. If their minds are not united, the Way becomes discordant as a result, and governance and transformation cannot be accomplished. Only in Your Grace's relation to the other two Dukes has the constancy of loyalty to the sovereign been attained through unswerving devotion, while the intention to plan for transformation is wondrously in mutual accord. Beginning it, continuing it in the middle, and completing it at the end—the times are not the same, yet the mind to transform Yin reaches a single conclusion through a hundred deliberations. Therefore, being able to be cautious, being able to harmonize, and being able to bring to completion—the tasks are different, yet the Way of transforming Yin reaches the same destination by different paths. With this mind, practicing this Way, through gradual nourishment and saturation, the flow of transformative principle becomes all-pervasive. With this Way, issuing this governance, through rousing order and cultivating administration, the spreading of the laws and institutions becomes perfectly orderly. Now, when governance is good, the people are at peace: all the multitude of the eastern outskirts who bathe in rich blessings will abundantly renew themselves—…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
矧多遜之徒耶內順則外嚴率左衽之夷而懷
服於德威者將帖然其求賴矣矧有夏之衆耶
是則內外咸謐而皆由於三后之協心如此公
可不旣厥心哉大抵大臣之輔理成化莫貴於
心之同也心同則事雖異而相成心異則事雖
同而相悖亦顧其愛君體國之念何如耳三后
相繼治殷時逾三紀矣寬嚴不同而致化維一
則周召之同時輔君者其心又可知也周家有
道之長胥此夫
===
詩
樂只君子殿天子之邦
劉敏寬
同考試官教諭葉　批〔認理精切措詞典確是深於詩〕
義者宜錄以式
考試官學正梅　批〔講殿邦意瑩徹傑作也〕
考試官教授朱　批〔詞暢而氣充〕
詩人美諸侯之德爲王國之所重焉夫德之有
係於人國也大矣諸侯具可樂之德而王國不
punctuated:
矧多遜之徒耶！內順則外嚴，率左衽之夷而懷服於德威者，將帖然其求賴矣，矧有夏之衆耶！是則內外咸謐，而皆由於三后之協心如此，公可不旣厥心哉？大抵大臣之輔理成化，莫貴於心之同也。心同則事雖異而相成，心異則事雖同而相悖，亦顧其愛君體國之念何如耳。三后相繼治殷，時逾三紀矣，寬嚴不同，而致化維一；則周、召之同時輔君者，其心又可知也。周家有道之長，胥此夫！

詩
「樂只君子，殿天子之邦。」
劉敏寬
同考試官教諭葉　批：〔認理精切，措詞典確，是深於《詩》〕義者，宜錄以式。
考試官學正梅　批：〔講「殿邦」意瑩徹，傑作也。〕
考試官教授朱　批：〔詞暢而氣充。〕

詩人美諸侯之德，爲王國之所重焉。夫德之有係於人國也大矣！諸侯具可樂之德，而王國不
translation_en:
How much more so the multitude of those who are compliant! When the interior is obedient, the exterior is held in awe; all the left-lapelled barbarians who cherish and submit to our virtue and majesty will submissively seek to rely upon us—how much more so the people of the Chinese states! Thus, both within and without all is tranquil, and all of this stems from the three governors uniting their minds in this manner; how could you, O Duke, not exhaust your heart in this? In general, when great ministers assist in governance and bring about transformation, nothing is more precious than unity of mind. When their minds are united, even though their affairs differ, they complement one another; when their minds differ, even though their affairs are the same, they run counter to one another. It simply depends on the nature of their devotion to loving their ruler and embodying the state's interests. The three governors successively governed Yin for a period exceeding three twelve-year cycles; though their leniency and strictness differed, the transformation they achieved was one and the same. From this, the minds of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, who assisted their ruler at the same time, can also be known. The long-enduring enlightened rule of the House of Zhou rested entirely upon this!

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
"Delightful are the princely men, who鎮 [stabilize/fortify] the state of the Son of Heaven."
By Liu Minkuan 劉敏寬.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Ye: 〔His grasp of principle is precise and incisive, and his diction is classical and exact; he is one deeply versed in the meaning of the Classic of Poetry,〕 and this ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Mei: 〔His explanation of the meaning of "fortifying the state" is pellucid; it is a masterpiece.〕
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu: 〔The phrasing is fluent and the vital breath is full.〕

The poet praises the virtue of the feudal lords as that which lends weight to the royal state. Now, the bearing that virtue has upon a state is great indeed! When the feudal lords possess delightful virtue, how could the royal state not…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
由之以取重哉今夫禮以覲君為大德以鎮國
為難脩禮秉德吾茲有取於來朝之君子矣蓋
其欽翼內蘊形而為祇愼之度者藹然粟而溫
也寅畏中涵煥而為齊遬之儀者肅乎恭而安
也誠哉可樂之君子矣而有不宜殿天子之邦
乎吾知冠裳一會而龍光咸在無忝王國之楨
帯幍一萃而屏翰畢集允矣百辟之憲出其敬
以脩文可以綏太平爲邦家之元氣若或培之
而使厚矣出其敬以講武可以勘禍亂爲國家
===
之神氣若或益之而使重矣仁賢聚而朝廷尊
王靈由之丕振國有君子而所以作臣民拱向
之誠者其在是乎賢智庸而統體肅國勢由之
增隆朝有重臣而所以懾遠人覬覦之私者端
在斯乎夫然則在鎬之飲莫非君子之貽而車
服之庸信乎心之不能自已矣吁周王歌此以
燕諸侯其得禮臣之道者乎抑論君臣相與非
徒嚴分之貴而相須之殷乃相成之為美有周
盛時魚藻美君須之也而規寓焉采菽答臣寵
punctuated: 由之以取重哉？今夫禮以覲君為大，德以鎮國為難。脩禮秉德，吾茲有取於來朝之君子矣。蓋其欽翼內蘊，形而為祇愼之度者，藹然粟而溫也；寅畏中涵，煥而為齊遬之儀者，肅乎恭而安也。誠哉可樂之君子矣，而有不宜殿天子之邦乎？吾知冠裳一會，而龍光咸在，無忝王國之楨；帯幍一萃，而屏翰畢集，允矣百辟之憲。出其敬以脩文，可以綏太平，爲邦家之元氣，若或培之而使厚矣；出其敬以講武，可以勘禍亂，爲國家之神氣，若或益之而使重矣。仁賢聚而朝廷尊，王靈由之丕振，國有君子，而所以作臣民拱向之誠者，其在是乎！賢智庸而統體肅，國勢由之增隆，朝有重臣，而所以懾遠人覬覦之私者，端在斯乎！夫然，則在鎬之飲，莫非君子之貽，而車服之庸，信乎心之不能自已矣。吁！周王歌此以燕諸侯，其得禮臣之道者乎？抑論君臣相與，非徒嚴分之貴，而相須之殷，乃相成之為美。有周盛時，《魚藻》美君，須之也，而規寓焉；《采菽》答臣，寵
translation_en:
… derive weight and standing from this? Now, in ritual, having an audience with the sovereign is the greatest matter; in virtue, stabilizing the state is the most difficult task. Cultivating ritual and upholding virtue—this is what I admire here in the noble men who have come to court. For their reverent care is stored within, and when it takes form as a respectful and cautious demeanor, it is genial—firm like grain yet warm; their awe and敬畏 are held inside, and when they shine forth as a庄重 and nimble deportment, it is solemn—courteous yet at ease. Truly they are noble men worthy of delight! And how could they not be fitting to镇守 the realm of the Son of Heaven?

I know that once caps and robes assemble, the royal favor and glory are everywhere present, bringing no shame to their role as pillars of the royal state; once sashes and headgear gather, the screens and bulwarks of the realm are all collected, truly serving as models for the hundred lords. When they bring forth their reverence to cultivate civil affairs, they can secure grand peace, and as the vital energy of the state and royal house, it is as though someone nourished it and made it thick; when they bring forth their reverence to practice military affairs, they can suppress calamity and rebellion, and as the spiritual energy of the state, it is as though someone augmented it and made it weighty. When the benevolent and worthy gather, the court is honored and the royal prestige is thereby greatly roused; when the state possesses noble men, does not the means to inspire the sincere allegiance of subjects and people lie right here? When the worthy and wise are employed, the governing body is solemn and the strength of the state is thereby increasingly exalted; when the court possesses weighty ministers, does not the means to overawe the selfish designs of distant peoples lie precisely in this?

This being so, the feasting at Hao was none other than the gift of these noble men, and the bestowal of carriages and robes in recognition of merit was truly something the king's heart could not help doing. Ah! When the King of Zhou sang this ode to feast the feudal lords, did he not grasp the Way of treating ministers with ritual? Moreover, if we discuss the relationship between sovereign and minister, it is not merely a matter of valuing strict distinctions of rank; rather, it is the earnestness of their mutual reliance and the beauty of their bringing each other to completion. In the flourishing age of the Zhou, the ode "Fish and Pondweed" (Yuzao) praised the sovereign, expressing reliance upon him while lodging admonition within; the ode "Gathering Beans" (Caishu) answered the ministers, showing favor…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之也而勸行焉明良遇而情意浹宛乎都俞吁
咈之遺響也噫此周治之所以稱隆也歟
武王靡不勝龍旂十乘大糦是承邦畿千
里維民所止肇域彼四海
張楠
同考試官教諭王　批〔高宗中興之盛重在武德是篇〕
獨得題旨取之不但以其文也
考試官學正梅　批〔精透可嘉〕
考試官教授朱　批〔純正無疵宜冠多士〕
===
詩人頌賢王繼夫先德而因以統夫大業焉夫
有土有人王業之大一統也自非有繼先之德
而何以能兼覆其盛如此哉此高宗之所以可
頌也且帝王之中興也必有繼先之德而後有
光前之業我祖成湯固以武德王天下矣其在
武丁何如哉但見其總乾剛以獨斷而英聲之
赫赫者質之於勇智而有光復舊物於維新而
威靈之濯濯者考之於聖武而無愧其在百辟
仰精明之治焉而順治之武此其克纘之矣其
punctuated:
之也，而勸行焉。明良遇而情意浹，宛乎都俞吁咈之遺響也。噫！此周治之所以稱隆也歟！

「武王靡不勝。龍旂十乘，大糦是承。邦畿千里，維民所止，肇域彼四海。」
張楠
同考試官教諭王　批：〔高宗中興之盛，重在武德。是篇〕獨得題旨，取之不但以其文也。
考試官學正梅　批：〔精透可嘉。〕
考試官教授朱　批：〔純正無疵，宜冠多士。〕

詩人頌賢王繼夫先德，而因以統夫大業焉。夫有土有人，王業之大一統也。自非有繼先之德，而何以能兼覆其盛如此哉？此高宗之所以可頌也。且帝王之中興也，必有繼先之德，而後有光前之業。我祖成湯，固以武德王天下矣；其在武丁，何如哉？但見其總乾剛以獨斷，而英聲之赫赫者，質之於勇智而有光；復舊物於維新，而威靈之濯濯者，考之於聖武而無愧。其在百辟，仰精明之治焉，而順治之武，此其克纘之矣；其
translation_en:
… them, yet encouragement operates therein. When an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet and their feelings and intentions are in full harmony, it is just like the lingering echoes of the approving and admonishing exchanges of antiquity! Ah! Is this not why the governance of Zhou is celebrated as so flourishing?

"The Martial King was equal to every demand. With ten chariots bearing dragon-blazoned banners, the great sacrificial millet is presented. The royal domain of a thousand li is where the people rest; and he opens up the borders to the four seas." [Book of Odes, "Xuan Niao" 玄鳥]
By Zhang Nan 張楠
