Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: 〔The flourishing of Gaozong's 高宗 dynastic restoration lay chiefly in his martial virtue. This essay〕 uniquely grasps the purport of the theme; I have selected it not merely for its literary style.
Examiner and Director of Studies Mei 梅 comments: 〔Incisive and thorough; worthy of praise.〕
Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: 〔Pure, orthodox, and flawless; fitting to stand at the head of the many scholars.〕

The poet praises the worthy king for continuing the virtue of his ancestor, and thereby unifying the great enterprise. Now, possessing both territory and people constitutes the grand unification of the royal enterprise. Had he not possessed the virtue to continue the work of his ancestors, how could he have embraced and sheltered such flourishing abundance as this? This is why Gaozong is worthy of praise. Moreover, when an emperor or king achieves a dynastic restoration, he must first possess the virtue that continues his ancestors' legacy before he can achieve an enterprise that glorifies his predecessors. Our ancestor Cheng Tang 成湯 indeed ruled the world as true king through his martial virtue; how was it, then, with Wu Ding 武丁? One sees only that he wielded heaven-like firmness to make resolute decisions alone, so that his illustrious renown, shining brightly, added luster when measured against the courage and wisdom [of Tang]; he restored the old patrimony in a grand renewal, so that his awe-inspiring prestige, gleaming brilliantly, occasioned no shame when examined alongside the sacred martiality [of his ancestor]. Among the hundred lords, all looked up to his discerning and clear governance, and thus the martial virtue that brings compliant order—this he was able to carry on! Among …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
在四夷仰㨗伐之烈焉而威嚴之武此其克承
之矣故蔦邦之諸侯湯所貽之臣辟也茲惟有
武德以聯屬之莫不飾車旂以就道奉大糦以
駿奔合萬國而祀先王不依然方命厥后之舊
乎率土之輿圖湯所貽之封域也茲維有武德
以撫綏之是以邦畿雖限於千里提封則盡於
海隅潏中國而統萬方不宛然奄有九有之日
乎是知武湯作之武丁述之一德相承均之有
商之令王也其敢忘所自哉抑高宗學於甘盤
===
任用良弼君臣師友之間麴蘖交脩終始典學
故中興之盛光昭千古蓋力學任賢之明驗也
然則德配武湯誠有不專於武者矣
春秋
春王正月城楚丘〔僖公二年〕
何東鳳
同考試官教諭唐 批〔責桓公專封之罪詞嚴義正讀之凜凜〕
考試官學正梅 批〔不逞浮詞而理趣悠然〕
punctuated:
在四夷，仰㨗伐之烈焉，而威嚴之武，此其克承之矣。故蔦邦之諸侯，湯所貽之臣辟也；茲惟有武德以聯屬之，莫不飾車旂以就道，奉大糦以駿奔，合萬國而祀先王，不依然方命厥后之舊乎？率土之輿圖，湯所貽之封域也；茲維有武德以撫綏之，是以邦畿雖限於千里，提封則盡於海隅，潏中國而統萬方，不宛然奄有九有之日乎？是知武湯作之，武丁述之，一德相承，均之有商之令王也，其敢忘所自哉？抑高宗學於甘盤，任用良弼，君臣師友之間，麴蘖交脩，終始典學，故中興之盛，光昭千古，蓋力學任賢之明驗也。然則德配武湯，誠有不專於武者矣。

《春秋》
春王正月，城楚丘。〔僖公二年〕
何東鳳
同考試官教諭唐批：〔責桓公專封之罪，詞嚴義正，讀之凜凜。〕
考試官學正梅批：〔不逞浮詞，而理趣悠然。〕
translation_en:
… among the tribes of the four quarters, they looked up to the brilliance of his swift punitive campaigns, and thus he was able to inherit that awe-inspiring martial valor. Therefore, the feudal lords of the myriad states [?] were the vassal rulers bequeathed by Tang. Now, solely because he possessed martial virtue to bind and unite them, there were none who did not adorn their chariots and banners to take to the road, presenting the great sacrificial millet and hastening swiftly to join the myriad states in sacrificing to the former kings—was this not still just as in the old days when instructions were given to the local rulers in all directions? The territory within the shores of the whole land was the domain bequeathed by Tang. Now, solely because he possessed martial virtue to pacify and soothe it, although the royal domain was limited to a thousand li, the total territory extended to the corners of the seas; surging through [?] the Central States and governing the myriad regions, was this not vivid as the days when Tang possessed the Nine Provinces? From this we know that Martial Tang initiated it and Wu Ding continued it; succeeding one another in pure virtue, both alike were exemplary kings of the Shang dynasty. How could they dare forget whence this came? Moreover, Gaozong studied under Gan Pan and employed a worthy assistant; between ruler and minister, teacher and friend, they acted as leaven and malt in mutual cultivation, constantly devoted to learning from beginning to end. Thus the flourishing of his dynastic revival shone brightly through a thousand ages, which was indeed the clear proof of his diligent learning and employment of the worthy. This being so, his matching the virtue of Martial Tang truly did not lie solely in martial prowess!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In spring, in the King's first month, they walled Chuqiu." 〔Second year of Duke Xi〕
He Dongfeng 何東鳳
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 唐: 〔It censures Duke Huan's crime of arbitrarily enfeoffing a state; the diction is stern and the principle upright—reading it inspires awe.〕
Comment by Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Mei 梅: 〔It does not indulge in superficial verbiage, yet its reasoned meaning flows deeply and naturally.〕

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授朱　批
意精而詞更警拔
春秋略霸主封國之功所以正王法也此見楚
丘之城王法之干也宜春秋略之而不序與昔
狄患迫而載馳賦桓也憂之楚丘所爲城也經
宜美其功者何爲而反微之耶蓋聞興滅繼絶
天王之大權也彼野處之衛非自遷之邢矣桓
能請命而後城則赫赫義舉不出夷儀之上乎
奈之何王命未將王臣未行一旦樹之君立之
國焉甲士乘馬齊可戍諸侯可從而號令不宜
===
自齊發也祭服重錦齊可歸衛可受而無虧不
宜自齊遣也外却狄人之勢功非不崇矣而君
令臣共之道未之聞焉君子謂是舉也功之首
罪之魁也功固不足論也內存康叔之裔利非
不溥矣而作威作福之義未之明焉君子謂是
舉也知有衛不知有周也利固不足紀也噫詩
稱朔方之城則曰天子命我稱東方之城則曰
王命仲山甫未聞無王命而擅自城者桓之罪
可勝言哉經故微而不序蓋曰寧可無一時之
punctuated:
考試官教授朱　批：
意精而詞更警拔。

春秋略霸主封國之功，所以正王法也。此見楚丘之城，王法之干也，宜春秋略之而不序與！昔狄患迫而載馳賦，桓也憂之，楚丘所爲城也。經宜美其功者，何爲而反微之耶？蓋聞興滅繼絶，天王之大權也。彼野處之衛，非自遷之邢矣。桓能請命而後城，則赫赫義舉，不出夷儀之上乎？奈之何王命未將，王臣未行，一旦樹之君，立之國焉？甲士乘馬，齊可戍，諸侯可從，而號令不宜自齊發也；祭服重錦，齊可歸，衛可受，而無虧不宜自齊遣也。外却狄人之勢，功非不崇矣，而君令臣共之道，未之聞焉。君子謂是舉也，功之首，罪之魁也，功固不足論也。內存康叔之裔，利非不溥矣，而作威作福之義，未之明焉。君子謂是舉也，知有衛，不知有周也，利固不足紀也。噫！詩稱朔方之城，則曰：「天子命我。」稱東方之城，則曰：「王命仲山甫。」未聞無王命而擅自城者。桓之罪，可勝言哉？經故微而不序，蓋曰：「寧可無一時之
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Professor:
The conception is refined, and the language still more striking and distinguished.

The Spring and Autumn Annals passes over the hegemon’s achievement in establishing a state in order to uphold royal law. Here we see that the fortification of Chuqiu infringed royal law. Surely it was fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should pass over his role without recording it! Formerly, when the threat from the Di pressed hard and “Galloping” was composed, Duke Huan was troubled by it; this was why Chuqiu was fortified. The Classic might be expected to praise his achievement: why, instead, does it obscure it? We have heard that restoring extinguished states and perpetuating severed lines of succession are great prerogatives of the king. Wei, whose people were living in the open country, was unlike Xing, which had relocated on its own. Had Duke Huan requested the royal command before fortifying the city, would this illustrious act of righteousness not have surpassed the fortification of Yiyi? How could he, before a royal command had been conveyed or a royal minister had set out, suddenly install a ruler for them and establish their state? As for armored soldiers and teams of horses, Qi could provide a garrison and the regional lords could join it, but the orders should not have issued from Qi. As for sacrificial robes and rich brocades, Qi could present them and Wei could accept them, but Wukui should not have been dispatched on Qi’s own authority.

In repelling the force of the Di from without, his achievement was certainly great; yet nothing was heard of the proper relationship in which the ruler commands and the subject obeys. The gentleman says of this undertaking: foremost in achievement, foremost also in guilt. Its achievement is therefore not worth discussing. In preserving the descendants of Kang Shu within, its benefits were certainly extensive; yet the principle governing the exercise of punishment and favor was not made clear. The gentleman says of this undertaking: he recognized Wei but did not recognize Zhou. Its benefits are therefore not worth recording.

Alas! When the Book of Odes speaks of fortifying Shuofang, it says, “The Son of Heaven commanded us.” When it speaks of fortifying the eastern city, it says, “The king commanded Zhong Shanfu.” Never have we heard of anyone presuming to fortify a city without a royal command. Could Duke Huan’s guilt ever be fully expressed? The Classic therefore obscures his role and does not record it, as if to say: “Better to forgo the transient …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
小惠而不可無萬世之王法也抑是狄也往歲
入邢今茲入衛不無事矣桓公主霸果何所爲
哉使能先事而備則衛可以不滅而楚丘可以
不城矣桓卒不然是養亂以爲功也春秋誅意
豈直不序之而已哉
晉趙盾帥師救陳宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯
會晉師于棐林伐鄭〔俱宣公元年〕
曹署篆
同考試官教諭梁　批〔春秋無義戰晉帥救陳伐鄭此〕
===
〔義舉也通篇發揮透徹得聖人與之之意〕
考試官學正梅　批〔純正可誦〕
考試官教授朱　批〔邃於理而暢於詞〕
霸國得恤患討罪之義春秋兩予之焉此陳之
救鄭之伐咸霸義之所當舉者也春秋予之也
固宜且夫兵非聖王之所尚而恤患討罪則義
之不可已者晉人救陳伐鄭之役有取焉
何言乎救陳也陳以先代之後而鄭附楚以侵
之不義甚矣晉視陳固同室之災也豈容以坐
punctuated:
小惠，而不可無萬世之王法也。抑是狄也，往歲入邢，今茲入衛，不無事矣，桓公主霸，果何所爲哉？使能先事而備，則衛可以不滅，而楚丘可以不城矣。桓卒不然，是養亂以爲功也。《春秋》誅意，豈直不序之而已哉？

「晉趙盾帥師救陳。宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭。」〔俱宣公元年〕
曹署篆
同考試官教諭梁　批：〔《春秋》無義戰，晉帥救陳伐鄭，此義舉也。通篇發揮透徹，得聖人與之之意。〕
考試官學正梅　批：〔純正可誦。〕
考試官教授朱　批：〔邃於理而暢於詞。〕

霸國得恤患討罪之義，《春秋》兩予之焉。此陳之救、鄭之伐，咸霸義之所當舉者也。《春秋》予之也，固宜。且夫兵非聖王之所尚，而恤患討罪，則義之不可已者。晉人救陳、伐鄭之役，有取焉。何言乎救陳也？陳以先代之後，而鄭附楚以侵之，不義甚矣。晉視陳，固同室之災也，豈容以坐…
translation_en:
…petty favor of the moment, yet we cannot be without the royal law for ten thousand generations. Moreover, as for these Di tribes: in a past year they invaded Xing, and now they have invaded Wei—they were certainly not inactive! With Duke Huan presiding as hegemon, what indeed was he doing? Had he been able to make preparations before the fact, Wei need not have been destroyed, and Chuqiu need not have been walled. That Huan ultimately failed to do so means he fostered disorder so as to turn it into his own merit. Since the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) condemns the underlying motive, how could it merely stop at not listing the participants by name?

"Zhao Dun of Jin led a force to rescue Chen. The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met the Jin force at Feilin and attacked Zheng." [Both from the first year of Duke Xuan.]
By Cao Shuzhuan 曹署篆.
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Liang comments: [In the Spring and Autumn Annals there are no righteous wars, yet the Jin commander's rescuing Chen and attacking Zheng was a righteous undertaking. The entire essay expounds this thoroughly and grasps the Sage's intention in commending it.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Mei comments: [Pure, correct, and worthy of recitation.]
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies (jiaoshou) Zhu comments: [Profound in principle and fluent in expression.]

When a hegemonic state upheld the righteousness of relieving distress and punishing crime, the Spring and Autumn Annals commended it on both counts. Here, the rescue of Chen and the attack on Zheng were both undertakings that hegemonic righteousness ought to have carried out. That the Spring and Autumn Annals commended them is indeed fitting.

Moreover, military force is not what the sage-kings esteemed; yet relieving distress and punishing crime are duties of righteousness that cannot be dispensed with. In the campaigns of the men of Jin to rescue Chen and attack Zheng, there is something worthy of approval. Why speak of "rescuing Chen"? Chen was the descendant of a former dynasty, yet Zheng attached itself to Chu in order to invade it—this was the extreme of unrighteousness. Jin viewed Chen's plight as truly a calamity within the same household; how could it bear to sit idly by and…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
視乎於是授鉞趙盾振旅前驅俾鄭不得附夷
以滋北國之虐者是救之力也噫狼淵縱敵晉
不在諸侯久矣而孰意今日有此舉也故特書
曰救豈非重其恤患之義乎何言乎伐鄭也楚
以猾夏之夷而鄭甘心附之不義甚矣晉視鄭
固門庭之寇也豈容以長亂乎於是會師列國
戮力徂征俾鄭不得弃夏以深南顧之憂者是
伐之力也噫翬朔行成晉不能服鄭久矣而孰
意今日有此舉也故特書曰伐豈非嘉其討罪
之義乎夫觀救者爲義則侵之者之罪益著觀
伐者爲義則見伐者之罪益明聖人於夷夏之
際嚴矣哉抑晉亦非無罪也當時宋鮑之逆不
能討而入之賂又列之會顧乃示恩于陳示威
于鄭是猶失肩背而養一指也卒使楚莊竊霸
中國莫敢誰何其何詞以自解乎然則救陳伐
鄭之役亦姑取節焉爾矣
===
禮記
紀綱既正天下大定天下大定然後正六
punctuated:
視乎？於是授鉞趙盾，振旅前驅，俾鄭不得附夷以滋北國之虐者，是救之力也。噫！狼淵縱敵，晉不在諸侯久矣，而孰意今日有此舉也？故特書曰「救」，豈非重其恤患之義乎？何言乎伐鄭也？楚以猾夏之夷，而鄭甘心附之，不義甚矣。晉視鄭，固門庭之寇也，豈容以長亂乎？於是會師列國，戮力徂征，俾鄭不得弃夏以深南顧之憂者，是伐之力也。噫！翬、朔行成，晉不能服鄭久矣，而孰意今日有此舉也？故特書曰「伐」，豈非嘉其討罪之義乎？夫觀救者爲義，則侵之者之罪益著；觀伐者爲義，則見伐者之罪益明。聖人於夷夏之際嚴矣哉！抑晉亦非無罪也。當時宋鮑之逆不能討，而入之賂，又列之會，顧乃示恩于陳，示威于鄭，是猶失肩背而養一指也。卒使楚莊竊霸，中國莫敢誰何，其何詞以自解乎？然則救陳伐鄭之役，亦姑取節焉爾矣。

禮記
紀綱既正，天下大定；天下大定，然後正六
translation_en:
… watch idly? Thus Jin conferred the battle-axe of command upon Zhao Dun 趙盾, marshaled its troops, and marched forth in the vanguard. That Zheng was prevented from aligning with the barbarians to worsen the cruelties inflicted upon the northern states was due to the strength of this rescue. Alas! Ever since letting the enemy go at Langyuan 狼淵, Jin had long failed to concern itself with the feudal lords—who would have expected it to undertake such an action today? Therefore the *Spring and Autumn Annals* (Chunqiu) specially records it as a "rescue"—is this not because it valued the righteousness of relieving distress?

And why does it speak of "attacking Zheng"? Chu was a barbarian state disturbing the Chinese lands (Xia 夏), yet Zheng willingly attached itself to Chu; this was the height of unrighteousness. To Jin, Zheng was truly a bandit at its own courtyard gate; how could Jin allow it to prolong disorder? Thus Jin assembled the armies of the various states and joined forces to march on a punitive expedition. That Zheng was prevented from abandoning the Chinese states and deepening the anxieties of looking southward was due to the strength of this attack. Alas! Ever since Gongzi Hui 公子翬 and赵朔 Zhao Shuo [趙穿 Zhao Chuan?] negotiated peace, Jin had long been unable to subdue Zheng—who would have expected it to undertake such an action today? Therefore the *Annals* specially records it as an "attack"—is this not because it praised the righteousness of punishing guilt?

When we see that the rescuer acted righteously, the guilt of the invader becomes all the more evident; when we see that the attacker acted righteously, the guilt of the one attacked becomes all the clearer. How strict the Sage was regarding the distinction between barbarian and Chinese!

Yet Jin, too, was not without fault. At that time, it was unable to punish the regicidal rebellion of Bao of Song 宋鮑 (Duke Wen of Song); instead, it accepted his bribes and even included him in interstate assemblies. Yet it turned around to display benevolence toward Chen and project military might against Zheng—this was like neglecting one's shoulders and back while tending to a single finger. In the end, it allowed King Zhuang of Chu 楚莊王 to usurp hegemony while the Central States dared not challenge him; with what words could Jin excuse itself? That being so, in the campaign to rescue Chen and attack Zheng, the Sage merely commended a single redeeming point!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"When the guiding principles and minor regulations were set right, the realm under heaven was greatly settled; after the realm under heaven was greatly settled, he then rectified the six …"

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
律和五聲弦歌詩頌
景　明
同考試官教諭葉　批〔筆力高古思致精邃而明瑩沖雅尤非淺學可及〕
考試官學正梅　批〔說理之文旨趣自別〕
考試官教授朱　批〔意味雋永〕
賢者論禮序而樂和以明古樂之由興也夫聲
音之道與政通也治定而樂作焉古樂之所由
來者遠矣于夏語魏文侯蓋曰樂與音不同觀
===
於古而樂其可知已昔聖人於大當之世固嘗
立紀綱以維天下矣誠使人紀肇脩而典常不
紊則道德一者風俗之自同宏綱具飭而彝則
克敦則軌物彰者名分之自定以恩合者定於
家恰然有恩以相愛也以義合者定於國燦然
有禮以相接也夫天下大定如此則太和在宇
宙間矣樂其可以不作耶夫然後以六律正
無以和聲也則酌元氣以定其損益之宜以五
聲弗和無以協律也則稽中數以諧其清濁之
punctuated:
律，和五聲，弦歌詩頌。
景明
同考試官教諭葉批：〔筆力高古，思致精邃，而明瑩沖雅，尤非淺學可及。〕
考試官學正梅批：〔說理之文，旨趣自別。〕
考試官教授朱批：〔意味雋永。〕
賢者論禮序而樂和，以明古樂之由興也。夫聲音之道，與政通也。治定而樂作焉，古樂之所由來者遠矣。于夏語魏文侯，蓋曰：樂與音不同，觀於古而樂其可知已。昔聖人於大當之世，固嘗立紀綱以維天下矣。誠使人紀肇脩而典常不紊，則道德一者，風俗之自同；宏綱具飭而彝則克敦，則軌物彰者，名分之自定。以恩合者定於家，恰然有恩以相愛也；以義合者定於國，燦然有禮以相接也。夫天下大定如此，則太和在宇宙間矣，樂其可以不作耶？夫然後以六律正，無以和聲也，則酌元氣以定其損益之宜；以五聲弗和，無以協律也，則稽中數以諧其清濁之
translation_en:
… pitches, harmonized the five notes, and accompanied the singing of the Odes and Hymns with stringed instruments."

Jing Ming 景明

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Ye 葉 comments: [The brushwork is lofty and archaic, the train of thought is subtle and profound, and its lucid, tranquil elegance is especially beyond the reach of shallow scholarship.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Mei 梅 comments: [In an essay that expounds upon principle, the purport and flair are naturally distinct.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu 朱 comments: [The flavor and meaning are rich and enduring.]

The worthy discusses how rites bring order and music brings harmony, so as to elucidate how ancient music arose. Now, the way of sounds and tones is bound up with governance. When order is settled, music is created; the origins of ancient music reach back far indeed. When Zixia 子夏 [transcribed 于夏] spoke to Marquis Wen of Wei 魏文侯, he said in effect: Music and mere tone are not the same; if one observes antiquity, music can be understood.

In the past, the sages in an age of great order and fitness certainly established fundamental principles and overarching norms to hold the world together. Truly, if human relationships are first cultivated and the constant canons are not thrown into confusion, then where morality is unified, customs will naturally become uniform; if the great overarching norms are fully put in order and the invariable rules are earnestly upheld, then where standards and emblems are manifest, statuses and duties will naturally be settled. Those united by affection are settled within the family, harmoniously possessing affection with which to love one another; those united by righteousness are settled within the state, brilliantly possessing rites with which to treat one another. Now, when the world is greatly settled like this, supreme harmony resides throughout the universe—how then could music not be created?

Only then, considering that if the six standard pitches are not rectified [? text has 正 without 弗], there is no means to harmonize the notes, one draws upon the primordial vitality to determine the proper measure of their shortening and lengthening; considering that if the five notes are not harmonized, there is no means to bring them into accord with the standard pitches, one examines the central numbers to harmonize the…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
節由是弦以琴瑟渢渢其和鳴也在治之無聲
者不於此宣其蘊乎由是歌以詩頌洋洋其盈
耳也至禮之不讓者不於此洩其精乎夫樂以
治定而作治以禮序而成古樂之隆如此彼溺
音烏足以擬之抑治者德之施也樂者德之華
也德苟至矣則君臣父子之間非禮弗履而身
度聲律咸英韶濩可繼響矣不然制作雖煩祇
爲粉飾之具已耳其如禮樂何哉故曰不閒性
與天道而能制禮作樂者未矣
===
其在朝廷則道仁聖禮義之序燕處則聽
雅頌之音行步則有環佩之聲升車則
有鸞和之音居處有禮進退有度百官
得其宜萬事得其序
王立賢
同考試官教諭王　批〔體格莊重詞語簡暢場中如此〕
作者絕少錄之
考試官學正梅　批〔雄渾警拔〕
考試官教授朱　批〔有力量有識見〕
punctuated:
節。由是弦以琴瑟，渢渢其和鳴也，在治之無聲者，不於此宣其蘊乎？由是歌以詩頌，洋洋其盈耳也，至禮之不讓者，不於此洩其精乎？夫樂以治定而作，治以禮序而成，古樂之隆如此，彼溺音烏足以擬之！抑治者，德之施也；樂者，德之華也。德苟至矣，則君臣父子之間，非禮弗履，而身度聲律，《咸》、《英》、《韶》、《濩》可繼響矣。不然，制作雖煩，祇爲粉飾之具已耳，其如禮樂何哉？故曰：不閒性與天道，而能制禮作樂者，未矣。
其在朝廷，則道仁聖禮義之序；燕處，則聽雅頌之音；行步，則有環佩之聲；升車，則有鸞和之音。居處有禮，進退有度，百官得其宜，萬事得其序。
王立賢
同考試官教諭王　批：〔體格莊重，詞語簡暢，場中如此〕作者絕少，錄之。
考試官學正梅　批：〔雄渾警拔。〕
考試官教授朱　批：〔有力量，有識見。〕
translation_en:
… cadences. Thereupon, when stringed on the qin and se zithers, how surging and harmonious is their sounding! Is not the soundless essence of orderly rule hereby expressing its inner store? Thereupon, when sung in odes and hymns, how vast and brimming they fill the ears! Is not the unyielding essence of supreme ritual hereby releasing its quintessence? Now, music is created when governance is settled, and governance is completed when ritual is ordered. Such was the flourishing of ancient music—how could those decadent airs ever be worthy of comparison with it? Moreover, governance is the application of virtue, and music is the efflorescence of virtue. If virtue has truly reached the utmost, then between ruler and minister, father and son, nothing contrary to ritual is trodden; when one's person serves as the measure and one's voice as the pitch-standard, the echoes of the Xian, Ying, Shao, and Hu music can be carried on. Otherwise, though institutions and compositions be elaborate, they are merely tools for superficial adornment—what can they do for ritual and music? Therefore it is said: without being conversant [?] with human nature and the Way of Heaven, no one has ever been able to institute ritual and create music.

"When he is in the court, he speaks of the order of benevolence, sageliness, ritual propriety, and righteousness; when taking his ease in private, he listens to the music of the Odes and Hymns; when walking, there is the sound of his girdle pendants; when mounting his carriage, there is the sound of the luan and he bells. In his dwelling and resting there is ritual propriety; in his advancing and retiring there is measure; the hundred officials obtain their proper places, and the myriad affairs obtain their proper order."

Wang Lixian 王立賢
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: 〔Its style and structure are dignified, and its diction is concise and fluent; in the examination hall, such〕 authors are exceedingly rare. Record it.
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Mei 梅 comments: 〔Vigorous, profound, and incisively outstanding.〕
Examiner and Prefectural Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: 〔Possesses strength and insight.〕

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖君純於所養而其治成矣蓋君身萬化之原
也養純而治成焉其機固如此哉且王者以一
身而臨御天下所以任使羣臣總理萬幾厥係
重矣德盛而養之弗純可乎故以朝廷爲四方
之極而仁聖禮義之序極之所以建也則於是
而道之奉至德以周旋循其當然之則也述天
理以時措順其自然之宜也猶未也於燕處則
雅頌歌焉於行步則環佩鳴焉於升車則鸞和
節焉致樂以治心所以養和平之藴者至矣於
===
居處必以禮焉於進退必以度焉致禮以治躬
所以履中正之矩者嚴矣夫如是而治之成也
不裕如哉吾見百官者儀刑於天子者也君身
正則莫不承式焉大臣法也小臣廉也惟所用
而皆賢矣萬事者統理於天子者也君德成則
莫不順治焉大綱舉也萬目張也惟所施而皆
當矣是知隨在致養天德豫也官宜事序王道
行也盛德大業至矣哉雖然要不外於一敬也
蓋溫恭具而後重華協聖敬躋而後昭假至古
punctuated: 聖君純於所養，而其治成矣。蓋君身，萬化之原也。養純而治成焉，其機固如此哉！且王者以一身而臨御天下，所以任使羣臣、總理萬幾，厥係重矣，德盛而養之弗純，可乎？故以朝廷爲四方之極，而仁、聖、禮、義之序，極之所以建也。則於是而道之：奉至德以周旋，循其當然之則也；述天理以時措，順其自然之宜也。猶未也，於燕處則雅頌歌焉，於行步則環佩鳴焉，於升車則鸞和節焉，致樂以治心，所以養和平之藴者至矣；於居處必以禮焉，於進退必以度焉，致禮以治躬，所以履中正之矩者嚴矣。夫如是，而治之成也，不裕如哉？吾見百官者，儀刑於天子者也，君身正則莫不承式焉，大臣法也，小臣廉也，惟所用而皆賢矣；萬事者，統理於天子者也，君德成則莫不順治焉，大綱舉也，萬目張也，惟所施而皆當矣。是知隨在致養，天德豫也；官宜事序，王道行也。盛德大業，至矣哉！雖然，要不外於一敬也。蓋溫恭具而後重華協，聖敬躋而後昭假至，古
translation_en: When the sage ruler is pure in his self-cultivation, his governance is brought to completion. For the ruler's own person is the source of all transformations. When his cultivation is pure, governance is achieved—such indeed is the pivotal mechanism! Moreover, the true king presides over the empire in his single person; the way he employs the multitude of officials and oversees the myriad affairs of state carries the utmost weight. Even if his virtue is abundant, how could it be acceptable if his cultivation is not pure? Therefore, taking the court as the standard for the four quarters, it is through the order of benevolence, sageliness, ritual propriety, and righteousness that this standard is established. Thereupon he guides himself by them: upholding supreme virtue in all his conduct, he follows the rules of what ought to be; transmitting heavenly principle in timely application, he accords with the fitness of what is natural. Yet even this is not all. In moments of leisure, the Odes and Hymns (Ya and Song) are sung; when walking, his jade pendants chime; when mounting his carriage, the luan and he bells keep the rhythm. Perfecting music to govern his mind, the way he nurtures the store of harmony and peace is utmost. In his dwelling, he invariably abides by ritual propriety; in advancing and withdrawing, he invariably conforms to measure. Perfecting ritual to govern his person, the way he treads the square of centrality and rectitude is strict. Being thus, is not the completion of governance achieved with effortless abundance? We see that the hundred officials take the Son of Heaven as their model; when the ruler's person is rectified, none fail to follow his pattern—the great ministers abide by the law, the lesser officials maintain integrity, and whomever he employs are all worthy. The myriad affairs are overseen and ordered by the Son of Heaven; when the ruler's virtue is perfected, nothing fails to be smoothly governed—the great guiding cord is lifted, the ten thousand meshes open wide, and whatever measures he implements are all fitting. Thus we know that devoting oneself to cultivation in every situation is the preparedness of heavenly virtue, and that officials finding their proper place and affairs their proper order is the practice of the kingly way. Splendid virtue and great enterprise—how supreme they are! Even so, in essence it goes no further than a single word: reverence. For only when gentle reverence was complete did Double Splendor (Chonghua, i.e., Shun) harmonize with the ruler; only when sagely reverence ascended daily did bright reach (zhaoge) arrive. In antiquity, …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之聖帝明王率由此道而風動之休允殖之化
胥此焉出也說者謂敬爲聖學始終之要信哉
第貳場
論
天下文章
王忠顯
同考試官教諭周　批〔體格明整詞華雅暢而通篇歸〕
重於誠有本之論
考試官學正梅　批〔意義完足〕
===
考試官教授朱　批〔雅當足式〕
大臣以至誠之道事其君故不自用其文而文
自顯於天下夫文何也生乎質者也質主於誠
者也天下夫質之俚故因以文之而彼大臣
者固將以文而潤色天下者也乃或日斤斤焉
求所謂文假先王之道以緣飾之苟可以收名
不必於獲實將必闊略其事爲靡靡無當而所
以經方致遠甄物成化之義舉廢缺焉卽黻黼
之飾麗藻之工也其何以章軌物樹鴻績哉故
punctuated:
之聖帝明王率由此道，而風動之休、允殖之化，胥此焉出也。說者謂敬爲聖學始終之要，信哉！

第貳場
論
《天下文章》
王忠顯
同考試官教諭周　批：〔體格明整，詞華雅暢，而通篇歸〕重於誠，有本之論。
考試官學正梅　批：〔意義完足。〕
考試官教授朱　批：〔雅當足式。〕

大臣以至誠之道事其君，故不自用其文，而文自顯於天下。夫文，何也？生乎質者也。質，主於誠者也。天下夫質之俚，故因以文之，而彼大臣者，固將以文而潤色天下者也。乃或日斤斤焉求所謂文，假先王之道以緣飾之，苟可以收名，不必於獲實，將必闊略其事，爲靡靡無當，而所以經方致遠、甄物成化之義，舉廢缺焉。卽黻黼之飾、麗藻之工也，其何以章軌物、樹鴻績哉？故
translation_en:
… sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity all followed this Way, and the excellence that moves people like the wind and the transformation that truly nurtures life all issued forth from this. Commentators say that reverence is the essential principle from beginning to end in the learning of the sages—truly it is so!

Second Session
Discourse
"The Literary Splendor of the Realm" (Tianxia wenzhang)
Wang Zhongxian
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhou comments: [The structure is clear and well-ordered, the diction refined and fluent, and the entire piece comes] back to throwing weight upon sincerity—a discourse rooted in what is fundamental.
Examiner Subprefectural Instructor Mei comments: [The meaning and argument are complete and sufficient.]
Examiner Prefectural Instructor Zhu comments: [Refined and fitting, worthy of serving as a model.]

When a great minister serves his ruler with the Way of utmost sincerity, he does not rely on his own literary embellishment, and yet literary splendor naturally manifests itself throughout the realm. Now, what is literary refinement (wen)? It is born of substance (zhi). And substance is governed by sincerity. When the substance in the world is rustic [?], one therefore uses refinement to adorn it; and those great ministers are indeed the ones who would use refinement to grace and embellish the realm. Yet if someone daily busies himself fastidiously seeking after so-called refinement, borrowing the Way of the former kings merely to dress things up—caring only to garner a reputation without necessarily attaining reality—he will inevitably neglect practical affairs, producing flashy, ungrounded work, while the principles for ordering the regions and reaching afar, for discerning things and accomplishing transformation, will all fall into neglect and deficiency. Even with the ornamentation of ceremonial embroidery and the craft of華麗 (florid) diction, how could that suffice to illuminate standard institutions and establish great achievements? Therefore…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
蹇蹇而匪躬者貞臣之行也抽辭而振藻者才
士之效也吾無庸文以付天下之才之能者吾
吾惟大其所隆以豫其可文之實則道脩而教
備德尊而化光不顯亦顯孰非文者此誠之徵
也韓魏公有焉公之相宋也歷事三朝定策兩
主出入將相名耀夷夏所謂垂紳正笏不動聲
色而措天下於泰山之安其德業豈不巍巍然
為有宋一代之鉅哉即庸人孺子而知之也而
歐陽脩者起文敝之後力以斯文為已任天下
===
學士大夫翕然宗之至方韓愈氏其文章亦豈
不炳炳烺烺聲稱耶或者以德業誦韓公而少
其文公亦不自有其文而以歸之脩於戲文非
公本心也意者非其心而漫以脩為解也曰非
也相天下之文與文人之文異文人言必稱先
聖明王道述禮樂聽之若軒縣金奏之音而視
之有重錦綺錯之色乃音不必登之清廟色不
必被之龍袞何者或無當於實故也而相天下
者誠異是上佐天子理陰陽順四時而下簡秩
punctuated: 蹇蹇而匪躬者，貞臣之行也；抽辭而振藻者，才士之效也。吾無庸文，以付天下之才之能者，吾吾惟大其所隆，以豫其可文之實。則道脩而教備，德尊而化光，不顯亦顯，孰非文者？此誠之徵也，韓魏公有焉。公之相宋也，歷事三朝，定策兩主，出入將相，名耀夷夏，所謂垂紳正笏，不動聲色，而措天下於泰山之安。其德業豈不巍巍然為有宋一代之鉅哉？即庸人孺子而知之也。而歐陽脩者，起文敝之後，力以斯文為已任，天下學士大夫翕然宗之，至方韓愈氏，其文章亦豈不炳炳烺烺聲稱耶？或者以德業誦韓公而少其文，公亦不自有其文而以歸之脩。於戲！文非公本心也。意者非其心而漫以脩為解也？曰：非也。相天下之文與文人之文異。文人言必稱先聖，明王道，述禮樂，聽之若軒縣金奏之音，而視之有重錦綺錯之色。乃音不必登之清廟，色不必被之龍袞，何者？或無當於實故也。而相天下者誠異是：上佐天子理陰陽、順四時，而下簡秩…
translation_en: …to be steadfastly loyal and selfless is the conduct of an upright minister; to spin out phrases and flourish rhetoric is the contribution of a talented scholar. I have no need to busy myself with literary ornament, leaving that instead to the talented and capable men of the world; I [?] simply magnify what is exalted in order to prepare the substance upon which ornament can be based. Then the Way is cultivated and instruction is complete, virtue is revered and transformation shines forth—even without striving for display, it becomes manifest. What part of this is not true culture (wen)? This is the verification of sincerity, and Duke Wei of Han (Han Qi 韓琦) possessed it. When the Duke served as Grand Councilor of Song, he served successively through three reigns, settled the succession for two sovereigns, went out as general and came in as councilor, his fame shining among both Chinese and non-Chinese. As the saying goes, with his sash hanging down and holding his tablet straight, without betraying a change of voice or countenance, he placed the realm upon the security of Mount Tai. Were his virtue and achievements not toweringly the greatest of the entire Song dynasty? Even ordinary folk and young children knew of him. Meanwhile, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 arose after a period of literary decline and vigorously took the cause of this culture (siwen) as his personal responsibility. The scholars and officials of the empire unanimously revered him as their master, even comparing him to Han Yu 韓愈; was his literary writing not also resplendently celebrated? Some praised Duke Han for his virtue and achievements while belittling his literary skill, and the Duke himself did not lay claim to literary skill, instead conceding it to Xiu. Alas! Literary ornament was not the Duke's primary concern. Could it be that because it was not his concern, he casually used Xiu as an excuse? I say: Not so. The culture of one who acts as councilor to the realm differs from the literature of a literary man. When a literary man speaks, he invariably cites the former sages, elucidates the Kingly Way, and recounts rites and music; listening to it is like the sound of suspended bells and bronze instruments, and looking at it is like the colors of layered brocade and patterned silk. Yet such sounds cannot necessarily be performed in the Sacred Temple, and such colors cannot necessarily be worn on the imperial dragon robes. Why is that? Because they may not correspond to substantive reality. One who acts as councilor to the realm is truly different from this: above, he assists the Son of Heaven in regulating yin and yang and harmonizing the four seasons, while below, he selects and orders…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
百職均一海內以制夷裔是故昭德塞違以明
示衆庶燮和叅贊文之經也紀綱法度文之紀
也禮樂名物文之象也於昭風動文之輝也大
夫章甫介士緩帶文之化也是必有積之無爲
極之本根誠一無僞以撰敘亮工而後其文顯
也夫本根實者枝葉茂文章枝葉者也天下未
有培其本沃其根而萎瘁其枝葉者故文章之
文有有也而無亦有也況夫以我之無收天下
之有舉世之所謂文學道藝者而優以禁闥之
===
寄議國是制辭命備顧問秉載記其所補於轄
理争化之道寧不亦籍待吾收之而何以致然
而亦何非吾之文也故智莫良於用才文莫大
於兼善黄鍾之律自我正之而衆音諧也龍袞
之文自我補之而衆色彰也夫韓公亦猶是也
當是時歐陽氏偃起五代之衰崇雅黜浮其思
所表樹當不在韓公後而其文亦豈專文人之
溺乃其以文名矣韓公之所無也公以相天下
之道任諸巳而以文推之歐陽氏若曰人有之
punctuated: 百職，均一海內，以制夷裔。是故昭德塞違，以明示衆庶。燮和叅贊，文之經也；紀綱法度，文之紀也；禮樂名物，文之象也；於昭風動，文之輝也；大夫章甫、介士緩帶，文之化也。是必有積之無爲，極之本根，誠一無僞，以撰敘亮工，而後其文顯也。夫本根實者枝葉茂，文章，枝葉者也。天下未有培其本、沃其根而萎瘁其枝葉者，故文章之文，有有也，而無亦有也。況夫以我之無，收天下之有，舉世之所謂文學道藝者，而優以禁闥之寄，議國是，制辭命，備顧問，秉載記，其所補於轄理争化之道，寧不亦籍？待吾收之，而何以致然？而亦何非吾之文也？故智莫良於用才，文莫大於兼善。黄鍾之律自我正之，而衆音諧也；龍袞之文自我補之，而衆色彰也。夫韓公亦猶是也。當是時，歐陽氏偃起五代之衰，崇雅黜浮，其思所表樹，當不在韓公後，而其文亦豈專文人之溺？乃其以文名矣，韓公之所無也。公以相天下之道任諸巳，而以文推之歐陽氏，若曰：人有之，
translation_en: … the hundred offices, unify all within the seas, and thereby control the barbarian borderlands. Therefore, he manifests virtue and blocks transgression so as to clearly display them to the multitude. Harmonizing and assisting in cosmic transformation are the warp of culture (wen); fundamental principles and laws and regulations are the woof of culture; ritual, music, titles, and emblems are the emblems of culture; shining brightly and moving people like the wind are the radiance of culture; grandees wearing the zhangfu cap and armored warriors wearing loose sashes are the transformative influence of culture. Thus, one must accumulate it in non-purposive action, carry it to the ultimate root and foundation, and with pure singleness and no falsity compose the order and assist in the achievements of governance—only afterward does one's culture become manifest. Now, when the root and trunk are solid, the branches and leaves are luxuriant; literary compositions are the branches and leaves. Nowhere in the world has anyone nurtured the trunk and watered the root only to have the branches and leaves wither. Therefore, as for the culture of literary composition, those who possess it possess it, and those who lack it also possess it. How much more so when, through what I lack, I gather in what the world possesses! Take all those in the world who are known for literature, moral learning, and the arts, and favor them with posts in the forbidden palace precincts—to deliberate on state policies, draft royal mandates, stand ready as advisors, and wield the brush for historical records. Is not what they contribute to the Way of governing and transforming [?] also substantial [?]? Yet it awaits my gathering them in—and how is this brought about, and how is it not also my own culture? Therefore, in wisdom nothing is better than employing talent, and in culture nothing is greater than encompassing the strengths of all. Once the pitch of the Yellow Bell is rectified by me, all notes are in harmony; once the patterns on the dragon robe are mended by me, all colors shine forth. Lord Han (Han Qi 韓琦) was just like this. At that time, Master Ouyang (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩) rose up [?] from the decline of the Five Dynasties, exalting refinement and rejecting superficiality. What he aspired to establish and accomplish was surely not behind Lord Han, and how could his writing be merely the indulgence of a literary man? Yet he became famous for his writing—which was what Lord Han lacked. The Lord took upon himself the Way of serving as Chief Councilor to the world, while yielding fame in literature to Master Ouyang, as if to say: "Others possess it, …"

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
我用之而人亦我也噫此公之不自用其文也
而亦不自有其文也夫公之相天下之文即無
論其業何如觀其言曰凡爲臣者盡力以事君
死生以之顧事之是非何如耳至於成敗天也
不可豫憂其不成而遂輟此其義豈可以聲音
笑貌爲之而其志亦豈易量哉故公當仁宗之
世雖號治平然而西北多故日不暇給至英神
之間益又異矣內廷猜貳賢邪竝進而公以不
撼不激之質砥柱乎其中忠誠意氣蓋素所熟
===
試於其主而天下事直已揉摩於胷中而無所
蒂儲貳未建則策定之非文則何以正而豫也
兩宮互疑則道以至性而調之如初非文則何
以和而中也請乘輿躬禱以荅天變而乞罷新
法非文則何以剴而切也以執政則引范仲淹
富弼以諫議則引蔡襄余靖王素非文則何以
明而確也以縱變倖則空勑而不名非文則何
以辨而嚴也是以三朝雖間亦有事而大要公
在朝廷之上後又濟濟海內熙熙晏晏鮮陰陽
punctuated: 我用之，而人亦我也。」噫！此公之不自用其文也，而亦不自有其文也。夫公之相天下之文，即無論其業何如，觀其言曰：「凡爲臣者，盡力以事君，死生以之，顧事之是非何如耳；至於成敗，天也，不可豫憂其不成而遂輟。」此其義豈可以聲音笑貌爲之，而其志亦豈易量哉！故公當仁宗之世，雖號治平，然而西北多故，日不暇給；至英、神之間，益又異矣，內廷猜貳，賢邪竝進，而公以不撼不激之質，砥柱乎其中。忠誠意氣，蓋素所熟試於其主，而天下事直已揉摩於胷中而無所蒂。儲貳未建，則策定之，非文則何以正而豫也？兩宮互疑，則道以至性而調之如初，非文則何以和而中也？請乘輿躬禱以荅天變，而乞罷新法，非文則何以剴而切也？以執政則引范仲淹、富弼，以諫議則引蔡襄、余靖、王素，非文則何以明而確也？以縱變倖，則空勑而不名，非文則何以辨而嚴也？是以三朝雖間亦有事，而大要公在朝廷之上，後又濟濟，海內熙熙晏晏，鮮陰陽…
translation_en: …I employ it, and what belongs to others is also mine." Ah! This is how the Duke did not employ his own literary brilliance for himself, nor did he claim ownership of his own literary brilliance. As for the Duke's brilliance in serving as Chief Councilor to the world, even setting aside what his achievements were like, consider his words: "All who serve as ministers exert their utmost strength to serve their ruler, staking life and death upon it, looking only at whether the matter is right or wrong. As for success or failure, that rests with Heaven; one must not worry in advance that it will not succeed and thereupon abandon it." How could the righteousness of this be achieved through mere tone of voice and smiling countenance, and how could his ambition be easily measured! Therefore, when the Duke lived in the reign of Emperor Renzong, although it was called an era of peace and order, the northwest was beset with troubles and there was not enough time in the day to attend to them all. By the reigns of Emperors Yingzong and Shenzong, things had grown even more different: there was suspicion and division within the inner court, while the worthy and the wicked advanced together. Yet the Duke, with a character neither shaken nor provoked, stood as a pillar amidst it all. His loyal sincerity and spirited resolve had long been thoroughly tested before his sovereigns, and the affairs of the world had already been thoroughly turned over and smoothed out in his breast without the slightest obstruction. When the Heir Apparent had not yet been established, he settled the matter through his counsel—if not for his brilliance, how could it have been done so properly and with such foresight? When the Two Palaces suspected each other, he guided them through their deepest natural affections and reconciled them as before—if not for his brilliance, how could it have been so harmonious and balanced? When he requested that the imperial carriage pray in person in response to heavenly anomalies, and begged for the abolition of the New Policies—if not for his brilliance, how could he have been so incisive and earnest? For administrative statesmen he brought forward Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 and Fu Bi 富弼, and for remonstrance officials he brought forward Cai Xiang 蔡襄, Yu Jing 余靖, and Wang Su 王素—if not for his brilliance, how could he have been so clear-sighted and decisive? For curbing favorites [?], he returned imperial edicts blank without inscribing the names—if not for his brilliance, how could he have been so discerning and strict? Thus, although across the three reigns there were occasionally troubles, in general while the Duke stood above at court, with an abundant array of worthy successors behind him, the realm within the seas was prosperous, tranquil, and at ease, rarely suffering from disasters of yin and yang or…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
四時之災契丹幸未侵暴而元昊贍寒且稱臣
於慶曆焉公之文章若此矣若乃遡公之生平
以觀所謂文則知初知制誥之時經略延州之
猷三判相州之政四策七事之陳率皆條理詳
明章章然雅重中外而奏名瑞雲天象等已應
之安在其少文也假令公之功業未盡章知
是而至誠惻怛之衷有所未至而猥以聲音笑
貌爲之即五代有史兩制有集以稱於天下後
世不過曰文人文人云耳奚益也故無聲之聲
===
天下之正聲也不色之色天下之正色也不文
之文天下之至文也故曰公不自有其文而非
以脩爲解也蓋昔者子產之相鄭也國小而偪
族大寵多外厭晉楚之求而內制伯有豐卷之
汰彼其時辭命不一日廢也乃子產未自爲之
則以命公孫揮而問四國之爲諸侯咸以爲子
產有辭公孫弘以漢相起賢良文學明春秋之
義輔漢武然而布被無實而不忍於一汲黯天
下未嘗稱其文何者弘僞而子產誠也韓之於
punctuated: 四時之災，契丹幸未侵暴，而元昊贍寒，且稱臣於慶曆焉。公之文章若此矣。若乃遡公之生平，以觀所謂文，則知初知制誥之時，經略延州之猷，三判相州之政，四策七事之陳，率皆條理詳明，章章然雅重中外，而奏名瑞雲、天象等已應之，安在其少文也？假令公之功業未盡章知是，而至誠惻怛之衷有所未至，而猥以聲音笑貌爲之，即五代有史，兩制有集，以稱於天下後世，不過曰「文人、文人」云耳，奚益也？故無聲之聲，天下之正聲也；不色之色，天下之正色也；不文之文，天下之至文也。故曰公不自有其文，而非以脩爲解也。蓋昔者子產之相鄭也，國小而偪，族大寵多，外厭晉、楚之求，而內制伯有、豐卷之汰。彼其時，辭命不一日廢也，乃子產未自爲之，則以命公孫揮而問四國之爲，諸侯咸以爲子產有辭。公孫弘以漢相起賢良文學，明《春秋》之義，輔漢武，然而布被無實，而不忍於一汲黯，天下未嘗稱其文。何者？弘僞而子產誠也。韓之於
translation_en: … calamities of the four seasons; the Khitan fortunately did not invade or ravage, while Yuanhao’s gall grew cold [in fear] and he declared himself a vassal during the Qingli reign (1041–1048). Such was the Duke’s [Han Qi’s 韓琦] literary brilliance! If we trace back the Duke’s life to examine what is called his writing, we know that from the time he first served as Drafter, his plans as Pacification Commissioner of Yanzhou, his administration when thrice serving as Prefect of Xiangzhou, and his presentation of the four policy essays and seven affairs were all detailed, clear, and well-ordered, brilliantly earning high esteem at court and in the provinces—and when his name was announced at the palace examination, auspicious clouds and celestial signs had already responded to it. How could it be that he lacked literary skill? Suppose the Duke’s achievements had not been as fully manifest as this [?], and his utmost sincerity and compassionate heart had fallen short in some way, so that he merely contrived things through outward voice and smiling countenance—even if he had written a history of the Five Dynasties and had collected works from his service in the two drafting offices for which to be praised across the realm and in later generations, people would merely have called him “a literary man, a literary man,” and nothing more. Of what benefit would that be? Therefore, the sound that is soundless is the true sound of the world; the color that is colorless is the true color of the world; the writing that is unadorned is the supreme writing of the world. Thus I say that the Duke did not claim literary skill as his own, and was not using [Ouyang] Xiu 歐陽脩 as an excuse. In antiquity, when Zichan 子產 served as chief minister of Zheng, the state was small and hemmed in, its clans were great and favored ones many; externally he satisfied the demands of Jin and Chu, while internally he curbed the arrogance of Boyou 伯有 and Feng Juan 豐卷. At that time, diplomatic correspondence could not be neglected for a single day. Yet Zichan did not compose it all himself; he ordered Gongsun Hui 公孫揮 to inquire into the affairs of the surrounding states, and the feudal lords all considered Zichan to be a master of diplomatic speech. Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 rose from the ranks of the Worthy and Upright and Literary Scholars to become Chancellor of Han, elucidating the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) to assist Emperor Wu of Han. Yet his coarse cloth quilt lacked genuine substance, and he could not even tolerate a single Ji An 汲黯; the world never praised his literary refinement. Why is this? Because Hong was deceitful whereas Zichan was sincere. In Han [Qi]’s relationship to …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
歐陽毋亦子產之謂乎而韓公誠以建業而終
之以文則固不止於有辭已也故曰大臣以至
誠之道事其君則不自用其文而文自顯於天
下
同前
張泰徵
同考試官教諭唐　批〔詞華英邁無一浮浪語是留心〕
〔於論學者取之〕
考試官學正梅　批〔氣焰光灶誦之忘倦〕
===
考試官教授朱　批〔有議論有學識〕
人臣有至文焉章於天下而非天下之所能知
也夫文而可名非至文也文而可名乃無闗於
天下之故者故天下知其文而不足以稱天下
之文天下之文之至也而天下之人不知之
則固以其經緯之業超於詞章之外而天下之
人日被其輝光而莫之能名惟不能名斯不能
加而其文爲至矣天下文章莫大於是魏公之
言其有得於相道也與哉且永叔之文章何如
punctuated:
歐陽，毋亦子產之謂乎？而韓公誠以建業，而終之以文，則固不止於有辭已也。故曰：大臣以至誠之道事其君，則不自用其文，而文自顯於天下。

同前
張泰徵
同考試官教諭唐　批〔詞華英邁，無一浮浪語，是留心於論學者，取之。〕
考試官學正梅　批〔氣焰光灶，誦之忘倦。〕
考試官教授朱　批〔有議論，有學識。〕

人臣有至文焉，章於天下，而非天下之所能知也。夫文而可名，非至文也；文而可名，乃無闗於天下之故者，故天下知其文，而不足以稱天下之文。天下之文之至也，而天下之人不知之，則固以其經緯之業超於詞章之外，而天下之人日被其輝光而莫之能名。惟不能名，斯不能加，而其文爲至矣。「天下文章莫大於是」，魏公之言，其有得於相道也與哉！且永叔之文章何如…
translation_en:
…Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修—is this not just what was meant by the case of Zichan 子產? Yet Duke Han (Han Qi 韓琦) established his great enterprise through sincerity and consummated it with literary culture; thus he certainly went far beyond merely possessing fine diplomatic rhetoric. Therefore it is said: When a great minister serves his ruler through the Way of utmost sincerity, he does not employ literary composition himself, yet his literary culture naturally becomes manifest throughout the realm.

Same topic as before.
By Zhang Taizheng 張泰徵.
Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Tang 唐 comments: [His literary elegance is heroic and surpassing, without a single frivolous or ungrounded word; this is someone who applies his mind to the study of discourse. Selected.]
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Mei 梅 comments: [Its spirit and brilliance shine forth [?]; reciting it, one forgets fatigue.]
Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu 朱 comments: [Possesses both solid argument and scholarly learning.]

A minister possesses the ultimate literary culture, which shines forth throughout the realm, yet the realm is incapable of recognizing it. Now, literary culture that can be named is not the ultimate literary culture. Literary culture that can be named is something unconnected to the great affairs of the realm; therefore, the realm may know of such writings, yet they are insufficient to be called the literary culture of the realm. When the literary culture of the realm reaches its ultimate height, yet the people of the realm do not recognize it as such, it is surely because its statecraft enterprise of warp and woof transcends mere rhetoric and composition, so that the people of the realm daily receive its radiant light without being able to put a name to it. Precisely because it cannot be named, nothing can be added to it, and thus its literary culture is the ultimate. "In the realm, there is no literary composition greater than this"—do not these words of the Duke of Wei 魏公 (Han Qi) grasp the true Way of a chief minister! Moreover, what was the literary composition of Yongshu 永叔 (Ouyang Xiu) like…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
也謹嚴祖於昌黎簡古宗於師曾者也正文體
而鉤棘險怪之習變進黨論而君子小人之朋
分以至五代有史兩制有集追班馬而侔訓誥
者當時誠重之矣魏公之爲相也而永叔爲學
士得以文章鳴於天下則永叔之文章孰非魏
公之文章乎噫公之文章以是名與公之文章
而以是名也是時人之所謂文章也唐虞之世
稷契皋夔俱稱聖賢之佐彼其垂休樹績照日
月而耀古今者豈在於衒官屈宋奴僕離騷爭
===
奇鬬巧如文人墨士流哉夫擷華擬菁以矜字
句之奇者此訓詁之文一人之文章也立言闡
義以發今昔之故者此著述之文一家之文章
也脩飾潤色以誇交好之儀者此詞命之文一
國之文章也一人者無論已卽一家一國之文
於天下奚稱焉夫宰相不自用然後能用人歐
陽氏以文章鳴於天下也伊誰用之哉故順理
成章論以爲文而僎之與公叔子同升也孔子
稱之曰可以爲文矣然則公之文章以此乎曰
punctuated: 也？謹嚴祖於昌黎，簡古宗於師曾者也。正文體而鉤棘險怪之習變，進《黨論》而君子小人之朋分，以至《五代》有史、《兩制》有集，追班、馬而侔訓誥者，當時誠重之矣。魏公之爲相也，而永叔爲學士，得以文章鳴於天下，則永叔之文章，孰非魏公之文章乎？噫！公之文章以是名與？公之文章而以是名也，是時人之所謂文章也。唐虞之世，稷、契、皋、夔俱稱聖賢之佐，彼其垂休樹績，照日月而耀古今者，豈在於衒官屈、宋，奴僕《離騷》，爭奇鬬巧，如文人墨士流哉？夫擷華擬菁，以矜字句之奇者，此訓詁之文，一人之文章也；立言闡義，以發今昔之故者，此著述之文，一家之文章也；脩飾潤色，以誇交好之儀者，此詞命之文，一國之文章也。一人者無論已，卽一家、一國之文，於天下奚稱焉？夫宰相不自用，然後能用人。歐陽氏以文章鳴於天下也，伊誰用之哉？故順理成章，論以爲文；而僎之與公叔子同升也，孔子稱之曰：「可以爲文矣。」然則公之文章以此乎？曰：
translation_en:
… [And what was the literary attainment of Yongshu (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修)] like? In rigorous precision he took Changli (Han Yu 韓愈) as his ancestor, and in concise antiquity he took Shizeng (Yin Zhu 尹洙) as his model. He rectified literary style so that the habit of thorny obscurity and bizarre eccentricity was transformed; he submitted his "Discourse on Factions" (Danglun) so that the cliques of gentlemen and petty men were distinguished; and furthermore, for the Five Dynasties there was his history, and from his service in the Two Drafting Groups there were his collected works—pursuing Ban Gu 班固 and Sima Qian 司馬遷 and equaling the ancient instructions and announcements. His contemporaries truly held him in high esteem! When Duke Wei (Han Qi 韓琦) was Grand Councilor, Yongshu served as an Academician and was able to make his name resound throughout the empire through his literary writings; what part of Yongshu's literary attainment, then, was not Duke Wei's literary attainment?

Alas! Is the Duke's literary attainment renowned merely for this? If the Duke's literary attainment were renowned merely for this, that would only be what the men of the time called literary attainment. In the age of Tang (Yao 堯) and Yu (Shun 舜), Ji 稷, Xie 契, Gao Yao 皋陶, and Kui 夔 were all acclaimed as aides to sages and worthies. How could their handing down of blessings and establishing of achievements—shining alongside the sun and moon and illuminating antiquity and the present—consist in making showy officers of Qu Yuan 屈原 and Song Yu 宋玉, reducing the "Encountering Sorrow" (Lisao) to a servant, and competing in novelty and ingenuity after the manner of mere literati and ink-men?

Now, plucking blossoms and imitating the finest essence in order to boast of the novelty of words and phrases—this is exegetical writing, the literary attainment of a single individual. Establishing words and elucidating principles in order to bring forth the causes of past and present—this is scholarly composition, the literary attainment of a single school. Polishing and embellishing in order to vaunt the ceremonial etiquette of diplomatic intercourse—this is diplomatic rhetoric, the literary attainment of a single state. Setting aside that of a single individual, even the writings of a single school or a single state—what claim do they have upon the entire empire?

Indeed, only when a Grand Councilor does not rely solely on himself is he able to employ others. That Master Ouyang made his name resound throughout the empire through his literary writings—who was it that employed him? Therefore, following principle to form coherent patterns is judged to be "cultured" (wen); and when Zhuan 僎 was promoted alongside Gongshu Wenzi 公叔文子, Confucius praised him, saying: "He deserves to be called 'Cultured' (Wen)." Was the Duke's literary attainment, then, based on this? I say: …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
未也語文章之宗者卽歸之孔子孔子之文章
蓋性與天道之顯設也故曰文王旣沒文不在
兹而文王之文光於四方顯於西土至其所以
爲文也曰純亦不已夫論文章而不本於德業
奚以言文章又奚以言天下之文章也魏公爲
相之時何時也大本未立人心未固邊烽未息
也公以一身而處危疑之際其所以振頹綱以
祚宋室者未易更僕數矣至其定策兩朝以立
大本調和兩宮以固人心經略西夏以靖邊塵
===
其績偉也秉與請禱而天變弭新法議罷而民
心悅四策七事之陳而安攘賴此其德業奚愧
於古人哉然卽公之所以爲文章者也夫干將
鏌釾人知其爲利器也而不知射斗之光在是
是故天下言干將鏌釾之利而不言其文崑壁
藍瑛人知其至寶也而不知應宿之輝在是是
故天下言崑壁藍瑛之寶而不言其文今之論
公何以異於是公以忠誠之德而運康濟之才
不動聲色而措天下於泰山之安凡其所施皆
punctuated: 未也。語文章之宗者，卽歸之孔子。孔子之文章，蓋性與天道之顯設也。故曰：「文王旣沒，文不在兹？」而文王之文，光於四方，顯於西土；至其所以爲文也，曰「純亦不已」。夫論文章而不本於德業，奚以言文章？又奚以言天下之文章也？魏公爲相之時，何時也？大本未立，人心未固，邊烽未息也。公以一身而處危疑之際，其所以振頹綱以祚宋室者，未易更僕數矣。至其定策兩朝以立大本，調和兩宮以固人心，經略西夏以靖邊塵，其績偉也；秉與請禱而天變弭，新法議罷而民心悅，四策七事之陳而安攘賴。此其德業，奚愧於古人哉？然卽公之所以爲文章者也。夫干將、鏌釾，人知其爲利器也，而不知射斗之光在是；是故天下言干將、鏌釾之利，而不言其文。崑壁、藍瑛，人知其至寶也，而不知應宿之輝在是；是故天下言崑壁、藍瑛之寶，而不言其文。今之論公，何以異於是？公以忠誠之德，而運康濟之才，不動聲色，而措天下於泰山之安，凡其所施，皆
translation_en:
Not yet. Those who speak of the supreme model of literary expression trace it straight to Confucius. The literary expression of Confucius was indeed the outward manifestation of human nature and the Way of Heaven. Thus he said, "Since King Wen has passed away, is not culture invested here in me?" And the culture of King Wen shone across the four quarters and was resplendent in the western lands; as for what made him "cultured" (wen), it is said: "His purity likewise never ceased." Now, if one discusses literary expression without grounding it in virtuous achievements, how can one speak of literary expression? And how much less can one speak of the literary expression of the entire realm?

What sort of time was it when the Duke of Wei [Han Qi 韓琦] served as Grand Councilor? It was a time when the great foundation of the state was not yet established, the hearts of the people were not yet secure, and the beacon fires on the frontiers had not yet died down. Standing alone amid peril and doubt, the ways in which the Duke revitalized decaying institutions to bless the house of Song are too numerous to count even if one changed attendants. As for his settling the succession across two reigns to establish the great foundation, harmonizing the Two Palaces to secure the hearts of the people, and managing the campaigns against Western Xia to pacify the frontier dust—his merits were magnificent! When the imperial carriage [reading 輿 for 與] went forth to pray for rain, heavenly anomalies were quelled; when he argued for the abolition of the New Policies, the hearts of the people rejoiced; and when he submitted his four strategies and seven affairs, internal peace and external defense depended upon them. In such virtuous achievements, how does he fall short of the ancients? Yet these very deeds are what constituted the Duke's literary expression.

As for the swords Ganjiang and Moye, people know them as sharp weapons, yet do not realize that the radiance shooting up to the Northern Dipper resides within them; therefore, the world speaks of the sharpness of Ganjiang and Moye, and not of theirpatterned brilliance (wen). As for the jade discs of Kunlun and the fine gems of Lantian, people know them as supreme treasures, yet do not realize that the luster answering to the constellations resides within them; therefore, the world speaks of the preciousness of Kunlun discs and Lantian gems, and not of their patterned brilliance. How is the present discussion of the Duke any different from this? With the virtue of loyalty and sincerity, the Duke wielded the talent to bring peace and relief; without betraying a sign in voice or countenance, he placed the realm upon the security of Mount Tai. All that he enacted was…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
足以珪璋治化黻黼皇猷昭華夷而耀今昔者
蓋關乎天下也而謂之非文章乎無文之文天
下之至文在焉則天下之文孰能有加而天下
之人亦孰能以名之耶嗚呼雲呈五彩公之文
章已預知於臚唱之時矣則公之重於天下者
信不徒以詞章已也如必曰金輿玉輦之富也
風穡陣馬之健也閑鷗立海輕雲蔽日之逸與
麗也以論文章而且責之宰相也則安劉者何
取於少文之勃賜周公之圖者乃不事詩書之
===
霍光耶是故河南之簡盱江之銳眉山之浩南
豐之毅以文章稱雄於天聖慶曆間者非獨廬
陵氏矣而相宋者必魏公也夫文而無補於世
無關於天下詞家者流也非相也乃相則以正
紀綱以安社稷以叅贊天地詞章非所尚也故
考究精專實踐未得卽永叔之文且無裨於世
用矣況其他乎昔者周公之相成王也王雖賢
猶稱沖子也公負扆而輔之以裨君德而臻太
和而公且亟亟焉吐握以下天下之士是故周
punctuated: 足以珪璋治化，黻黼皇猷，昭華夷而耀今昔者，蓋關乎天下也，而謂之非文章乎？無文之文，天下之至文在焉；則天下之文孰能有加，而天下之人亦孰能以名之耶？嗚呼！雲呈五彩，公之文章，已預知於臚唱之時矣；則公之重於天下者，信不徒以詞章已也。如必曰金輿玉輦之富也，風穡陣馬之健也，閑鷗立海、輕雲蔽日之逸與麗也，以論文章而且責之宰相也，則安劉者何取於少文之勃？賜周公之圖者，乃不事《詩》、《書》之霍光耶？是故河南之簡，盱江之銳，眉山之浩，南豐之毅，以文章稱雄於天聖、慶曆間者，非獨廬陵氏矣；而相宋者，必魏公也。夫文而無補於世，無關於天下，詞家者流也，非相也。乃相則以正紀綱，以安社稷，以叅贊天地，詞章非所尚也。故考究精專，實踐未得，卽永叔之文且無裨於世用矣，況其他乎？昔者周公之相成王也，王雖賢，猶稱沖子也。公負扆而輔之，以裨君德而臻太和；而公且亟亟焉吐握以下天下之士。是故《周
translation_en: …sufficient to serve as jade tablets adorning governance and transformation, and as ceremonial robes embellishing the imperial plan, shining upon Chinese and non-Chinese alike and illuminating past and present—for all these concern the entire realm. How then could they be called anything other than literary composition (wenzhang)? In the composition that has no ornate words lies the supreme literary composition of the world; what writing in the world could surpass it, and who in the world could find a name for it? Alas! When the clouds displayed five colors, the Duke's [Han Qi 韓琦, Duke of Wei 魏公] literary brilliance was already foreknown at the time his name was called out at the palace roll call; thus, the esteem in which the Duke was held throughout the realm truly did not rest merely upon belles-lettres! If one insists on speaking of the richness of golden carriages and jade palanquins, the vigor of wind-driven sails [?; 風穡, for 風檣] and battle horses, or the leisurely grace and beauty of idle gulls standing by the sea and light clouds shading the sun in order to judge literary composition, and moreover demands such things of a Grand Councilor—then why did the one who secured the Liu 劉 clan turn out to be Zhou Bo 周勃, who lacked literary refinement? And why was the one granted the painting of the Duke of Zhou 周公 none other than Huo Guang 霍光, who did not occupy himself with the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu)? Therefore, with the conciseness of Henan 河南 [Yin Shu 尹洙], the sharpness of Xujiang 盱江 [Li Gou 李覯], the vastness of Meishan 眉山 [Su Xun 蘇洵 / the Su family], and the firmness of Nanfeng 南豐 [Zeng Gong 曾鞏], those who were renowned as masters of literary composition during the Tiansheng 天聖 (1023–1032) and Qingli 慶曆 (1041–1048) eras were not limited to Mr. Luling 廬陵 [Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修] alone; yet the one who served as Grand Councilor of the Song 宋 had to be the Duke of Wei! Writing that brings no benefit to the age and has no bearing upon the realm belongs to the class of mere rhetoricians, not to a Grand Councilor. A Grand Councilor, by contrast, rectifies the laws and institutions, secures the altars of state, and assists in the transforming work of Heaven and Earth; belles-lettres are not what he prizes. Thus, if one's scholarly inquiry is specialized and refined while practical implementation remains unattained, even the writings of Yongshu 永叔 [Ouyang Xiu] would be of no avail for practical use in the world—how much less those of others! In antiquity, when the Duke of Zhou served as chief minister to King Cheng 成王, although the King was worthy, he was still called a young child. The Duke stood before the embroidered screen and assisted him, thereby augmenting the sovereign's virtue and attaining supreme harmony; and yet the Duke also urgently spat out his food and bound up his wet hair to humble himself before the scholars of the realm. Therefore, the Rites of Zhou (Zhou…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
官之文炳燿千古孔子稱之曰郁郁乎文哉夫
郁郁之文周公之文也知周公可以知魏公矣
然而先儒猶不足其規模之麤也抑以魏公之
文章尚有歉於周公也
表
擬
駕幸太學
賜三氏子孫宴謝表
景明
===
同考試官教諭梁　批〔仰惟〕
〔視學〕
〔賜宴乃我〕
〔朝特典子能揄揚其盛蓋不獨四六之工巳也取之〕
考試官學正梅　批〔駢麗〕
考試官教授朱　批〔忠愛之意藹然〕
擬
駕幸太學
賜三氏子孫宴謝表
punctuated:
官之文，炳燿千古。孔子稱之曰：「郁郁乎文哉！」夫郁郁之文，周公之文也。知周公，可以知魏公矣。然而先儒猶不足其規模之麤也，抑以魏公之文章，尚有歉於周公也。

表
擬駕幸太學賜三氏子孫宴謝表
景明
同考試官教諭梁　批〔仰惟視學賜宴，乃我朝特典，子能揄揚其盛，蓋不獨四六之工巳也。取之。〕
考試官學正梅　批〔駢麗。〕
考試官教授朱　批〔忠愛之意藹然。〕
擬駕幸太學賜三氏子孫宴謝表
translation_en:
…culture of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouguan) shines resplendently through a thousand ages. Confucius praised it, saying, "How rich and glorious is its culture!" Indeed, that rich and glorious culture was the culture of the Duke of Zhou. If one understands the Duke of Zhou, one can understand Duke Wei [Han Qi 韓琦]. Yet earlier Confucians were still dissatisfied with the coarseness of his overall framework—perhaps because Duke Wei's cultural attainment still fell short of the Duke of Zhou's.

Memorial
Proposed Memorial of Thanks on the Occasion of the Imperial Carriage Visiting the National University and Bestowing a Banquet upon the Descendants of the Three Clans [Confucius, Mencius, and Yan Hui]
Jing Ming 景明
Associate Examiner, Instructor Liang, comments: [Reverently considering that inspecting the National University and bestowing a banquet is a special grace of our Dynasty, you have been able to extol its magnificence; this is not merely skill in four-and-six parallel prose alone. Accepted.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Xuezhen (Director of Studies) Mei, comments: [Finely paired and ornate.]
Examiner, Prefectural Instructor Zhu, comments: [An abundance of loyal and affectionate sentiment.]

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆四年八月某日恭遇
駕幸太學伏蒙
聖恩賜〔臣某〕等宴謹奉
表稱
謝者伏以
化溥菁莪宏千載右文之治
恩深湛露荷
九重禮士之仁驚
玉輅之遙臨辟廱風動喜
===
龍光之下被俎豆春融寵溢黌宮慶流文軌〔臣〕
〔某〕竊惟
聖主必崇儒而重道明時斯建學以育才自敎
述六經木鐸洪鳴於泗水而蒙開萬古金
聲大振乎尼山十哲雲從四科首列深幸
私淑有地誰云未得爲徒博約親承功深
卓爾誠明獨契統繼聞知相與後先啓授
受之傳詎意今古錫聖賢之號道未墜地
追封之特典時加文其在玆什奠之秩儀
punctuated:
萬曆四年八月某日，恭遇駕幸太學，伏蒙聖恩賜〔臣某〕等宴，謹奉表稱謝者。

伏以化溥菁莪，宏千載右文之治；恩深湛露，荷九重禮士之仁。驚玉輅之遙臨，辟廱風動；喜龍光之下被，俎豆春融。寵溢黌宮，慶流文軌。〔臣〕〔某〕竊惟：聖主必崇儒而重道，明時斯建學以育才。自敎述《六經》，木鐸洪鳴於泗水；而蒙開萬古，金聲大振乎尼山。十哲雲從，四科首列。深幸私淑有地，誰云未得爲徒？博約親承，功深卓爾；誠明獨契，統繼聞知。相與後先，啓授受之傳；詎意今古，錫聖賢之號。道未墜地，追封之特典時加；文其在玆，什奠之秩儀
translation_en:
On a certain day in the eighth month of the fourth year of the Wanli reign [1576], having reverently encountered the Imperial Carriage visiting the Directorate of Education, and humbly received the Sacred Grace bestowing a banquet upon [Your Servant So-and-So] and others, we respectfully present this memorial to express our gratitude.

We humbly reflect that as transforming influence spreads like the luxuriant tarragon [of the "Jing'e" ode], it expands a thousand years of governance that esteems civil culture; as grace runs deep like the heavy dew [of the "Zhanlu" ode], we are blessed with the Ninefold Palace's benevolence in honoring scholars. Awed by the distant approach of the Jade Carriage, the Biyong hall is stirred as if by the wind; rejoicing in the dragon light shining down upon us, the ritual vessels warm as if in spring. Favor overflows the school palace, and celebration streams across the realm of shared script and axle-width.

[Your Servant] [So-and-So] humbly reflects: a sage ruler必ず esteems Confucians and reveres the Way, and an enlightened era thus establishes schools to nurture talent. Ever since teachings were transmitted through the Six Classics, the wooden-tongued bell resounded mightily by the Si River; and as ignorance was dispelled for ten thousand ages, the bronze chimes vibrated grandly on Mount Ni. The Ten Savants followed like clouds, and the four categories of disciples stood at the forefront. How fortunate that there was a place to cultivate oneself through his influence from afar—who says one could not be his direct disciple [like Mencius]? Personally receiving the teaching of broadening with learning and restraining with ritual, [Yan Hui's] effort reached the depths of "standing lofty before me"; uniquely grasping sincerity and enlightenment, [Zisi and Mencius] continued the lineage of knowing by hearing and knowing by seeing. Succeeding one another earlier and later, they opened up the transmission of master-to-disciple instruction; how could they have anticipated that across past and present, they would be granted the titles of Sages and Worthies? This Way has not fallen to the ground, and special acts of grace conferring posthumous enfeoffments have been added from time to time; culture is lodged right here, and the ordered ceremonies of the sacrificial libations [shidian, for shidian 釋奠?]…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
漸備闕里肇脩大祀永平再舉曠儀輯美
唐皇四拜禮隆於繳衮傳芳宋世五品錫
渥乎儒臣所慚實德未崇奚取虛文徒飾
隆汙所在治忽攸關仰惟
昭代弘模卓越前王彛梗恭惟
皇帝陛下
英明天縱
仁孝性生
郊禮同
===
廟饗時親式重精禋之典
常朝與
講筵日御每廑延訪之誠
筆底龍蛇不嗜鍾王李篆
宮中宵旰常酬孔思周情謂太學爲賢士所
闗而先聖實生民未有曾
齋心而視奠遂筮日以
臨雍
清蹕聲傳胄監覩
punctuated: 漸備。闕里肇脩大祀，永平再舉曠儀；輯美唐皇，四拜禮隆於繳衮；傳芳宋世，五品錫渥乎儒臣。所慚實德未崇，奚取虛文徒飾？隆汙所在，治忽攸關。仰惟昭代弘模，卓越前王彛梗。恭惟皇帝陛下，英明天縱，仁孝性生。郊禮同廟饗時親，式重精禋之典；常朝與講筵日御，每廑延訪之誠。筆底龍蛇，不嗜鍾、王、李篆；宮中宵旰，常酬孔思、周情。謂太學爲賢士所闗，而先聖實生民未有，曾齋心而視奠，遂筮日以臨雍。清蹕聲傳，胄監覩
translation_en:
… gradually became complete. At Queli, the grand sacrifice was first instituted; in the Yongping era, the rare ceremony was performed once again. Gathering praise in the reigns of the Tang emperors, the rite was exalted with four bows in imperial dragon robes [?]; transmitting fragrance through the generations of the Song, generous conferrals of the fifth rank were bestowed upon Confucian scholars. Yet what was regrettable was that substantive virtue was not truly revered—what use was there in merely embellishing with empty formalities? Herein lies the distinction between flourishing and decline, and upon this hinges good governance or neglect. Looking up in reflection upon the grand model of our Illustrious Dynasty, it far surpasses the standard norms [?] of former kings.

Reverently, I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor is endowed by Heaven with heroic brilliance, and born with a nature of benevolence and filial piety. The suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temple offerings are seasonally attended in person, showing deep reverence for the canons of pure sacrifice; the regular court audiences and the Classics Colloquium are presided over daily, ever demonstrating earnest sincerity in receiving and consulting officials. Though Your Majesty's brush moves like dragons and snakes, You do not indulge in the calligraphy of Zhong Yao, Wang Xizhi, or the seal script of Li Si; working from before dawn until late at night in the palace, You constantly engage with the thoughts of Confucius and the sentiments of the Duke of Zhou. Deeming that the Imperial University is vital to worthy scholars, and that the Former Sage was truly unequaled since the birth of mankind, You have purified Your heart to oversee the libations, and thus divined an auspicious day to visit the Imperial University. As the sound of the herald clearing the imperial way is transmitted, the Directorate of Education beholds …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
鑾輿之近祥輝色耀宮牆瞻
黼座之光翕道壁之金絲雅音繼作委
上方之玉帛祀事肅將
喜洽泮芹
心遊神聖乃進官而論道爰愛星以及烏氈
集六儒坐講沐非常之寵觴聯三姓
傳頒欣既醉之榮伏念〔臣某〕等杏壇遺裔空
含詩禮餘馨鄒魯庸流濫附冠裳末品學
非顓達志非眞卿養非孟敏魚麗誤辱於
===
南宮飲效簞瓢飯效蔬食恍效拳弱燕享
叨承乎
北闕〔臣〕敢不含咀道旨嚅嚌性眞勉力象賢
期無玷乎箕裘之舊協衷報
主願少攄乎葵藿之忱伏願
帝學益純
聖眞默契鹽梅麴蘖嘗懷鼎鼐之思
宗廟百官每切羹牆之見位
君師而建極求調
punctuated: 鑾輿之近；祥輝色耀，宮牆瞻黼座之光。翕道壁之金絲，雅音繼作；委上方之玉帛，祀事肅將。喜洽泮芹，心遊神聖。乃進官而論道，爰愛屋以及烏。氈集六儒，坐講沐非常之寵；觴聯三姓，傳頒欣既醉之榮。伏念〔臣某〕等，杏壇遺裔，空含詩禮餘馨；鄒魯庸流，濫附冠裳末品。學非顓達，志非眞卿，養非孟敏，魚麗誤辱於南宮；飲效簞瓢，飯效蔬食，恍效拳跼，燕享叨承乎北闕。〔臣〕敢不含咀道旨，嚅嚌性眞，勉力象賢，期無玷乎箕裘之舊；協衷報主，願少攄乎葵藿之忱。伏願帝學益純，聖眞默契。鹽梅麴蘖，嘗懷鼎鼐之思；宗廟百官，每切羹牆之見。位君師而建極，求調
translation_en:
…the approach of the imperial carriage; as auspicious radiance shines brightly, the walls of the temple gaze upon the splendor of the imperial throne. Harmonizing with the metal and silk instruments heard in the wall of the Way, elegant music successively arises; presenting the jade and silk from the Imperial Manufactories, the sacrificial rites are reverently performed. Joy pervades the semicircular academy pool and its cress, while Your mind roams among the divine and sage. Thereupon You summon the officials to discourse upon the Way, extending Your affection even to the crows upon the roof. On the felt rugs gather the six Confucian scholars, who in seated lectures are bathed in extraordinary favor; the wine goblets unite the three clans of the sages' descendants, who through the transmitted bestowals rejoice in the glory of the ode "Already Drunk" (Jizui).

Humbly we reflect that Your servants [so-and-so] and others are the surviving descendants of the Apricot Altar, vainly holding the lingering fragrance of the Odes and Rites; mediocre men of Zou and Lu, we unworthily attach ourselves to the lowest ranks of the capped and robed. In learning we lack the comprehension of Zhuansun Shi (Zizhang), in aspiration the true ministership of Zhong You (Zilu), and in self-cultivation the acuity of Meng Ke (Mencius), yet the banquet of the ode "Fish Traps" (Yuli) has mistakenly graced us at the Southern Palace; in drink we imitate Yan Hui's single gourd dish, in food we imitate his coarse fare, and in manner we imitate his reverent, bent-kneed posture [?], yet we have unworthily received the ceremonial feast at the Northern Portal. How dare Your servants not savor the purport of the Way, taste the truth of human nature, and strive to emulate the worthy, hoping not to blemish the old heritage of our ancestors' craft; and unite our hearts to repay our Sovereign, wishing to express in some small measure the sincerity of the sunflower turning toward the sun?

We humbly pray that the imperial learning may become ever purer, and that You may silently accord with the truth of the sages. With salt, plum, and leaven, may You ever cherish thoughts of the sacrificial tripods of statecraft; amidst the ancestral temple and the百官 (hundred officials), may You always feel the earnestness of seeing the ancient sages in Your soup and on Your walls. Occupying the position of both ruler and teacher to establish the supreme standard, may You seek to harmonize…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
玉燭於萬年
兼述作以成功常固
金甌於億載〔臣〕無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
===
策〔五道〕
第一問
同考試官教諭周　批〔我〕
王忠顯
皇上約已裕民至意原自我
二祖
列聖政要中得來子能敷揚明悉而末復惓惓於保持節儉之義是沾濡王化而抱忠愛之心
者宜錄以為
當宁獻
punctuated:
玉燭於萬年，兼述作以成功，常固金甌於億載。〔臣〕無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策〔五道〕
第一問
同考試官教諭周批：〔我〕
王忠顯
皇上約已裕民至意，原自我二祖、列聖政要中得來。子能敷揚明悉，而末復惓惓於保持節儉之義，是沾濡王化而抱忠愛之心者，宜錄以為當宁獻。
translation_en:
… the Jade Candle of cosmic harmony for ten thousand years; and combining transmission and creation to achieve success, forever secure the Golden Urn of the empire for a hundred million ages. [Your servant] is overcome with the utmost emotion and reverent trepidation in gazing up at Heaven and looking up to Your Sacred Majesty, and respectfully presents this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's information.

Third Session

Policy Essays [Five Questions]

First Question

Wang Zhongxian 王忠顯

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhou 周: [Our] August Emperor's supreme intention to restrain himself and enrich the people originally derives from the essential governance of our Two Ancestors and Successive Sacred Emperors. You are able to expound this clearly and thoroughly, and at the end you again show earnest devotion to the principle of maintaining frugality. This marks one who is steeped in kingly transformation and cherishes a heart of loyalty and affection; it should be recorded and presented to the Throne.

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正梅　批〔節儉我〕
皇上至德而足國裕民之大本此作備悉此義無亦於王政而觀其深者耶
考試官教授朱　批〔說催科之弊剴切錄之〕
帝王之爲生民計者甚悉也有中正之法
焉有法外之仁焉則壤成賦惟正之供法
也法不得以過取則取之亦所以仁之也
損上益下有孚惠心仁也仁則不欲其取
盈所以維是法於不窮者也此古昔之繇
以稱隆也顧其機在上不在下是故循其
===
法制而劑量焉順其時宜而盈縮焉則必
有所以爲之本者而生民之命脉所繇以
厚也且賦稅之說何昉乎自夏以來財賦
分爲三等有總銍秸服粟米之類有漆枲
絺紵鹽鐵之類有玄纁璣組龜貝之類凡
土所出者無不輸也然夏五十而貢未嘗
加於虞商七十而助未嘗加於夏也自周
以來財賦分爲三等有田畝穀米則掌於
地官有園廛布縷則掌於載師有金帛臬
punctuated:
考試官學正梅　批〔節儉，我皇上至德，而足國裕民之大本。此作備悉此義，無亦於王政而觀其深者耶？〕
考試官教授朱　批〔說催科之弊剴切，錄之。〕

帝王之爲生民計者，甚悉也。有中正之法焉，有法外之仁焉。則壤成賦，惟正之供，法也；法不得以過取，則取之亦所以仁之也。損上益下，有孚惠心，仁也；仁則不欲其取盈，所以維是法於不窮者也。此古昔之繇以稱隆也。顧其機在上不在下，是故循其法制而劑量焉，順其時宜而盈縮焉，則必有所以爲之本者，而生民之命脉所繇以厚也。且賦稅之說，何昉乎？自夏以來，財賦分爲三等：有總、銍、秸服、粟米之類，有漆、枲、絺、紵、鹽、鐵之類，有玄纁、璣組、龜貝之類，凡土所出者，無不輸也。然夏五十而貢，未嘗加於虞；商七十而助，未嘗加於夏也。自周以來，財賦分爲三等：有田畝穀米，則掌於地官；有園廛布縷，則掌於載師；有金帛泉…
translation_en:
Examiner Mei, Subprefectural Director of Studies, commented: "Frugality is the supreme virtue of Our Sovereign and the great foundation for enriching the state and bringing abundance to the people. This essay thoroughly grasps this principle; has the writer not observed the deeper meaning of kingly governance?"
Examiner Zhu, Prefectural Director of Studies, commented: "Its discussion of the abuses of tax collection is incisive and to the point. Record it for inclusion."

The plans that emperors and kings make on behalf of the common people are most comprehensive. There are impartial and upright laws, and there is benevolence that goes beyond the laws. Assessing revenues according to the grade of the soil and supplying only the regular dues—this is the law; because the law does not permit excessive exaction, even the act of taking from the people is a way of showing benevolence toward them. Diminishing those above to benefit those below, and possessing a sincere heart of kindness—this is benevolence; because benevolence does not wish to exact the full measure, it serves to sustain these laws without exhaustion. It was by this means that antiquity was celebrated as prosperous. Yet the pivotal mechanism lies with those above, not those below. Therefore, in following legal institutions and adjusting their measure, and in adapting to what is timely and expanding or contracting accordingly, there must be something that serves as the fundamental root, whereby the lifeblood of the people is strengthened.

Moreover, how did the system of land taxes and levies originate? From the Xia dynasty onward, revenues and tribute were divided into three categories: there were such things as whole grain stalks, grain ears, straw, and husked grain; there were such things as lacquer, hemp, fine and coarse kudzu cloth, ramie, salt, and iron; and there were such things as dark and crimson silks, pearl-strung ribbons, tortoise shells, and cowries. Whatever the land produced was without exception delivered as tribute. Yet under the Xia, fifty mu were allotted and the gong (tribute) system was used, which added nothing beyond the practice of Yu [Shun]; under the Shang, seventy mu were allotted and the zhu (mutual-aid) system was used, which added nothing beyond the practice of the Xia. From the Zhou dynasty onward, revenues and tribute were also divided into three categories: there were fields and grain, which were administered by the Minister of Revenue (Diguan); there were gardens, homesteads, and cloth and silk thread, which were administered by the Tithe Collector (Zaishi); and there were gold, silk fabrics, and coin [泉 written as 臬]…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
貨則掌於太府凡民所有者無不稅也然
鄉遂有貢十分取一都鄙用助九分取一
是三代之制雖有不同而什一之法無或
異也當其時富藏億兆之室祿養千八百
之君國有餘財民有餘力康阜之治蔑以
尚矣降及後世魯宣公履畝加稅以濟國
用民由之困固矣而又無裨於國其後至
於作丘甲而用猶不足則宣公啓之也君
子曰宣之初稅畝也其侈心之萌乎漢文
===
帝屢詔免租以甦民困天下之富庶固矣
而又無妨於國太倉之粟陳陳相因其後
至於遵洪業而財日以充則文帝留之也
君子曰文之屢免租也其儉德之符乎漢
以後無論已
國家稽古定制因地宜而等則之歲有定額
家有常數非若先度其數而賦於人者也
隨其田之寬狹取其稅之多寡非若以一
年之科率最多者以爲額也其數具於黃
punctuated: 貨，則掌於太府，凡民所有者無不稅也。然鄉遂有貢，十分取一；都鄙用助，九分取一。是三代之制雖有不同，而什一之法無或異也。當其時，富藏億兆之室，祿養千八百之君，國有餘財，民有餘力，康阜之治蔑以尚矣。降及後世，魯宣公履畝加稅以濟國用，民由之困固矣，而又無裨於國；其後至於作丘甲而用猶不足，則宣公啓之也。君子曰：「宣之初稅畝也，其侈心之萌乎！」漢文帝屢詔免租以甦民困，天下之富庶固矣，而又無妨於國；太倉之粟陳陳相因，其後至於遵洪業而財日以充，則文帝留之也。君子曰：「文之屢免租也，其儉德之符乎！」漢以後無論已。國家稽古定制，因地宜而等則之，歲有定額，家有常數，非若先度其數而賦於人者也；隨其田之寬狹，取其稅之多寡，非若以一年之科率最多者以爲額也。其數具於黃…
translation_en:
…and currency [? 泉貨], which were managed by the Grand Treasurer (Taifu)—whatever the people possessed, none of it went untaxed. Yet in the inner districts and outer districts there was the tribute system, taking one part in ten; in the lesser cities and borderlands they used the mutual-aid system, taking one part in nine. Thus, although the institutions of the Three Dynasties differed, the principle of taxing roughly one-tenth never varied. At that time, wealth was stored in the households of the myriad people, while emoluments sustained the one thousand eight hundred feudal lords. The state had surplus wealth, the people had surplus strength, and the governance of peace and abundance could not be surpassed.

Coming down to later ages, Duke Xuan of Lu surveyed the fields to increase taxes in order to supply state expenditures. That the people were impoverished by this goes without saying, and yet it brought no benefit to the state; when later on they went so far as to institute the military levy by districts (zuo qiujia) and revenues were still insufficient, it was Duke Xuan who had started it. The gentleman says: "When Xuan first taxed the acres, was it not the sprouting of an extravagant heart?" Emperor Wen of Han repeatedly issued edicts remitting land taxes to relieve the people's distress. That the empire became rich and populous goes without saying, and yet it caused no harm to the state; the grain in the Grand Granary was piled layer upon old layer, and when later on his successors followed his grand enterprise and wealth grew more abundant by the day, it was Emperor Wen who had left it to them. The gentleman says: "When Wen repeatedly remitted taxes, was it not the tally of his frugal virtue?" Of the eras after the Han, there is no need to speak.

Our Dynasty examined antiquity to establish its institutions, grading land taxes according to the suitability of the soil. Each year has a fixed quota, and each household has a regular assessment—unlike the practice of first estimating required expenditures and then levying that amount upon the people. According to the breadth or narrowness of their fields, a greater or lesser tax is taken—unlike the practice of taking the year with the highest tax rate and fixing that as the permanent quota. The figures are recorded in the Yellow…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
籍總於司農其徵輸期限責之藩服守令
非若別設両稅使以督之也有味乎陸贄
之言曰其取法也遠其立意也深其斂財
也均其成人也固其裁規也簡其備患也
周此六言者其惟我
國家經賦之制乎夫經制備矣而磽瘠不無
也土地墾矣而逋逃不無也人民聚矣而
歳祲不無也歳時稔矣而意外之費不無
也執一定之法以齊不一之遇其謂斯民
何
===
二祖
列聖一德相承若曰
國之本在民民之本在食重賦而奪之食非
所以厚民本也食奪而民愈貧非所以培
國本也以是蠲租之
詔炳然如日中天有因地方凋敝而免者以助
地利之不及也有因戶口逋逃而免者以
助人力之不及也有因歳時水旱而免者
punctuated: 籍，總於司農；其徵輸期限，責之藩服、守令，非若別設両稅使以督之也。有味乎陸贄之言曰：「其取法也遠，其立意也深，其斂財也均，其成人也固，其裁規也簡，其備患也周。」此六言者，其惟我國家經賦之制乎！夫經制備矣，而磽瘠不無也；土地墾矣，而逋逃不無也；人民聚矣，而歳祲不無也；歳時稔矣，而意外之費不無也。執一定之法，以齊不一之遇，其謂斯民何？二祖、列聖一德相承，若曰：「國之本在民，民之本在食。重賦而奪之食，非所以厚民本也；食奪而民愈貧，非所以培國本也。」以是蠲租之詔，炳然如日中天。有因地方凋敝而免者，以助地利之不及也；有因戶口逋逃而免者，以助人力之不及也；有因歳時水旱而免者，
translation_en:
… Registers, and consolidated under the Minister of Revenue; its deadlines for collection and delivery are the responsibility of provincial authorities, prefects, and magistrates, unlike separately establishing Commissioners of the Two Taxes to supervise them. How meaningful are the words of Lu Zhi 陸贄: "Its adoption of models is far-reaching; its establishment of intent is profound; its collection of wealth is equitable; its support of the people is firm; its formulation of regulations is simple; its precaution against calamities is comprehensive." Do not these six statements describe none other than our Dynasty's system of regular taxation?

Now, even when regular institutions are complete, barren and poor lands are not absent; even when land is brought under cultivation, fugitives and tax evaders are not absent; even when the people are gathered together, annual dearth and calamity are not absent; even when the yearly harvests are abundant, unexpected expenses are not absent. If one clings to a fixed law in order to equalize unequal circumstances, what will become of these people?

The Two Ancestors and Successive Sagely Emperors succeeded one another in a single virtue, as if to say: "The foundation of the state lies in the people, and the foundation of the people lies in food. To impose heavy taxes and deprive them of food is not the way to strengthen the foundation of the people; when food is deprived and the people grow ever poorer, it is not the way to nurture the foundation of the state." Therefore, the imperial edicts remitting taxes shine as brightly as the sun at midday. Some remissions are granted because a region is exhausted and distressed, so as to make up for what the productivity of the land fails to reach; some are granted because households have fled and absconded, so as to make up for what human labor fails to reach; some are granted because of seasonal floods and droughts, …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
以助天時之不及也有因多事之後而免
者以助流離轉徙之不及也或盡免者溥
其施也或不必盡免者酌其宜也或今年
既免而明年復免者重憫之也或今年免
於甲而明年免於乙者變而通之者也今
其
令甲具在大都在洪永之際者十之六七在
累朝者十之三四蓋甫定之民枵然待哺者甚
夥也非大不得已則不忍輒取其民故居
===
六七者若以為常也無事之民熙然樂業
者甚夥也非大不得已則亦不忍不供其
上故居三四者若以為間一行之者也總之
二祖
列聖所以愛養黎元以為培植基本之圖者其
心一而已矣
皇上登極以來
總握元化
默感太穌經制之備如舊也而地則日益以
punctuated:
以助天時之不及也；有因多事之後而免者，以助流離轉徙之不及也。或盡免者，溥其施也；或不必盡免者，酌其宜也；或今年既免而明年復免者，重憫之也；或今年免於甲而明年免於乙者，變而通之者也。今其令甲具在，大都在洪、永之際者十之六七，在累朝者十之三四。蓋甫定之民，枵然待哺者甚夥也，非大不得已，則不忍輒取其民，故居六七者，若以為常也；無事之民，熙然樂業者甚夥也，非大不得已，則亦不忍不供其上，故居三四者，若以為間一行之者也。總之，二祖列聖所以愛養黎元、以為培植基本之圖者，其心一而已矣。

皇上登極以來，總握元化，默感太穌。經制之備如舊也，而地則日益以
translation_en:
…in order to make up for the deficiencies of the seasonal weather; and there were exemptions granted in the aftermath of numerous disturbances, in order to make up for the deficiencies caused by displacement and wandering. Sometimes taxes were exempted in full, to make the bounty universal; sometimes they did not need to be exempted in full, weighing what was appropriate; sometimes they were exempted this year and exempted again the next year, out of deep commiseration for the people; and sometimes they were exempted in region A this year and in region B the next year, adapting flexibly to circumstances. Today these statutory ordinances are all extant: roughly six or seven out of ten date from the Hongwu (1368–1398) and Yongle (1403–1424) eras, while three or four out of ten date from the successive reigns thereafter. For among a newly pacified populace, those who were famished and waiting to be fed were numerous indeed; unless driven by great and unavoidable necessity, the rulers could not bear to readily extract resources from their people, and thus the six or seven out of ten cases were treated almost as a regular norm. Among a populace in times of peace, those who were thriving and content in their livelihoods were numerous indeed; unless driven by great and unavoidable necessity, the people likewise could not bear to fail in supplying their superiors, and thus the three or four out of ten cases were treated as measures carried out only from time to time. In sum, the way in which the Two Ancestors and the Successive Sacred Emperors cherished and nourished the common people as a plan for cultivating and strengthening the fundamental basis of the state stemmed from one and the same mind.

Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, You have held total mastery over primal transformation and silently moved the Great Harmony. The completeness of the regular institutions remains as of old, while the land is increasingly…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
開墾矣民則日益以復業矣時和年豐矣
荒服者獻琛納款邊陲靖矣嘯聚者改心
易慮腹裏安矣則所謂意外之費者何有
也乃
聖念兢兢日惟惠民是務諸所嚴飭吏治者固
畀之撫字以安吾民而有司未悉
上意嚮相率而尚催科之靡文董董塞責以求
日安乎其位嗚呼撫字之與催科勢相倍
蓰者也急催科緩撫字辟之竭澤而漁者
===
然呂氏春秋曰竭澤而漁豈不得魚明年
無魚蓋取稅於民猶取魚於澤也澤以養
魚必常有所養斯常有所生不慮其難以
繼也而數罟日日臨之則一取而盡矣民
以供賦必常有所恤斯常有所供不慮其
難以繼也而峻法日日臨之亦一取而盡
矣
皇上洞見隱微
詔責有司幷免積逋此其約已裕民至意蓋有
punctuated: 開墾矣，民則日益以復業矣，時和年豐矣，荒服者獻琛納款、邊陲靖矣，嘯聚者改心易慮、腹裏安矣。則所謂意外之費者，何有也？乃聖念兢兢，日惟惠民是務。諸所嚴飭吏治者，固畀之撫字以安吾民，而有司未悉上意嚮，相率而尚催科之靡文，董董塞責，以求日安乎其位。嗚呼！撫字之與催科，勢相倍蓰者也。急催科、緩撫字，辟之竭澤而漁者然。《呂氏春秋》曰：「竭澤而漁，豈不得魚？明年無魚。」蓋取稅於民，猶取魚於澤也。澤以養魚，必常有所養，斯常有所生，不慮其難以繼也；而數罟日日臨之，則一取而盡矣。民以供賦，必常有所恤，斯常有所供，不慮其難以繼也；而峻法日日臨之，亦一取而盡矣。皇上洞見隱微，詔責有司，幷免積逋。此其約已裕民至意，蓋有
translation_en:
…been opened for cultivation, the people have increasingly returned to their livelihoods, the seasons are harmonious and the harvests abundant, those in the distant荒服 (wilderness domains) present precious tribute and submit in allegiance so that the frontiers are pacified, and those who had banded together in lawlessness have had a change of heart and mind so that the interior is secure. What, then, could there be of so-called unforeseen expenditures?

Yet His Majesty's thoughts are ever cautious and attentive, daily making kindness to the people his sole concern. All his strict admonitions regarding official administration were surely meant to entrust officials with nurturing care so as to bring peace to our people. However, the local authorities have failed to comprehend His Majesty's intentions; following one another's lead, they prize the empty formalities of pressing for tax collection, barely fulfilling their duties in order to remain comfortably in their posts from day to day. Alas! Nurturing the people and pressing for taxes stand in stark opposition to one another. Being urgent in pressing for taxes while negligent in nurturing care is just like draining a marsh to catch fish. The Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Lü (Lüshi chunqiu) says: "If you drain the marsh to catch fish, how could you fail to get fish? Yet next year there will be no fish." Indeed, extracting taxes from the people is like taking fish from a marsh. A marsh nourishes fish: only when they are constantly nourished will they constantly reproduce, and one need not worry that the supply cannot be sustained; if fine-meshed nets are cast into it day after day, then in a single catch it will be exhausted. The people supply revenue: only when they are constantly shown compassion will they constantly be able to provide, and one need not worry that their contributions cannot be sustained; if harsh laws are brought to bear on them day after day, they too will be exhausted at a single stroke.

His Majesty, perceiving the subtlest hidden realities, issued a decree reprimanding the authorities and at the same time remitting accumulated tax arrears. This supreme intention of restraining himself to enrich the people truly…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
以同符
二祖重光
列聖而陋漢文於不居矣薄海內外罔不舉手
加額而歌
皇仁誠千萬禩一時也即有司者何敢以不肖
之心應之而不思所以仰承
德意乎第經費有常歲出不可省而
詔免積逋歲入不及額其所以濟盈縮以裕公
私之用者果安在哉蓋我
