As for what are called the defensive ramparts of Bingzhou and Jizhou, to the north is Datong; south of Datong they wrap around Ningwu and Yanmen, and turning westward there are Piantou and Laoying. Where Datong borders the Caitiffs, the distance is less than a single day's march at the nearest, and no more than two or three days' march at the farthest; the same is true of Piantou and Laoying. Now, Datong later indeed came to have officials specifically charged with its defense. As for Piantou-Laoying, Ningwu, and Yanmen, these are what are called the Three Passes. The topography of the Three Passes is arranged like overlapping fish scales: to the east and slightly south is Yanmen; a hundred and eighty li farther brings one to Ningwu, and another two hundred li brings one to Piantou Pass. Piantou Pass hangs isolated in the northwest, standing opposite Datong, whereas Yanmen and Ningwu still have Mayi and Shuozhou serving as their outer buffer.

In the past, because Datong could not serve as an effective shield, it was proposed to mark off separate territorial zones and defend them separately: the command of the Three Passes was assigned to the Grand Coordinator of all Shanxi, while the Regional Commander stationed at Piantou was moved to Ningwu, as if to direct operations from a central position and prepare for coordinated support to both east and west. Recently, those who plan frontier affairs have put forward a revised proposal, considering this arrangement inconvenient. They argue that abandoning the outer territory to draw close to the interior [?] amounts to abandonar the outer lands to the enemy; that when the Grand Coordinator is so far removed from the frontier battlefields, matters are hampered by the difficulty of requesting instruction and confirmation; and that when subordinate commanders dwell in isolation, the soldiers cannot rely on relief from the Regional Commander. They wish instead to place both the Grand Coordinator and the Regional Commander at Piantou and Laoying, forming mutual support like horns with Datong and concentrating strength at the vital choke points; and should the Caitiffs invade by way of Mayi and Shuozhou, our forces, catching them by the horns [?]…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
得收弊於寧鴈也噫是則然矣愚以爲制
虜之術在抑其勢審勢者人也專計於人
相宜而圖之則建官責守有可更者有不
必更者夫撫臣折衝之任也非有親冐矢
石列陣行間之事平居申約束明賞罰謹
烽堠隘備儲厲兵秋防駐代俾虜不得隙
入一旦有儆當寇者走軍吏計事轅門而
撫臣亦數馳赴之以便授策故在太原猶
偏老也如必居偏老而後可是將親與抗
===
也平居之所經略宜何事耶假令虜大舉
南侵則彼必數月集我必數月備悉吾之
精銳視險易而愼守之虜必不濟若遊騎
突入禦之一徤將事耳何足以辱撫臣夫
天下之事恒起於時之所趨而亂於數易
偏關之設也在洪武之三十三年而成化
丁亥始創老營堡前乎此者未嘗命一卒
守也亦未有大患乃今師武臣力開府運
籌而猶惧有丁卯之患焉即多多奚益哉
punctuated: 得收弊於寧、鴈也。噫！是則然矣，愚以爲制虜之術，在抑其勢，審勢者人也。專計於人，相宜而圖之，則建官責守，有可更者，有不必更者。夫撫臣，折衝之任也，非有親冐矢石、列陣行間之事。平居申約束，明賞罰，謹烽堠，隘備儲，厲兵，秋防駐代，俾虜不得隙入。一旦有儆，當寇者走軍吏計事轅門，而撫臣亦數馳赴之，以便授策，故在太原猶偏、老也。如必居偏、老而後可，是將親與抗也，平居之所經略，宜何事耶？假令虜大舉南侵，則彼必數月集，我必數月備，悉吾之精銳，視險易而愼守之，虜必不濟。若遊騎突入，禦之一徤將事耳，何足以辱撫臣？夫天下之事，恒起於時之所趨，而亂於數易。偏關之設也，在洪武之三十三年，而成化丁亥始創老營堡，前乎此者，未嘗命一卒守也，亦未有大患。乃今師武臣力，開府運籌，而猶惧有丁卯之患焉，即多多奚益哉？
translation_en: … be able to take advantage of their exhaustion at Ningwu 寧武 and Yanmen 鴈門. Alas, that much is true! Yet in my humble opinion, the art of controlling the caitiffs lies in curbing their momentum, and those who assess momentum are men. If one focuses on the men and plans according to what is appropriate, then in establishing offices and assigning defensive responsibilities, there are things that may be changed and things that need not be changed. Now, the Grand Coordinator (撫臣) bears the responsibility of repelling aggression through strategy; it is not his business to personally brave arrows and stones or array battle lines in the ranks. In ordinary times, he reiterates regulations, clarifies rewards and punishments, keeps careful watch over signal beacons, stocks provisions at the passes, sharpens the troops, and during the autumn defense stations himself at Dai 代, ensuring that the caitiffs find no opening to enter. Once an alarm arises, those facing the raiders send military officers to deliberate at his headquarters gate, and the Grand Coordinator also rides forth repeatedly to confer strategies as convenient. Thus, being at Taiyuan 太原 is the same as being at Piantou 偏頭 and Laoying 老營. If it were only acceptable for him to reside at Piantou and Laoying, then he would be personally confronting the enemy—what then would be the purpose of all his strategic planning in ordinary times? Suppose the caitiffs launch a massive invasion southward: they must take several months to assemble, and we will certainly have several months to prepare. If we mobilize all our elite forces, assess the difficult and easy terrain, and guard it prudently, the caitiffs will surely not succeed. As for roving cavalry making a sudden incursion, repelling them is merely the task of a single stalwart commander—how could it be worth troubling the Grand Coordinator? Indeed, the affairs of the world ever arise in response to the trends of the times, and fall into disorder through frequent changes. The establishment of Piantou Pass (偏關) took place in the thirty-third year of Hongwu 洪武 [sic, 1400], and only in the dinghai 丁亥 year of Chenghua 成化 (1467) was Laoying Fort (老營堡) first founded. Prior to this, not a single soldier had ever been ordered to garrison it, yet neither was there any great disaster. Now, however, with martial officers exerting their strength and a grand headquarters devising strategies, we still fear a disaster like that of the dingmao 丁卯 year (1567)—so even if we add more and more officials, what benefit would there be?

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
虜之畏我以有實也非畏名也今之所以
稱藩而市馬者利金繒也弟必設撫臣以
爲名彼於畏何有議者曰設撫臣於偏老
視延寧甘肅之例也夫事苟利固無庸例
然而以陝例之者誤也延寧甘固實稱四
鎮置三撫臣而固原一鎮以總督當之總
督趨花馬池則以撫臣之在長安者移領
鎮焉而固原而西至於蘭靖西南至於洮
岷蓋方數千里番虜雜吞烽燧時警然皆
===
撫臣之在長安者兼制之陝西之撫內者
何嘗不兼邊也山西幅幀不滿千里民又
甚瘠而三關固太原一郡地耳必以一郡
建兩撫臣無論供億煩苛無益勝負之數
而又以滋病郎內有分地則外之召兵於
內者難外有分地則內之轉饟於外者緩
牽制沮格之患不可不虞也故曰建官惟
其人不必備若乃總兵之移則有可言者
總兵雖信大將與文吏異古者中軍在御
punctuated: 虜之畏我，以有實也，非畏名也。今之所以稱藩而市馬者，利金繒也；弟必設撫臣以爲名，彼於畏何有？議者曰：「設撫臣於偏、老，視延、寧、甘肅之例也。」夫事苟利，固無庸例；然而以陝例之者，誤也。延、寧、甘、固實稱四鎮，置三撫臣，而固原一鎮以總督當之。總督趨花馬池，則以撫臣之在長安者移領鎮焉。而固原而西至於蘭、靖，西南至於洮、岷，蓋方數千里，番虜雜吞，烽燧時警，然皆撫臣之在長安者兼制之。陝西之撫內者，何嘗不兼邊也？山西幅幀不滿千里，民又甚瘠，而三關固太原一郡地耳。必以一郡建兩撫臣，無論供億煩苛，無益勝負之數，而又以滋病。郎內有分地，則外之召兵於內者難；外有分地，則內之轉饟於外者緩。牽制沮格之患，不可不虞也。故曰：「建官惟其人，不必備。」若乃總兵之移，則有可言者。總兵雖信大將，與文吏異。古者中軍在御，
translation_en: The northern caitiffs fear us because we possess actual strength, not because they fear mere titles. The reason they now declare themselves vassals and trade horses with us is that they covet our gold and silks; if we merely insist on establishing a Grand Coordinator (fuchen 撫臣) for the sake of the title, what fear will that inspire in them? Those who deliberate on the matter say: "Establishing a Grand Coordinator at Pianguan and Laoying follows the precedent of Yansui, Ningxia, and Gansu." Now, if a measure is truly beneficial, there is certainly no need to rely on precedent; yet to use Shaanxi as a precedent here is a mistake. Yansui, Ningxia, Gansu, and Guyuan are in fact known as the Four Defense Commands (sizhen 四鎮). Three Grand Coordinators are appointed there, while the single defense command of Guyuan is handled by the Supreme Commander (zongdu 總督). When the Supreme Commander advances to Huamachi, the Grand Coordinator stationed in Chang'an moves to take charge of the defense command at Guyuan. And from Guyuan westward to Lanzhou and Jinglu, and southwestward to Taozhou and Minzhou, across an expanse of several thousand square li where Tibetan and Mongol tribes are mingled together [?] and beacon fires frequently sound the alarm, all of it is jointly controlled by the Grand Coordinator stationed in Chang'an. When has the official who coordinates the interior of Shaanxi ever failed to concurrently oversee the frontier? Shanxi's territory does not even reach a thousand li across, its people are furthermore extremely impoverished, and the Three Passes (sanguan 三關) are in fact merely the territory of the single prefecture of Taiyuan. To insist on establishing two Grand Coordinators within a single prefecture—not to mention that the provisioning and exactions would be burdensome and harsh, contributing nothing to the outcome of victory or defeat—would moreover only multiply our ailments. If [reading 即 for 郎] the interior has its separately demarcated jurisdiction, it becomes difficult for the exterior to summon troops from the interior; if the exterior has its separately demarcated jurisdiction, the interior becomes slow to transport military supplies to the exterior. One cannot fail to guard against the dangers of mutual hindrance and obstruction. Therefore it is said: "In establishing offices, seek only the right men; one need not fill every post." As for the relocation of the Regional Commander (zongbing 總兵), however, there is something to be said. Although the Regional Commander is indeed a great general, his role differs from that of civil officials. In antiquity, the commander of the central army rode in his chariot…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
援枹而鼓朱殷輪而不惰令猥以爲持衡
握銓之臣虞偏關多故或失之而以移之
寧武無謂也夫重移鎮者蓋以寧武之衝
燕水雕窩陽方盤道相望廣衍紆漫騎得
成列萬一虜擣我虛直入將狠顧失據焉
噫獨不虞偏關之可達汾來乎馬邑朔州
大同地也尚寄一帶之衛於寧鴈而虜志
俘掠則大同其饜足處耳饜足則不南望
即南望吾且有備安得爲虛耶偏關逼近
===
虜巢即已款貢而叛升叛人歲時窺伺又
夷人叩關者月無虛日所不能高枕也故
大將不可以深居深居則偏裨觀效士氣
日懈夫寧武之赴偏關猶偏關之還而自
救其地里獨鴈門稍遠也誠令總兵移偏
關仍協之以參將而寧武則撤馬站遊擊
居之偏頭加一大將與副將俱是關士倍
也人情偷於習鼓於新旌幟一耀其耳目
號令一作其頹靡則重關之固壯於戒嚴
punctuated: 援枹而鼓，朱殷輪而不惰。令猥以爲持衡握銓之臣，虞偏關多故，或失之，而以移之寧武，無謂也。夫重移鎮者，蓋以寧武之衝，燕水、雕窩、陽方、盤道相望，廣衍紆漫，騎得成列；萬一虜擣我虛直入，將狠顧失據焉。噫！獨不虞偏關之可達汾來乎？馬邑、朔州，大同地也，尚寄一帶之衛於寧、鴈；而虜志俘掠，則大同其饜足處耳。饜足則不南望；即南望，吾且有備，安得爲虛耶？偏關逼近虜巢，即已款貢，而叛升、叛人歲時窺伺，又夷人叩關者月無虛日，所不能高枕也。故大將不可以深居，深居則偏裨觀效，士氣日懈。夫寧武之赴偏關，猶偏關之還而自救，其地里獨鴈門稍遠也。誠令總兵移偏關，仍協之以參將，而寧武則撤馬站遊擊居之。偏頭加一大將，與副將俱，是關士倍也。人情偷於習，鼓於新。旌幟一耀其耳目，號令一作其頹靡，則重關之固，壯於戒嚴；
translation_en: …grasped the drumstick and beat the drum; even when dark-red blood stained the chariot wheels, they did not slacken. Now to rashly treat him as an official who merely holds the scales and grasps the balances, and out of fear that Pianguan is full of trouble and might be lost, to move him to Ningwu—this is senseless! Those who attach importance to moving the garrison command do so because at the strategic approaches of Ningwu—where Yanshui, Diaowo, Yangfang, and Pandao face one another—the terrain is broad, flat, and sprawling, allowing cavalry to form ranks; if by chance the caitiffs strike a weak spot and charge straight in, our generals would look back in panic and lose their footing. Alas! Do they alone not worry that from Pianguan the enemy can reach the Fen River and Lishi [? 汾來]? Mayi and Shuozhou are territory of Datong, yet they still entrust the defense of that belt of land to Ningwu and Yanmen; whereas if the caitiffs' ambition is plunder and captives, Datong is the place where they can glut themselves. Once glutted, they will not look south; and even if they look south, we are moreover prepared—how could it be considered a weak spot? Pianguan presses close to the caitiffs' lair. Even though they have already submitted to tribute relations, rebel leaders [? 叛升] and defectors spy on us throughout the year, and there is not a day in the month without barbarians knocking at the pass; it is a place where one cannot sleep on a high pillow in peace. Therefore, the Commander-in-Chief must not dwell deep in the interior; if he dwells deep within, the subordinate commanders will follow his example, and the morale of the troops will slacken day by day. Now, going from Ningwu to the aid of Pianguan is no different in distance from returning from Pianguan to rescue Ningwu itself; in terms of mileage, only Yanmen is somewhat farther. If we truly order the Regional Commander to move to Pianguan, assisted as before by an Assistant Regional Commander, and at Ningwu transfer the Mobile Corps Commander of Mazhan to reside there, then Piantou (Pianguan) will gain a supreme commander together with the Vice Regional Commander, which will double the spirit of the troops at the pass. Human nature grows lax with familiarity and is roused by what is new. Once the banners and standards dazzle their eyes and ears, and the commands and orders rouse them from their decadence, the solidity of the double passes will be strengthened by heightened alert. …

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
今之援寧武亦昔之援偏老矣夫何間也
若鴈門故有叅備且近撫臣當必無害顧
乃謂偏老遠不可居何歟總兵之設也始
於宣德既罷復於弘治當是時皆偏老居
也寧武設於成化丙戌置守備耳而幸無
事弘治間置守禦千戶所耳而亦無事總
兵居寧武之議果何見耶要之撫臣職在
謀筭者也總兵職在征戰者也二者甚可
相能而不必茲處故因勢以命職因職以
===
任人因人以度勢建官之要罔踰於此矣
雖然三關之地皆稱要也三關之守皆宜
嚴也故有禦夷之遠略則何地而非守有
體國之實心則何守而不固區區一隅一
隙之補所見者淺也而責守之事且或有
未盡者邊墻綿亘數百里戍卒僅四五萬
星羅棋布殊多中空彼聚而攻我驍騎衝
軼直如決大河潰蟻壤此畫地而守之難
故不如無與爭鋒各令收聚入保堅壁以
punctuated:
今之援寧武，亦昔之援偏、老矣，夫何間也？若鴈門，故有叅、備，且近撫臣，當必無害。顧乃謂偏、老遠不可居，何歟？總兵之設也，始於宣德，既罷，復於弘治，當是時皆偏、老居也。寧武設於成化丙戌，置守備耳，而幸無事；弘治間，置守禦千戶所耳，而亦無事。總兵居寧武之議，果何見耶？要之，撫臣職在謀筭者也，總兵職在征戰者也，二者甚可相能而不必茲處。故因勢以命職，因職以任人，因人以度勢，建官之要，罔踰於此矣。
雖然，三關之地皆稱要也，三關之守皆宜嚴也。故有禦夷之遠略，則何地而非守？有體國之實心，則何守而不固？區區一隅一隙之補，所見者淺也，而責守之事，且或有未盡者。邊墻綿亘數百里，戍卒僅四五萬，星羅棋布，殊多中空。彼聚而攻我，驍騎衝軼，直如決大河、潰蟻壤，此畫地而守之難。故不如無與爭鋒，各令收聚入保，堅壁以
translation_en:
Reinforcing Ningwu today is just like reinforcing Piantou and Laoying in the past—what difference is there? As for Yanmen, it originally has an Assistant Regional Commander and a Commandant, and moreover it is close to the Grand Coordinator, so it should certainly be safe from harm. Yet why is it said that Piantou and Laoying are too distant to reside in? The establishment of the Regional Commander began in the Xuande era (1426–1435); after being abolished, it was restored in the Hongzhi era (1488–1505). At those times, they always resided at Piantou and Laoying. Ningwu was established in the bingxu year of the Chenghua era (1466); only a Commandant was placed there, and fortunately there were no incidents. During the Hongzhi era, only an Independent Chiliarchy was placed there, and again there were no incidents. On what view, then, was the proposal for the Regional Commander to reside at Ningwu really based? In sum, the duty of the Grand Coordinator lies in strategic planning, while the duty of the Regional Commander lies in combat and warfare. The two can work together very well without needing to reside in the same place. Therefore, assigning offices according to the strategic situation, appointing men according to the offices, and assessing the strategic situation according to the men—the essentials of establishing official posts do not go beyond this.

Even so, the territories of all Three Passes are considered vital, and the defenses of all Three Passes ought to be strict. Thus, if one has a far-reaching strategy for defending against the barbarians, what place is not to be defended? If one has a genuine heart dedicated to the state, what defense will not be solid? Merely patching up a single corner or a single gap reflects a shallow view, and the business of fulfilling defensive responsibilities may still leave something undone. The frontier wall stretches continuously for several hundred li, while the garrison soldiers number only forty or fifty thousand; scattered like stars and arrayed like pieces on a chessboard, they leave a great many empty spaces in between. When the enemy masses to attack us, their valiant cavalry charge and break through just like breaching a great river or collapsing an anthill—this is the difficulty of dividing up the ground to defend it. Therefore, it is better not to contend with their sharp edge, but instead to order everyone to gather and withdraw into the forts, strengthening the ramparts to…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
待彼縱掠無所得又懼深入必自遁矣是
求地利於人也戎伍隸尺籍者虛耗以半
而日餉數錢多浚剝於渠帥老弱無營者
應募勇悍多技者畏羈此無兵而守之難
故莫如嚴覈軍實養一夫必得一夫之力
而又優幕府之用俾不取盈於下則備在
我不在虜矣是求兵於將也往吾與虜防
也邊氓懼爲俘戮故死不敢即夷人自爲
守也今胡越一家而愚夫無遠略或爭趨
===
之以辟賦䖏邊後將何支焉盍亦揃循百
姓輕其徭稅俾居者固而去者思乎虜與
吾市也馬皆異產不與中土習分發郡縣
輙踣死而償之民也夫民無所得馬而樂
於償固以免兵弭患彼亦與有利焉盍亦
以此補營馬之虛而仍輸郡邑之值將不
軍知惠而市無損乎歲選內地丁壯脩守
邊隙顧募犒來之費全省以數萬計而丁
壯至邊顧救死扶傷不暇安所裨於事哉
punctuated: 待，彼縱掠無所得，又懼深入，必自遁矣，是求地利於人也。戎伍隸尺籍者虛耗以半，而日餉數錢多浚剝於渠帥，老弱無營者應募，勇悍多技者畏羈，此無兵而守之難。故莫如嚴覈軍實，養一夫必得一夫之力，而又優幕府之用，俾不取盈於下，則備在我不在虜矣，是求兵於將也。往吾與虜防也，邊氓懼爲俘戮，故死不敢即夷，人自爲守也。今胡越一家，而愚夫無遠略，或爭趨之以辟賦，䖏邊後將何支焉？盍亦揃循百姓，輕其徭稅，俾居者固而去者思乎？虜與吾市也，馬皆異產，不與中土習，分發郡縣輙踣死，而償之民也。夫民無所得馬而樂於償，固以免兵弭患，彼亦與有利焉。盍亦以此補營馬之虛，而仍輸郡邑之值，將不軍知惠而市無損乎？歲選內地丁壯脩守邊隙，顧募犒來之費，全省以數萬計，而丁壯至邊，顧救死扶傷不暇，安所裨於事哉？
translation_en: …wait for them. When they plunder and gain nothing, and moreover fear penetrating too deeply, they will surely flee on their own. This is seeking geographical advantage through men. As for those in the military ranks registered on the rosters, half are lost to empty depletion, while their daily rations of a few coins are mostly extorted by their commanders. The old and weak who have no livelihood answer the call for recruits, whereas the brave, fierce, and skilled fear being tied down. This is the difficulty of defending when there are no true soldiers. Therefore, nothing is better than strictly verifying the actual strength of the army, so that in supporting one man we are certain to obtain the strength of one man, and furthermore generously providing for the expenses of the command headquarters so that they do not extract a surplus from their subordinates. Then preparedness will rest with us and not with the caitiffs; this is seeking soldiers through the generals. In the past, when we guarded against the caitiffs, the frontier people feared being captured or slaughtered, so to the death they dared not approach the barbarians, and each person defended himself. Now, Hu and Yue are one family, and foolish men lack farsighted plans; some vie to flock to them in order to evade taxes. In managing the frontier, how shall we sustain it later on? Why not also comfort and soothe the common people [? 揃循 for 撫循] and lighten their corvée labor and taxes, so that those who remain are secure and those who have left long to return? When the caitiffs trade with us, their horses are all of foreign breed, unaccustomed to the central lands; when distributed to the prefectures and counties, they immediately collapse and die, and the common people must make restitution for them. Now, the people get no use of the horses and yet are glad to pay restitution, surely because by avoiding warfare and averting disaster, they too share in the benefit. Why not also use these horses to fill the vacancies among the camp horses, while still forwarding the price from the prefectures and counties? Would not the troops then know the bounty while the horse markets suffer no loss? Every year, able-bodied men from the interior are selected to repair and defend the gaps along the frontier. The expenses of hiring them and rewarding their arrival amount to tens of thousands for the whole province; yet when the able-bodied men reach the frontier, they scarcely have time to save themselves from death and tend to their injuries—how does this benefit the affair at all?

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
盡亦徵募金於官委輸邊郡召士著而簡
練之止則爲民動則成旅而內地丁壯番
休者則求以保障不調焉此其利固不獨
貽三關磐石之固也凡此數者非益於兵
與民之外而皆因其舊以重其守所謂先
爲不可勝以待敵之可勝守亦戰也抑又
聞之昔者李牧之備代鴈門也趙疆起之
恣所欲行牧日椎牛饗士具選車得三百
乘百金之士五萬人彀者十萬先以數千
委匈奴竟滅襜襤破東胡單于奔走不敢
近塞魏尚一雲中守耳亦日饗賓客軍吏
虜會一入尚率車騎擊之所殺傷甚衆而
上功首虜差六級竟坐罰作今元戎宿將
即負巨代能聽令出入軍市租不問乎能
聽令以數千人委虜不計乎噫其不爲魏
尚無幾矣如此其如建官責守之意何哉
此固明問之所未及也而愚敢妄以爲言
以備菲葑之采
punctuated: 盡亦徵募金於官，委輸邊郡，召士著而簡練之，止則爲民，動則成旅，而內地丁壯番休者，則求以保障不調焉？此其利固不獨貽三關磐石之固也。凡此數者，非益於兵與民之外，而皆因其舊以重其守，所謂先爲不可勝以待敵之可勝，守亦戰也。抑又聞之，昔者李牧之備代、鴈門也，趙疆起之，恣所欲行。牧日椎牛饗士，具選車得三百乘，百金之士五萬人，彀者十萬，先以數千委匈奴，竟滅襜襤，破東胡，單于奔走，不敢近塞。魏尚一雲中守耳，亦日饗賓客軍吏。虜會一入，尚率車騎擊之，所殺傷甚衆，而上功首虜差六級，竟坐罰作。今元戎宿將，即負巨代，能聽令出入軍市租不問乎？能聽令以數千人委虜不計乎？噫！其不爲魏尚無幾矣。如此，其如建官責守之意何哉？此固明問之所未及也，而愚敢妄以爲言，以備菲葑之采。
translation_en:
Why not also levy the hiring funds through the officials and transport them to the frontier commanderies, recruiting the local inhabitants [?] and selecting and drilling them, so that at rest they are civilians and in action they form an army, while the able-bodied men from the interior who serve in rotation are sought only to provide local defense without being mobilized? The benefit of this would surely not merely bequeath a rock-solid security to the Three Passes. All of these several measures do not add anything outside of the existing soldiers and civilians, but rather build upon what is already there in order to strengthen defense; this is what is meant by first making oneself invincible in order to await the enemy's vulnerability—defense is also offense.

Furthermore, I have heard that in the past, when Li Mu 李牧 guarded Dai 代 and Yanmen 鴈門, Zhao raised him from the borderlands [?] and allowed him to act entirely as he wished. Every day Li Mu slaughtered cattle to feast his troops; he prepared and selected three hundred war chariots, fifty thousand warriors worth a hundred pieces of gold, and a hundred thousand archers. At first he abandoned a few thousand men to the Xiongnu, yet in the end he annihilated the Chanlan 襜襤, routed the Donghu 東胡, and sent the Chanyu fleeing, never daring to approach the frontier. Wei Shang 魏尚 was merely a Grand Administrator of Yunzhong 雲中, and he too feasted his guests and military officers every day. When the caitiffs once invaded [?], Shang led his chariots and cavalry to attack them, killing and wounding a great many; yet when he reported his merits, the tally of heads and captives was off by six, and in the end he was convicted and sentenced to penal labor. Today, even if our supreme commanders and veteran generals bear great responsibilities across the era [?], would the court allow them to collect and spend the military market taxes without inquiry? Would it allow them to abandon several thousand men to the caitiffs without calling them to account? Alas! Those who do not end up like Wei Shang are few indeed. If it is like this, what becomes of the original intent of establishing offices and demanding accountability in defense? This is admittedly a matter that the wise question did not touch upon, yet in my foolishness I dare to speak of it rashly, to offer it as humble greens and turnips for your selection.

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
萬曆丙子山西鄉試竣役業
以諸偕計士所爲文籍之矣
在廷蒿目而就業焉固渾渾
灝灝之遺文如在也乃羣偕
計士振袂而中告之曰嗟而
士也而亦知
===
聖澤之所以裨益爾多士者乎諸
所爲振風教而養惇裕者且
勿論已先是晉地數苦虜患
其防守在秋虜闌入烽火晝
夜稱警晉以此不獨完何亶
縵纓組練之夫暨彼齊民者
至兢兢也即如而文士挾筴
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

萬曆丙子，山西鄉試竣役，業以諸偕計士所爲文籍之矣。在廷蒿目而就業焉，固渾渾灝灝之遺文如在也。乃羣偕計士，振袂而中告之曰：「嗟，而士也，而亦知聖澤之所以裨益爾多士者乎？諸所爲振風教而養惇裕者，且勿論已。先是，晉地數苦虜患，其防守在秋，虜闌入，烽火晝夜稱警，晉以此不獨完。何亶縵纓組練之夫暨彼齊民者至兢兢也？即如而文士，挾筴
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the bingzi year of the Wanli reign (1576), the work of the Shanxi Provincial Examination was completed, and the essays written by the scholars recommended to accompany the tribute accounts had already been compiled into the register. I, Zaiting, read through and completed my review of their work with great earnestness; truly, the vast and boundless legacy of ancient literature seemed still alive in them. Thereupon I gathered the recommended scholars, shook my sleeves, and addressed them directly, saying:

"Ah, you scholars! Do you also realize how the sacred beneficence of the throne has benefited you, the multitude of scholars? Setting aside for now all that has been done to rouse moral customs and education and to cultivate sincere generosity: previously, the land of Jin (Shanxi) repeatedly suffered from the depredations of the northern caitiffs. Because the frontier defense falls in autumn, when the caitiffs broke in across the border, beacon fires signaled alarms day and night, and because of this Jin could not remain intact on its own. How could it be only the warriors in plain helmet-cords and braided armor, along with the common people, who were reduced to trembling apprehension? Even literary scholars such as yourselves, clasping your writing tablets…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
而讀聽鉦鼓而與之訌擔簦
而游荷戈鋋而與之俱籍第
令有主者而多士之心固且
夕嗜義而不能下咽也六七
年間虜慓然款貢乃今愈益
服習
聖化邊鄙肅清而士也畢得媮快
===
而譚詩書耽弦歌晉故要害
不圖與與然文物之至於斯
也凡是者孰非
主上聖神文武所變化哉士生其
時而又得占一經以售於有
司信厚幸矣是故〔作 延〕披籍
而誦多士所謂文闈經術津
punctuated: 而讀，聽鉦鼓而與之訌，擔簦而游，荷戈鋋而與之俱。籍第令有主者，而多士之心，固且夕嗜義而不能下咽也。六七年間，虜慓然款貢，乃今愈益服習聖化，邊鄙肅清，而士也畢得媮快而譚《詩》《書》，耽弦歌。晉故要害，不圖與與然文物之至於斯也！凡是者，孰非主上聖神文武所變化哉？士生其時，而又得占一經以售於有司，信厚幸矣。是故〔作 延〕披籍而誦多士所謂文闈經術，津
translation_en: …and reading, hearing the gongs and drums and being thrown into confusion alongside them; traveling with umbrellas on their shoulders, and marching along with those carrying halberds and spears. Even supposing there were examiners to preside over them, the hearts of the many scholars would still, even when savoring righteousness at nightfall, be unable to swallow a bite. Within six or seven years, the northern nomads eagerly submitted and offered tribute [referring to the 1571 peace settlement with Altan Khan], and now they have grown ever more submissive and accustomed to His Majesty's sacred transformation. The frontier regions are peaceful and clear, and the scholars are all able to delight in discussing the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu) and to immerse themselves in string music and song. Jin [Shanxi] was formerly a strategic frontier stronghold—who would have expected its flourishing cultural refinement to reach such heights as this! In all these things, what is not the result of transformation wrought by the sacred, divine, civil, and martial virtues of Our Sovereign on High? For scholars to be born in such an age, and furthermore to be able to specialize in one of the Classics so as to present their talents to the authorities, is truly great good fortune. Therefore, as I, [Zuo] Yan, open the scripts and recite what the many scholars have composed of classical learning in the examination compound, how…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
津如也持論侃侃如也標情
宣德引經飾吏鏗鏗如也鑿
鑿如也連類而詰射之洸洸
洋洋如也所謂媮快而譚詩
書耽弦歌者效居然可睹已
楚有丈人之承蜩猶掇之也
仲尼既聞其道顧謂弟子曰
===
用志不分乃凝於神吾所習
者專也而士也洵美且都脫
令旁不可懷馴如鄉時而且
聽鉦鼓而且荷戈鋋則用志
分而神不凝詎能媮快然收
專一之效乃臻是乎而士也
怳然思所以報稱之矣雖然
punctuated: 津如也，持論侃侃如也，標情宣德、引經飾吏鏗鏗如也、鑿鑿如也，連類而詰射之洸洸洋洋如也。所謂媮快而譚《詩》《書》、耽弦歌者，效居然可睹已。楚有丈人之承蜩，猶掇之也。仲尼既聞其道，顧謂弟子曰：「用志不分，乃凝於神。」吾所習者專也，而士也洵美且都。脫令旁不可懷馴如鄉時，而且聽鉦鼓，而且荷戈鋋，則用志分而神不凝，詎能媮快然收專一之效乃臻是乎？而士也怳然思所以報稱之矣。雖然，
translation_en: …overflowing with interest; when they maintain their discourses, they are forthright and bold; when they express sentiments and proclaim virtue, or cite the Classics to adorn administrative practice, they are resonant and verifiable; and when they draw analogies and probe into policy questions, they are vigorous and expansive. The efficacy of what I called happily discussing the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu) and delighting in stringed instruments and song can indeed be clearly seen here! In Chu there was an old man who caught cicadas on a sticky pole as easily as picking them up with his fingers. After Zhongni [Confucius] heard his Way, he turned and said to his disciples: "When the application of the will is undivided, it concentrates in the spirit." What we practice is undivided concentration, and these scholars are truly admirable and refined. Suppose that the surrounding borders could not be pacified and tamed as in former times, and they had at once to listen to gongs and drums and at once to shoulder spears and lances—then the application of their will would be divided and their spirit unfocused; how could they happily reap the effects of undivided concentration so as to reach this level? Thus the scholars must thoughtfully consider how to repay and match this grace. Even so,…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
士自束髮受書三歲而一上
於有司幸而效也奚忍懸空
文以自見而有司爲
社稷得人則亦曰千里一士猶
然比肩而立心故切切焉以
才難爲懼而畢收之斯二者
寧無當於求乎抑聞之困士
===
之臣多智遯國之臣多迂士
困於昔而遯於今固智與迂
之所繇以辨也〔在廷〕顧多士
之爲智也毋芬華而離其質
毋竊情而小其器毋狃治安
而不周於慮毋汩汩於利害
失得而回謬其途域其心競
punctuated: 士自束髮受書，三歲而一上於有司，幸而效也，奚忍懸空文以自見？而有司爲社稷得人，則亦曰：「千里一士，猶然比肩而立。」心故切切焉以才難爲懼而畢收之。斯二者，寧無當於求乎？抑聞之：困士之臣多智，遯國之臣多迂。士困於昔而遯於今，固智與迂之所繇以辨也。〔在廷〕顧多士之爲智也，毋芬華而離其質，毋竊情而小其器，毋狃治安而不周於慮，毋汩汩於利害失得而回謬其途、域其心，競…
translation_en: … From the time a scholar binds his hair and receives instruction in books, once every three years he presents himself to the authorities; when he is fortunate enough to prove successful, how could he bear to display mere empty words to show himself off? And as for the authorities who obtain men of talent for the altars of soil and grain, they too say: "Even if one finds only a single scholar in a thousand miles, it is still as though they stand shoulder to shoulder." Thus in their hearts they are earnestly fearful that talent is hard to find, and they gather them all in. Could these two attitudes fail to answer to what is sought? Yet I have heard it said: the ministers of a state that hard-presses its scholars are mostly wise, whereas the ministers of a state that indulges in ease [?] are mostly impractical. That scholars were hard-pressed in the past and are at ease in the present is surely whereby wisdom and impracticality are distinguished. I [Zaiting] hope that the many scholars will act with wisdom: do not pursue florid ornament and depart from substance; do not indulge private feelings and belittle your capacity; do not grow accustomed to peace and order and fail to be comprehensive in your deliberations; do not be submerged in calculations of advantage and harm, loss and gain, thereby perverting your path and confining your mind; but strive…

title: 萬曆四年山西鄉試錄
text:
虓焉直若聽鉦鼓荷戈鋋而
抉策擔簦之不置也則
國家之事可幾而理矣無若寶
宵練者然古昔有寶宵練之
劍者藏以千金之匣劍化而
去猶然寶其匣焉嗟乎寶匣而
不寶劍虛文而不適於用者
===
也迂亦甚矣而士也且新發
於硎其尚爲鏌鋣爲干將以
斬不虛大冶者意也即所以
圖報稱者其在斯乎其在斯
乎
四川眉州儒學學正梅〔在廷〕
謹序
punctuated:
虓焉直若聽鉦鼓、荷戈鋋，而抉策擔簦之不置也，則國家之事可幾而理矣。無若寶宵練者然。古昔有寶宵練之劍者，藏以千金之匣，劍化而去，猶然寶其匣焉。嗟乎！寶匣而不寶劍，虛文而不適於用者也，迂亦甚矣！而士也，且新發於硎，其尚爲鏌鋣、爲干將，以斬不虛大冶者意也。即所以圖報稱者，其在斯乎！其在斯乎！
四川眉州儒學學正梅〔在廷〕謹序。
translation_en:
…and fiercely, just as if listening to gongs and drums, shouldering halberds and spears, and never ceasing to grasp their whips and carry their parasols; then the affairs of the state may nearly be put in order. Do not be like the one who treasured the Xiaolian sword. In antiquity, there was someone who treasured the Xiaolian sword and stored it in a scabbard worth a thousand pieces of gold; when the sword transformed and vanished, he still treasured its scabbard just the same. Alas! To treasure the scabbard and not the sword is to value empty form that is unsuited for practical use—what extreme pedantry! Now our scholars are like blades newly come from the whetstone; may they strive to be Moye and Ganjiang swords, so as to severed [obstacles? / resolve?] not to disappoint the intentions of the Great Smelter. Could not the very means by which they seek to repay and match [Imperial grace] lie right in this? Could it not lie right in this?

Respectfully prefaced by Mei Zaiting, Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Meizhou in Sichuan.
